jobs.description:
DIRECTOR OF FINANCE

New York City · On-site

THE VOICE AI WORKFORCE FOR HEALTHCARE

Healthcare runs on phone calls and loses $450B a year to the administration around them. Patients wait on hold, staff spend hours calling insurers, and revenue leaks at every handoff.

At Prosper, we're building the AI workforce that runs healthcare operations end to end. Our voice AI agents answer patient calls, schedule appointments directly in the EHR, verify insurance benefits, automate billing, and get payors on the phone when humans would otherwise wait on hold. We've grown revenue 5x in the last year, partnered with 100+ healthcare organizations covering more than 150,000 providers, and raised $35M, including a $30M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.

THE ROLE

We're hiring a Director of Finance, our first finance hire, to own Prosper's numbers end to end: planning, metrics, reporting, and the finance operations underneath them.

Think of it as building a function rather than filling a seat. You'll own both sides of finance: the strategic side (planning, metrics, reporting) and the operational side (accounting, monthly close, payroll and taxes), run with an outsourced partner you manage.

Prosper is at an inflection point. Revenue is up 5x in the last year, and finance has to scale with it. It's early enough that the finance playbook is yours to write, and consequential enough that writing it well changes the trajectory of the company.

If you've spent years building models and advising on other companies' numbers, this is the version where you own the plan, run the function, and see the business move.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own strategic finance

 - Build the operating model from a blank page: annual plan, budget, monthly forecast, and the drivers behind each of them

 - Own the metrics the company runs on: ARR bridge (new logo, expansion, contraction, churn), contracted vs. live ARR, time to go-live, gross margin, burn, and runway

 - Prepare the monthly investor updates

 - Keep gross margin accurate, with COGS and vendor costs, including voice AI infrastructure, categorized right every month

Run finance operations

 - Run a fast, accurate monthly close with an accounting partner you choose and manage

 - Own payroll, taxes, and filings

 - Get invoices out on time and cash collected on schedule

 - Set up spend controls: department budgets, expense policies, and a weekly AP and approval process, so the founders stop approving every expense

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4-6 years of experience, ideally starting in investment banking and followed by finance at a high-growth startup.

 - Rigor as a core competency. People trust your numbers because they never have to check them twice

 - Builder mentality. You're comfortable being the only finance person at first and getting deep into the details of a close, and just as comfortable stepping back to tell the founders what the numbers mean.

BONUS POINTS

 - Healthcare or health tech exposure, at a company or covering the sector in banking

 - Hands-on with modern finance tools like Brex, Carta, NetSuite or QuickBooks

 - You've supported a fundraise, a first audit, or a finance system rollout

 - You've managed an outsourced accounting firm and held it to a high bar

WHY PROSPER

 - A trillion-dollar problem, real customers, and revenue growing 5x

 - A function you own outright: the plan, the metrics, and the team you build

 - Direct access to the founders and the board

 - Competitive base and meaningful equity

jobs.description:
ABOUT SYGALDRY

Sygaldry Technologies is building quantum-accelerated AI servers to exponentially speed up training and inference for AI. By integrating quantum and AI, we're accelerating the path to superintelligence, and addressing the problem of rising compute costs and energy bottlenecks. Sygaldry AI servers combine multiple qubit types within a single, fault-tolerant architecture to deliver the combination of cost, scale, and speed necessary for advanced AI applications. We pioneer new domains in physics, engineering, and AI, tackling the hardest challenges with a grounded, optimistic, and rigorous culture. We're looking for individuals ready to define the intersection of quantum and AI and drive its profound global impact.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Nanophotonics Fabrication Engineer to develop and execute fabrication processes for photonic devices and test structures. You will own process development, cleanroom fabrication, characterization, and yield improvement, working closely with design and experimental teams. The ideal candidate has substantial hands-on nanofabrication experience, enjoys troubleshooting complex process flows, and takes pride in careful documentation and reproducible results.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Develop, execute, and refine multistep fabrication flows for nanophotonic devices, from substrate preparation through final inspection.

 - Perform high-resolution lithography, thin-film deposition, wet and dry etching, and associated cleaning and surface preparation steps.

 - Use microscopy and thin-film and surface metrology to assess pattern fidelity, film quality, etch profiles, and fabrication defects.

 - Design structured experiments to identify process limits, diagnose failure modes, and improve uniformity, repeatability, and yield.

 - Maintain process travelers, recipes, fabrication records, and clear documentation of process changes and results.

 - Collaborate with photonic designers and test engineers to relate fabrication outcomes to measured optical performance and inform design and process improvements.

 - Coordinate fabrication activities with shared cleanroom staff and external partners, while maintaining safe working practices and careful sample tracking.

YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - A B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Applied Physics, or a related field. Significant hands-on fabrication experience is especially valued.

 - Substantial cleanroom experience and demonstrated ownership of process development or troubleshooting for a multistep microfabrication or nanofabrication flow.

 - Practical experience with high-resolution lithography and pattern transfer, including an understanding of how process variation affects device geometry and performance.

 - Experience with microscopy and metrology for process characterization, defect analysis, and process control.

 - Strong experimental design and data analysis skills, with experience using Python or similar tools.

 - The ability to work independently, communicate results clearly, and collaborate across technical disciplines.

 - Fabrication of integrated photonic or other nanoscale optical devices.

 - Electron-beam lithography, dry-etch process development, or thin-film process optimization.

 - Connecting fabrication measurements with optical characterization results.

 - Working autonomously in shared university or partner cleanrooms.

 - Developing repeatable processes from early research workflows and transferring them between tools or facilities.

HOW WE’RE DIFFERENT

At Sygaldry, curiosity and intellectual courage drive our work. We approach ambitious challenges with a grounded, optimistic, and rigorous culture and know that kind people build the strongest teams. We prioritize mission over ego and collaborate openly with a strong sense of shared purpose. We dream big, yet we execute with a love of detail. We’re looking for scientists, engineers, and operators to forge new paths with us at the intersection of quantum and AI.

CULTURE & BENEFITS

 - Visa Sponsorship - We know what it takes to make top talent thrive here. We’re open to supporting visas whenever possible.

 - Compensation - We value your contribution and invest in your future with a competitive salary and meaningful equity.

 - Benefits - Your well-being matters. We provide company-sponsored health coverage to give you and your family peace of mind.

 - Connection - Whether it’s company offsite or casual crew socials, we make time to connect, recharge, and have fun together.

 - Time Off - We trust you to take the time you need. Unlimited PTO so you can rest, recharge, and come back ready to make an impact.

We encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. If you don’t think this role is right for you, but you believe that you would have something meaningful to to contribute to our mission, please reach out at [email in original advert]

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

 1. 💙 Care deeply

 2. 🏋️‍♀️ Work hard

We have an ambitious mission: to unlock access to healthcare by navigating patients to the right place, first time. We’re going to create a world where every appointment is transparent and bookable, starting in General Practice. We're the team to do this - We were previously ranked 8th fastest growing startup in UK and 33rd fastest in Europe.

We are hiring Account Executives to help us get in front of more practices. Your core focus will be on full cycle sales from lead generation to closing and onboarding practices.

You’ll be joining an ambitious sales team with prior experience at Monzo, Revolut, the Civil Service, the NHS, investment banking, consulting, and other VC-backed startups. Everyone works in pairs to own a geographic patch. We work in pairs because we believe it encourages peer learning and healthy team culture.

Progression works across three dimensions:

 2. Selling more advanced products

 3. Training/ coaching other members of the team

This is a place to do your life’s best work.

Our mission is to unlock access to healthcare. You will contribute by increasing appointment supply. This is achieved through selling more products to more practices.

 - You will own a geographical patch and do everything it takes to get at least 10 live practices a week.

 - You will hone your craft until you achieve a 70% demo-to-sign rate (demo conversion rate) and a 90% sign-to-live rate (funnelling).

 - You will help the team aim for a stretch target of 15 practices live per person per week.

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it. 

THE ROLE

Agents don't run in browsers. They run in sandboxes — and you will lead the team building ours.

You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. 

We build secure, isolated, network-controlled environments with snapshotting primitives, designed for AI agents and reinforcement-learning workloads. An RL training run doesn't need one environment; it needs thousands, created and destroyed every second. An agent needs to be sandboxed from the world while still feeling fast enough to be useful. That tension — airtight isolation, at fleet scale, at low latency — is the product.

Your customers are the people building the next generation of AI software on our infrastructure; the primitives you ship become the runtime their agents live in.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build the isolation layer: microVMs or containers, namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, snapshot and restore.

 - Own the security boundary. Customers run code they didn't write and can't fully trust — your systems make that safe.

 - Scale to fleets: creation latency, density, and lifecycle management for thousands of concurrent environments.

 - Design and build alongside your team, owning the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

 - Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

 - Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

 - Partner with Product Managers to turn frontier research needs into shippable primitives.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

 - Deep Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, virtualization — ideally microVMs of the Firecracker class.

 - You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

 - You understand network isolation at the packet level — not just firewall rules.

 - Performance instincts: you know what a syscall costs, and you have the profiles to prove you've cared.

 - 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems.

 - You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

 

WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

 

WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is seeking a Senior Ground Software Engineer (Telemetry & Control) to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is excited to own all of our aircraft’s data from the moment it leaves the plane until a command goes back to it: everything from the aircraft radio down. You will architect the end-to-end system that ingests, processes, stores, and visualizes flight telemetry in Mission Control, observes the health of the aircraft, and commands the plane. This is not a big-data problem; the data is modest in volume but complex and time critical, and it should reach an operator’s screen within one second of leaving the aircraft. Your work at Astro Mechanica will be fast-paced in a dynamic startup environment and will have a direct impact on our mission.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Architect and build the end-to-end ground data pipeline, from telemetry ingestion off the radio link through real-time processing, storage, backend APIs and business logic, to front-end visualization in Mission Control

 - Drive low latency across the entire system, not just one stage, targeting roughly one second from aircraft to operator display

 - Design for fault tolerance so that a failed network path, a crashed service, or a cloud region outage never puts the aircraft at risk

 - Select and operate the right database technologies, including time series databases, for flight telemetry

 - Build the tools operators use to monitor aircraft health and command the plane

 - Keep the pipeline clean and simple enough that the team can reason about it end to end

 - Work closely with flight software and other engineering disciplines to define the interfaces between the aircraft and the ground

 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Math, or a Science discipline and 5+ years of professional software development experience

 - Experience building real-time data or telemetry ingestion and processing systems

 - Experience implementing a cloud stack that ingests data, stores it in a database, and processes it to serve an application (web, mobile, or otherwise)

 - Hands-on experience with time series databases and a strong understanding of the trade-offs between database technologies and data ingestion approaches

 - Experience designing low-latency, high-reliability systems, including fault tolerance for network and service failures

 - Proficiency in the languages, frameworks, and API design used to expose data from a database to applications

 - Breadth across the stack, with the greatest depth on the backend and cloud side; you don’t need to have built every layer

 - Front-end experience building web apps that query a server and render live data is a plus

 - Experience with telemetry from physical systems (aircraft, launch vehicles, satellites, autonomous vehicles, or connected vehicle fleets), radio links, or mission control and observability tooling is a plus
 
 

PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment
 
 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Senior Power Electronics Controls Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

 

WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

 

WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is seeking a Power Electronics Controls Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is a controls engineer at heart who is excited to own the control of the power electronics that drive our propulsion: an 800-volt system delivering 1 megawatt of electrical power to the motors on our Gen 5 engine. You will bring that same controls expertise to our ground power systems, where large turbines and generators must be governed and kept in sync. You will work on a small, tight team alongside a mechanical engineer focused on the liquid-cooled inverter enclosure and an electrical engineer focused on the inverter hardware. Your work at Astro Mechanica will have a direct impact on the configuration and performance of our engine.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Design, implement, and tune control systems for the inverters that drive the motors on our 800 V, 1 MW propulsion system

 - Develop controls for related power electronics, including DC-DC converters and motor controllers

 - Own bus control and governor design for our electrical systems

 - Support ground power by synchronizing and governing coupled systems, such as a 13 MW turbine and generator or a connection to grid power

 - Take systems from concept through hardware, validating control performance on real equipment

 - Work closely with mechanical, electrical, and propulsion engineers to bring the inverter from design through test

 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field and 5+ years of experience in power electronics controls

 - Hands-on experience designing controls for power electronic systems, such as DC-DC converters, motor controllers, or inverters

 - Proven track record of building one of these systems, not just modeling or analyzing it

 - Working knowledge of motor control, including Field Oriented Control (FOC) and related techniques

 - Experience with three-phase electrical systems and machines, such as permanent magnet motors

 - Experience with high-voltage, high-power-density systems, such as EV traction or eVTOL propulsion

 - Inverter design experience is a plus

 - Experience synchronizing and governing coupled, complex power systems, such as multiple inverters, or turbines and generators for bus-tied or grid-tied power, is a plus
 
 

PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment
 
 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Sr. Electrical Harness Engineer
jobs.description:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full‑Time

Job Title: Senior Electrical Harness Engineer

 

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

 

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

EDDA's cables are its nerves, and we're hiring the person who owns them: every harness in the product — power, signal, data and fiber — from wire list through connector selection, routing across moving axes, bench prototyping, qualification and production sourcing. You have shipped rugged, high-flex-life harnesses and are equally at home with copper, fiber and hybrid builds.

EDDA is the low-cost counter-UAS solution, so the job is one judgment made hundreds of times: rugged where it matters, cost-efficient where it doesn't. MIL-spec circular connectors and continuous-flex cable where a harness crosses the elevation axis and takes recoil; a less-rugged sealed connector and standard jacket where it sits bolted inside the base. You defend each call with test data and a cost roll-up.

 

What You'll Own

 - Power: battery, bus and motor-drive feeds — conductor sizing, voltage drop, thermal budgets, fusing, grounding.

 - Signal and data: encoder, sensor, CAN, Ethernet, USB and camera links, with the shielding they need.

 - Fiber and hybrid: EMI-immune, high-bandwidth links between sensor heads and compute, including copper/fiber hybrids through one rugged connector.

 - Moving axes: continuous-flex and torsion-rated cables, service loops, cable carriers and slip-ring interfaces across EDDA's azimuth and elevation joints.

 - Connectors and sealing: rugged circular MIL-spec where it earns its place, less-rugged sealed or overmolded connectors where it doesn't.

 - Manufacturing and sourcing: formboard drawings, IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship, contract-manufacturer qualification, second sources and cost-down.

 

Essential Duties

 - Architect the harness system: turn the electrical architecture into a harness topology — segmentation, connector locations, grounding and shield strategy, service loops and slip-ring boundaries — that is buildable, field-serviceable and cheap to make.

 - Design and specify: wire lists, schematics, 3-D routings and formboard drawings; select conductors, jackets, shielding and connectors against electrical, environmental and cost requirements, with the margin shown.

 - Design for flex life: specify cable construction, bend radii, twist limits, carrier geometry and strain relief for harnesses that cross moving axes and take recoil; set and prove cycle-life targets.

 - Prototype at the bench: build first-article harnesses yourself — crimp, solder, terminate fiber, trial overmolds — so every drawing is proven by hand before it goes to a supplier.

 - Test and qualify: flex, pull and vibration rigs; continuity, hipot and insertion-loss tests; shock, vibration, temperature, water and dust qualification; root-cause failures that come back from the range.

 - Engineer the cost: hold the harness BOM to target — standardize connector families, cut unique part numbers, go rugged only where the requirement demands it.

 - Source and release: qualify contract manufacturers, run RFQs, manage second sources and lead times, and release drawings and acceptance tests that production can build from without you.

 

Requirements

 - Experience: 8+ years designing, specifying and sourcing cable harnesses for shipped hardware — robotics, aerospace, defense or industrial equipment that lives outdoors and gets abused.

 - Rugged, high-flex-life harnesses: you have designed harnesses across moving joints (pan-tilt, gimbal, turret, robot arm or cable-track), specified continuous-flex constructions and bend limits, and proven cycle life on a flex rig.

 - Copper, fiber and hybrid: hands-on with shielded multi-conductor copper builds, single-mode and multimode fiber termination and testing, and copper/fiber hybrids through a shared connector.

 - Connectors and sealing: working command of rugged circular MIL-spec families (MIL-DTL-38999 or similar) and less-rugged sealed families — when each is right, how to terminate and seal them, and what they cost.

 - Harness CAD and documentation: wire lists, 3-D routing and formboard drawings in SolidWorks Electrical/Routing, Zuken E3, Capital, Altium or similar; drawings a contract manufacturer can quote and build from.

 - Workmanship: IPC/WHMA-A-620 fluent; you crimp with calibrated tooling and pull-test your terminations.

 - Signal integrity basics: shielding, grounding and impedance control for Ethernet, USB, CAN and camera links.

 - Test and failure analysis: continuity, hipot, insertion-loss and flex testing; you have cut open a failed harness, found the root cause and fixed the design.

 - Compliance: U.S. citizenship and the ability to pass a background check.

 

Nice‑to‑Have

 - MIL-STD-810 shock, vibration, temperature, sand/dust and immersion; MIL-STD-461 EMI/EMC.

 - Harnesses on weapon-mounted or recoil-loaded systems.

 - Slip rings and rotary joints — electrical, fiber and hybrid.

 - Expanded-beam and MIL-PRF-29504 fiber termini; OTDR and fusion splicing.

 - Overmolding and potting design rules and tooling.

 - UAS or counter-UAS plat

jobs.title: CNC Machinist
jobs.description:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full‑Time

Job Title: CNC Machinist

 

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

 

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

You are the second half of a two-person machine shop, working alongside our Machine Shop Manager to keep the spindles turning across a wider band of hours than one person can. You bring about five years of stick time on CNC mills and lathes, you program your own parts in Mastercam, and you handle the rest of a working shop: manual machines, sawing, deburring, tapping, fitting and inspection. The shop builds the hardware EDDA's R&D and test program runs on — turret structure, mounts, drive parts, fixtures and test rigs — often from a CAD model that landed that morning.

 
 

Essential Duties

 - Program your own parts: CAD to toolpaths in Mastercam, tooling, speeds and feeds, prove-out at the machine, G-code edits at the control.

 - Set up and run CNC mills and lathes: workholding, offsets, probing, first article to print, then hold tolerance across the run.

 - Do the rest of the shop's work: manual mill and lathe, saw, drill press, tapping, deburring, press fits and inserts, light fitting and assembly.

 - Inspect and document: hand tools on a surface plate, GD&T, first-article records — in aluminum, steel, stainless, plastics and the occasional titanium.

 - Run the shop with the manager: split and stagger the queue, hand off cleanly, give engineers honest lead times and DFM feedback, keep the machines maintained and the shop safe and clean.

 

Requirements

 - Experience: about 5 years (3–7) in a working machine shop, with real stick time on both CNC mills and CNC lathes.

 - CNC programming (required): you write your own programs from CAD in CAM — we run Mastercam — read and edit G-code at the control, and have proven out your own programs. Running someone else's program does not meet this bar.

 - Setup and operation: workholding, fixturing, tool and work offsets, first-article proof-out; you hold ±0.001" when the print calls for it.

 - General shop process and inspection: manual machining, sawing, drilling, tapping, deburring and fitting; read GD&T and inspect with calipers, micrometers, height and bore gauges.

 - Flexible schedule: willing to work a staggered shift coordinated with the Machine Shop Manager — early starts some weeks, late finishes others.

 - Compliance and physical: U.S. citizenship, ability to pass a background check, lift 50 lb and stand for long periods.

 

Nice‑to‑Have

 - Prototype or R&D shop background: one-offs, fast turnaround, incomplete drawings, engineers at your elbow.

 - 4th/5-axis milling, live-tooling lathes, Fanuc macros and probing cycles.

 - CAD, not just CAM: model a fixture or simple part in SolidWorks and design your own workholding.

 - Secondary processes: TIG welding, sheet metal, 3-D printing, or spec'ing anodize, plating and heat treat.

 - Weapon, firearms, aerospace or defense hardware; security clearance or the ability to obtain one.

 

Benefits

 - Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.

 - Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.

 - Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.

 - The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.

 - 100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.

 - Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.

 - Zero Red Tape: You report to the founders. You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.

 - Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.

 - Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

 

About the Interview

 1. Virtual interview (45 min via MS Teams)

 2. Onsite interview in Austin (1.5 hr in-person)

You will combine hands-on data analysis, statistical reasoning, and systems engineering to turn complex data into insights that shape development, support verification and validation (V&V), and inform launch readiness.

 - Define development and autonomy performance metrics, and implement them in code against fleet, test, and simulation data

 - Build data pipelines, analyses, and tools using Python, SQL, or similar technologies to turn large datasets into insights on performance, gaps, and launch readiness.

 - Track metrics over time, catch regressions early, and guide engineering priorities with data

 - Read autonomy stack code to trace system behavior back to requirements and root causes

 - Work with systems engineers to translate requirements into measurable metrics and evaluation criteria.

 - Drive verification and validation across simulation, closed-course, and on-road testing

 - Build dashboards and readiness views for engineering leadership and customers

 - Collaborate across autonomy, perception, hardware, safety, and test teams

We're looking for someone who has:

 - 3+ years of experience in data science, data engineering, systems engineering, V&V, or a related role in ADAS, autonomous driving (L2–L4, L4 preferred), or robotics.

 - MS/BS in Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, Computer Science, Robotics, Data Science, or equivalent

 - Hands-on experience analyzing large datasets with Python and SQL, including statistical analysis, data visualization, and interpreting variability and uncertainty.

 - Experience defining and reporting metrics that drive decisions on a development program

 - Ability to read production code (Python, C++, or similar) well enough to trace behavior through an autonomy or robotics stack

 - Strong systems engineering fundamentals: requirements, functional decomposition, architecture, and test planning

 - Experience with V&V for ADAS/AD or robotics, including defining what is sufficient for launch

 - Working knowledge of fault management and a solid understanding of AV stack components

 - Strong communication skills for explaining data-driven findings to engineers, leadership, and customers

Nice to have:

 - Autonomous trucking, off-highway, or off-road autonomy experience.

 - Simulation-based validation and scenario-based testing

ABOUT ARTIE

Artie is a fully-managed real-time data streaming platform that replicates production databases into data warehouses and lakes - in real time, with zero maintenance. We make high-volume data replication simple, reliable, and scalable for engineering teams.

Our platform powers mission-critical use cases including fraud and risk monitoring, inventory visibility, customer-facing analytics, and AI/ML workloads.

We’re trusted by teams like Substack, Alloy, and ClickUp, and raised a Series A from top-tier investors including Standard Capital, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Pathlight, and the founders of Dropbox and Mode.

Artie is built for engineers who care about performance, reliability, and operational simplicity - and we’re growing fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Founding Customer Success Manager to own every customer after the contract is signed: onboarding, adoption, renewals, and growing the account.

Today our founders and engineers run post-sales themselves. Our customers love the product and the responsiveness, but at our size that model doesn't scale, and customers deserve one person who owns both their outcome and their commercial relationship. That person is you.

This role is half trusted advisor, half account owner. Our customers are data engineers and platform leads running Artie in production, where a stale table or a missing row matters. You'll be technical enough to diagnose most issues yourself, and commercial enough to carry a renewal and expansion number, negotiate contracts, and run expansion deals end to end. You'll work directly with our founders, sales, and engineering, and set the bar for every CSM and account manager who comes after you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - When something does go wrong, own the customer side of the incident: a clear timeline, a plain explanation of root cause, and what will prevent it next time

Own renewals

 - Run every renewal starting three months out: usage review, pricing, terms, and the conversation itself

 - Forecast renewals accurately in our CRM and flag risk early, well before the renewal date

 - Negotiate contract terms, multi-year commitments, and price changes, and work through customer procurement and security reviews

Manage and grow your accounts

 - Turn happy customers into references, case studies, and referrals

jobs.description:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full‑Time

Job Title: Senior Mechatronics Engineer - Actuation & Drivetrain

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

EDDA is only as good as its actuators, and we're hiring the person who owns them. You will be our servo wizard: the single owner of every motor, actuator, gearbox and solenoid in the product, from the first torque and inertia calculation through supplier selection, bench characterization, control-loop tuning, abuse testing and production release. You are as fluent in gearbox design — backlash, torsional stiffness, efficiency, lubrication, lifetime — as you are inside the current loop of the servo driving it. And you have lived with motion systems that get rained on, dropped, fired next to and bounced across a field on the back of a truck.

What You'll Own

Everything in the product that converts electrons into motion is yours — the parts, the suppliers, the test data and the tuning.

 - Motors and actuators: BLDC/PMSM and frameless torque motors, steppers where they earn their place, linear actuators — every axis that moves EDDA's azimuth, elevation and auxiliary mechanisms.

 - Gearboxes and drivetrain: planetary, strain-wave (harmonic), cycloidal, worm and belt stages; the direct-drive-versus-geared call on each axis; bearing arrangements, preload, backlash and the stiffness budget that sets achievable control bandwidth.

 - Solenoids and discrete actuators: latches, safeties, indexing and release mechanisms — the fast, simple actuators that must work every time, in the cold, after being dropped.

 - Motor drives and tuning: drive selection or specification, commutation and feedback (encoders, resolvers, Hall sensors), current/velocity/position loop tuning, feedforward and filtering.

 - Characterization and test: dynamometer and bench rigs, thermal derating, torque ripple and cogging, efficiency maps, endurance and abuse testing, and the acceptance tests production runs on every unit.

 - The actuation supply chain: vendor qualification, custom motor and gearbox specifications, second sources, cost-down and the lead times that production depends on.

Essential Duties

 - Size and select: turn slew-rate, acceleration, pointing-accuracy and duty-cycle requirements into torque, speed, reflected-inertia and thermal budgets; pick or specify the motor, gear ratio and drive that meet them with margin — and show the math.

 - Design the drivetrain: own the mechanical path from rotor to load — gear stages, couplings, shafts, bearings, preload, lubrication and seals — and the stiffness and backlash budget that determines how hard the loops can be pushed.

 - Characterize everything: build the rigs and run the tests — torque constant, back-EMF, inductance, cogging and ripple, friction and stiction, efficiency, thermal rise, backlash and lost motion — so tuning starts from a measured plant, not a datasheet.

 - Tune the loops: commission and tune current, velocity and position loops (PID, feedforward, notch filters, observers) for aggressive high-bandwidth tracking without exciting structural modes or cooking the motor.

 - Engineer for abuse: design and qualify actuation for shock and vibration from vehicle mounts and weapon firing, dust, mud, water, salt, EMI and temperature extremes; lead failure analysis when hardware comes back from the range broken, and make sure the next revision doesn't.

 - Own the supply chain: qualify vendors, write motor, gearbox and solenoid specifications, manage second sources and lead times, and drive cost-down for production volumes.

 - Bridge the teams: be the technical interface between mechanical, electrical, firmware and robotics on anything that moves; triage failures at the hardware-software boundary and call whether a problem is mechanical, electrical or control.

 - Document and release: derating curves, tuning procedures, acceptance tests and drawings that production and field teams can execute without you in the room.

Requirements

 - Experience: 10+ years in mechatronics or motion-system engineering with a track record of shipping servo-driven products — ideally pan-tilt units, gimbals, turrets, robotic joints or vehicle-mounted systems.

 - Servo depth: hands-on selection, commissioning and tuning of BLDC/PMSM servo systems: field-oriented control, current/velocity/position loops, encoder and resolver feedback, drive configuration, and diagnosing instability, resonance and thermal limits on the bench.

 - Gearbox fluency: working command of planetary, strain-wave, cycloidal and worm drives — ratio selection, efficiency, backlash, torsional stiffness, lubrication and lifetime — and a clear sense of when direct drive beats gearing.

 - Actuator characterization: you have built test rigs and run dynamometer, thermal, efficiency and endurance tests; comfortable with scopes, current probes, DAQ and Python or MATLAB to extract plant parameters from data.

 - Drivetrain design: can design and detail the mechanical path from rotor to load — bearings, shafts, couplings, seals, preload — in CAD (SolidWorks or similar) with tolerance analysis.

jobs.title: Electricals Materials Handler (Inventory)
jobs.description:
About Etched

Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Job Summary

The Electricals Materials Handler owns the lifecycle of every electrical component that goes onto an Etched module: from receiving, through storage, inspection and kitting, to consumption on our in-house SMT line and at our contract manufacturers (CMs). You'll sit on the Inventory team and be the source of truth for board electricals: what we have, where it is, what condition it is in, and what is about to run out.

This hire will run clean consignment with CMs.Success looks like: Etched-owned material at CM sites is counted, reconciled and traceable, so builds don't stall on a missing reel and variances get closed.Board materials are accounted fully: moisture-sensitive parts are handled correctly, kits match the released BOM with no shortages or substitutions, and scrap and write-offs trend toward zero. The data you produce lets Procurement buy against real on-hand, consumed and in-transit numbers instead of estimates.

Key Responsibilities

 - Storage and handling: Receive, label, measure quantity, inspect and put away board electricals, connectors and boards, with full traceability. Run ESD-safe handling and moisture-sensitivity (MSD) control: dry cabinets, bake-out, exposure-time tracking.

 - Consignment with CMs: Own the record of Etched-owned material held at contract manufacturers: shipments out, consumption, returns and scrap. Run cycle counts and periodic reconciliations against CM reports; investigate and close every variance.

 - Incoming quality control: Inspect incoming lots: part marking, quantity, packaging, reel and tray condition, date codes. Quarantine and disposition non-conforming material; raise supplier issues through Procurement. Keep first-article and inspection records for every new part number and supplier.

 - Kitting: Pull and kit components to the released BOM and revision for prototype builds, bring-up boards, in-house SMT runs and CM production. Flag shortages, substitutions and revision mismatches before the kit ships, not after the line stops. Pack and document kits for line-side staging and CM handoff, including MSD status and special-handling notes.

 - Reporting to Procurement: Publish a weekly view of on-hand, allocated, in-transit and at-CM quantities by part number. Flag parts approaching reorder point, excess or obsolete stock, and lots nearing MSD or shelf-life limits. Feed actual consumption and scrap data back so forecasts and PO quantities match reality.

 - Processes: Write the SOPs for receiving, consignment transfers, RMA and return-to-stock so the process does not depend on who is on shift. Contribute to the ESD, 5S and safety programs shared with the SMT line.

 - Automation: Help our agentic manufacturing team pull inventory and consumption data into automated reporting and reorder signals.

 - Able to read a BOM, a PCB assembly drawing and a component datasheet, and spot when a delivered part does not match them.

Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)

 - Exposure to datacenter hardware: accelerator cards, server base boards, high-power or high-speed interconnect components.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
At Parallel, we build AI agents that help healthcare organizations automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.

Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost to manual, repetitive administrative tasks. Legacy software hasn't helped: it has made work slower, more complex and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change this. Our technology combines large language models with system-level automation to do real work inside existing hospital tools. No integration, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding and frees up time for medical teams to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024 and already have 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people. We are backed by top-tier investors (Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI), and this is just the beginning.

The future of healthcare isn't just digital, it's automated. Come help us build it!

CONTEXT

Parallel is an AI-powered platform that helps hospitals code medical acts faster and more accurately. We're a small, fast-moving team building a product that's already live in hospitals — and we're scaling.

Until now, the Operations team has been handling everything: client onboarding, customer success, internal process building, and analytics. We're growing fast, and we need someone who can take full ownership of a client portfolio and help us structure our ops for the next stage.

Your mission

As our new Ops, you'll work hand in hand with Clémentine (Operations Manager) to deliver a best-in-class experience to our hospital clients and internal coders — from day one of onboarding to long-term success. You'll also contribute to building the operational backbone that lets Parallel scale without losing quality.

Concretely, you will :

 - Own the onboarding and follow-up of a portfolio of 30+ clients (hospitals and internal coders), ensuring smooth adoption and top-tier support

 - Build and maintain scalable CS processes, tools and routines to monitor client satisfaction and usage

 - Leverage data to identify bottlenecks and opportunities across client workflows and internal coding operations

 - Act as the key link between clients and our Product & Tech teams — translating field insights into actionable priorities
 
 

Outcomes

At 6 months, you will have :

 - Independently managed a portfolio of clients end-to-end, with no escalation needed for standard situations

 - Deployed and trained new clients without Clémentine's direct involvement

 - Identified and implemented 1 to 2 process improvements on internal ops (tracking, dashboards, workflows)

 - Established yourself as a trusted point of contact for both clients and internal teams
 
 

You are :

 - Autonomous and structured. You manage your workload without being told what to do next. You build your own tracking systems, follow up proactively, and close loops without being reminded.

 - Hands-on and pragmatic. You'd rather ship an imperfect solution and iterate than wait for the perfect framework. You figure things out.

 - Analytically sharp. You don't rely on gut feel alone — you look at the data, spot patterns, and propose concrete actions.

 - A strong communicator in French. You've dealt with clients before. You know how to adapt your tone whether you're talking to a hospital DG or a medical coder, without changing your substance.

 - Genuinely curious about product, AI, or healthcare — or all three.
 
 

This job is for you if :

 - You have 2–4 years of experience in a startup, consulting firm, or project management role

 - You've managed client relationships directly — and you're comfortable being the face of a company

 - You thrive when there's no playbook yet and see that as an opportunity, not a problem

 - You want to join a small team at a pivotal moment and have a real impact on how we operate
 
 

Hiring process

 1. Quick call with Wallerand (talent)

 2. Call with Clémentine, Operations Manager

 3. Case study in our Paris office (with Paul & Clémentine)

 4. Final meeting with Paul, CEO

Fast, no fluff. We'll give you clear feedback at every step.

Why should you join us ?

 - You'll work on a product that's already live and used daily in French hospitals — real impact, fast

 - You'll have full ownership from day one — no micro-management, no hand-holding

 - You'll be embedded in a tight-knit team where your work is visible and your voice matters

 - You'll learn across ops, analytics, product and client management simultaneously

 - Clear path to Lead Ops at 24 months as we structure the team into verticals

 - Flexibility: on average one day of remote work per week, and one remote week per year

 
 
 

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.
If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

jobs.title: Founding Sales
jobs.description:
Four months ago Mastra was an incredibly popular open-source agent tool with very little monetization. Then we launched our platform, our head of demand gen joined, and our chief of staff joined. Now we’re closing a couple of deals a week.

So now we’re looking for you to join. Yeah, that’s right, you. You’ll be our founding AE.

This is the second dedicated sales hire at Mastra. Our pipeline is growing faster than one person can work it. The math to our 2026 number says we need you.

You'll start day 1 with a warm pipe. Your job is to run the motion hard, then make it better.

We tilt full-cycle, mid-market. Think: Series A–C companies, usually with regulatory or infra constraints. Hot leads that land as existing users of the open-source framework, and a sales cycle measured in mid-single-digit weeks. You'll talk to eng leaders, earn their trust, and close.

What you'll be selling

Mastra is the open-source TypeScript-native framework and platform for building AI agents with a serious developer following, and the commercial products that following graduates into:

 - Platform (Enterprise) — Studio, Server, and the infrastructure teams use to develop, run, debug, observe, and scale agents in production. Hosted by us or self-hosted for regulated and air-gapped orgs.

 - Agent Builder — build and edit agents without touching code. This is the wedge into non-technical buyers and the centerpiece of more and more conversations.

 - Concierge — embedded Mastra engineers (FDE model) shipping alongside the customer's team, with direct access and SLAs.

These conversations need an expert craftsmen who can run discovery, scope a solution, and close. And, by the way — we’ll be launching some more products at our conference in late January — we think could double your close rate.

What great + What’s hard about this job + what you’ll need

Every week at Mastra is a launch week. Read our blog to get a sense. The product is constantly evolving. So you have to be the kind of person who finds that energizing.

Our platform and enterprise features are still relatively new. Our most attractive features, like trace intelligence, agent learning, and knowledge, are still in early access.

You need to be able to understand how our open-source developer framework works. Not on the level of an engineer, but you’ll need to come across as a smart PM that can understand their use cases and challenges. Dev tools, OSS, infra, or AI sales experience is a strong plus. Comfort with ambiguity and constant change is non-negotiable.

We have a lot of small startups and bootstrapped startups and you need to be willing to sell some $5K-$10k deals to highly enthusiastic users that don’t have a ton of budget, at least for the first few months. That’s one of the reasons this is closer to a 60-hour-a-week job than a 40-hour-a-week job.

The best founding sellers we've seen are former founders (or founder mentalities) who are product-obsessed, customer-obsessed, and insanely driven.

We don't need you to invent the process. We need you to adapt it, push on it, and tell us what to fix.

Process

Introductory Call: Margarita, our recruiter (30 minutes)

First Interview: Josh, Chief of Staff (1 hour)

Remote Super Day:

A. Sam, CEO (45 minutes)

B. Shane, CPO (45 Minutes)

C. Aron, Head of Demand Gen (45 Minutes)

The first 45 days

Week 1: Mostly training. Listen in on all active sales deals. We’ve also got more game tape than you’d have time to watch, dozens of case studies in written and video form.

Week 2-3: Game on. We’ll quickly ramp up to 10-15 first meetings / week. Remember, our pipeline is our community. We need you to qualify aggressively but gracefully.

Week 4-5. Deep dives. Your first deal or two should be in procurement — at least. You’re starting to viscerally feel how to accelerate the process and move folks through the pipeline.

Week 6-7. Closing time. Our Chief of Staff closed his first enterprise logo 43 days into starting the job. With a new platform. You’d better beat his time — and we’ll toss 2K to you (extra) for each enterprise license deal you close before this date.

One last thing

We’re competitive here, but we’re nerds, we play fair, and we’re a team. Our founders sat on weekend evenings during their winter YC batch at the SF Athletic bar and watched the playoffs, Vikings vs Lions and Rams vs 49ers on the big screen while they drank beer and coded.

Each one of them roots for a different team but they all cheered together and went home as friends. We all want to win and we all win together.

If you work out here we’ll have five people you help us hire in not too long. That means we won’t hire jerks, so don’t be one. Chat soon.

ABOUT MASTRA

Mastra is the open-source TypeScript framework for building AI agents. Built by the team behind Gatsby, backed by Y Combinator https://www.ycombinator.com and Spark Capital https://www.sparkcapital.com, with $35M raised total. We went from 0 to 28k+ stars https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra and 2M+ weekly npm downloads https://npmtrends.com/@mastra/core in less than 2 years. 

Small team, shipping fast, fully remote. Most of us work across North American and European time zones.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Site Reliability Engineering
jobs.description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Replit enables people to build software with AI. The systems underneath that experience must support safe production changes, measurable reliability, and predictable performance as usage grows.

This Engineering Manager will lead SRE across observability, incident management, load testing, performance engineering, cloud cost and capacity, and rollout infrastructure. You'll lead and grow an existing team that builds and operates production platforms and works hands-on across application and infrastructure boundaries.

This is a software-building leadership role, not simply an incident-management function. You'll help teams ship safely, understand production behavior, and remove performance bottlenecks through concrete engineering improvements. You should be comfortable going deep on a rollout failure or performance investigation while developing technical leaders and sustainable ownership across a distributed team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Observability. Build and operate metrics, logs, traces, and alerting capabilities. Help teams establish meaningful SLOs and use production telemetry to diagnose problems and verify improvements.

 - Incident Management. Own incident tooling and practices, coordinate cross-team response, and turn incident reviews into engineering improvements that reduce recovery time and repeat failures.

 - Load Testing. Build and maintain load/failure testing capabilities. Validate critical paths under expected demand, quantify headroom, and test recovery and production readiness with service owners.

 - Performance Engineering. Lead deep engagements with internal teams on SLOs and end-to-end performance. Use profiling, telemetry, and load tests to identify bottlenecks and deliver improvements with service owners—not just recommendations.

 - Stay technically engaged. Review designs and production changes, debug difficult failure modes, and use AI coding tools—including Replit—to prototype and automate. Apply rigorous review and verification to AI-generated changes.

 - Build and grow a high-ownership engineering team. Coach engineers, develop technical leaders, manage performance, and hire against agreed needs. Make distributed collaboration, mentoring, and backup coverage deliberate rather than relying on a few permanent escalation points.

 - Measure outcomes and close the loop. Track rollout safety, recovery time, repeat incidents, critical-path latency/throughput, test coverage, and improvements arising from cost/capacity analysis. Agree success measures and continuing ownership with partner teams.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Demonstrated engineering management. You have led and developed engineers, made prioritization and performance decisions, hired thoughtfully, and delivered through a team—not only acted as its strongest individual contributor.

 - Software-oriented production systems depth. You have built and operated distributed systems or reliability platforms and can reason across deployment behavior, Kubernetes, telemetry, service dependencies, and recovery mechanisms.

 - Safe-change and performance judgment. You have led consequential migrations or incidents and used measurement to diagnose reliability or performance problems. You can distinguish symptoms from causes and validate fixes under realistic conditions.

 - Platform-product and cross-team judgment. You can build capabilities other teams adopt, lead hands-on engagements without absorbing every service's operations, and make clear tradeoffs among reliability, performance, engineering effort, and cost.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with GitOps or progressive-delivery platforms such as Harness, ArgoCD, or Kargo.

 - Experience with observability, profiling, load-testing, and failure-testing systems, including OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling.

 - Experience with cloud cost attribution, capacity planning, and provider coordination, particularly on GCP.

 - Experience growing distributed teams and using AI tools to increase engineering output while preserving production safeguards.

jobs.title: Solution Engineer - Vehicle OS
jobs.description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a bright engineer to help our customers solve complex technical problems across Applied Intuition’s Vehicle OS portfolio. In this role you will work closely with vehicle software and tooling teams at OEMs and Tier 1s to ensure Applied’s solutions deliver maximum impact in advancing customers’ Software-Defined-Vehicle (SDV) strategies and in-cabin user experiences.

Vehicle OS is Applied Intuition’s software platform for SDV. It enables OEMs to modernize their E/E architecture through three interconnected areas:

 - IVI & in-vehicle infotainment Android Automotive OS (AAOS) based platform, HMI/cluster software, and intelligent in-cabin experiences including Cabin Intelligence (DMS, OMS, voice, occupant interaction).

This role sits at the intersection of all three areas, and the balance will depend on the customer mix.

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Act as the technical bridge between automotive customers and Applied Intuition’s engineering and product teams

 - Support OEMs in adopting Vehicle OS: middleware stack, developer SDK, and IVI/infotainment integration

 - Lead technical discussions, architecture reviews, demos, and early-stage deployments with OEM and Tier 1 engineering teams

 - Help customers adopt Applied’s code-first developer toolchain, onboarding engineering teams onto the SDK, setting up virtual ECU environments, and integrating with customers’ existing CI/CD pipelines

 - Guide OEMs through the design and implementation of service-oriented vehicle architectures and support system integration across ECUs, domain controllers and high-performance compute

 - Work with customers’ IVI and infotainment teams on AAOS integration, Linux-based IVI stack deployment, HMI/cluster software, and Cabin Intelligence features (driver monitoring, occupant monitoring, voice/AI interaction)

 - Collaborate with customers and internal product teams to triage and resolve technical issues

 - Experience with AUTOSAR (Classic or Adaptive) and automotive developer tooling

 - Familiarity with vehicle communication protocols: SOME/IP, DDS, CAN, LIN, or automotive Ethernet

 - Experience with at least one of the following:
 
 - Vehicle software developer toolchain: SDK-based development, virtual ECUs, SIL environments, or CI/CD pipelines for automotive software
 
 - IVI / infotainment platforms: Android Automotive OS (AAOS), Linux-based IVI, HMI/cluster software, or display middleware

 - Execution-driven mindset with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple customer engagements in parallel

 - Experience working directly with customers on complex problems at the intersection of software and vehicle systems

 - Degree in computer science, electrical engineering, or related field

 - Basic / intermediate programming experience in C/C++, Python, or similar

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; German and/or additional European language is a significant plus

NICE TO HAVE:

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative

As an organization, we deliver for our customers by living our values. We operate from a place of humility, take ownership of problems and successes, approach challenges with a growth mindset, and put our customers at the center of everything we do.

About the Role & Team

The U.S. Sales Development team at Amplitude is looking for a Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our dynamic New York or San Francisco office.

At Amplitude, SDRs build pipeline in two ways. You generate opportunities that fuel the business, and you develop into the next generation of Amplitude talent. We invest in this role intentionally: through structured training, close collaboration with senior sellers, and a clear path to growth into roles across the organization. jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

The Consumer team owns the Kraken app experience used by millions of traders and crypto newcomers worldwide, the product that turns someone's first crypto curiosity into a long-term relationship with Kraken. We build the interfaces people actually use to buy, sell, manage their portfolio, and interact with their assets. Our stack is React on web and React Native on mobile, and we ship fast, measure everything, and iterate based on real user behaviour. We work agile, globally distributed, and we care as much about why we build something as how we build it.

We're looking for a world-class Senior Frontend Engineer to join our product-minded engineering team: we care about customer problems, measurable outcomes, frontend craft, and fast iteration. We work across web and mobile surfaces, partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Platform teams, and use experimentation, observability, and user behaviour to guide what we build next.

 - Drive A/B testing and experimentation strategies forming hypotheses, designing experiments, analysing results, and iterating based on data.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Data, and Mobile engineers to create coherent experiences across Kraken’s consumer surfaces.

 - Make opinionated technical decisions on framework and architecture choices (we want engineers who have strong views on things like TanStack Router vs Next.js App Router and can back them up with real experience).

 - Set the standard for high-quality code — functional correctness, accessibility, performance, and testability are non-negotiables.

 - Mentor engineers across seniority levels and contribute to a culture of craft and continuous improvement.

 - Lead and collaborate on complex cross-platform initiatives, driving alignment across web and mobile surfaces.

 - Deep expertise in TypeScript and the React ecosystem, you have opinions about state management, data fetching patterns, and component architecture, and you can articulate the trade-offs.

 - Production experience with React Native and cross-platform mobile development, including App Store and Google Play release pipelines.

 - Experience with Next.js — specifically familiarity with App Router, React Server Components, and the client/server boundary decisions that come with them.

 - Hands-on experience with A/B testing, feature flags, and experimentation frameworks (LaunchDarkly, Optimizely, or similar).

 - Experience with WebSockets or Server-Sent Events for real-time UI updates.

 - Strong testing culture Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright or Cypress, and the judgement to know when to use each.

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. jobs.title: People & Operation Manager
jobs.description:
ZeitMind, the autonomous data engineer for the European mid-market

About Zeit AI

In the coming years, companies will replace their internal data teams with AI agents to run more efficiently. We will be the solution they'll use. ZeitMind connects to the systems companies already run (ERP, CRM, spreadsheets, internal databases), cleans messy data, runs analyses on its own and builds data applications. Every employee can then work with data in plain language, with no technical degree and no help from IT. Our customers use it to organise agricultural inventories, to schedule maintenance, crew and flights for jet operators, and to replace controllers' manual Excel reports.. Founded by Marvin and Leopold, both ex-Palantir. YC S24, backed by Oxford Seed Fund and Sequoia Scout. Customers in manufacturing, agriculture and aviation. Zero to €1M ARR in our first twelve months with six people. Small team, one room in Munich, regular team offsites.

What This Role Is

At our size, every hire shapes the company, and the team we build over the next year will decide how far ZeitMind goes. That's why this role matters so much to us.

As our first People hire, you own how people join and grow at Zeit AI, from a candidate's first touchpoint to their first months on the team. You make hiring fast, personal and professional. You keep us compliant across Germany and the UK, and you build the People foundations we'll rely on at 20, 50 and 100 people. You work directly with Marvin and Leopold, shape the function from day one, and help make Zeit AI a place great people want to join and stay.

Your Daily Business - no two days are alike

 - Recruiting in Ashby, end to end: job postings, sourcing support, screening, scheduling interviews, collecting feedback and following up with candidates. No candidate waits a week for an answer

 - Comfortable hiring for both technical and non-technical roles. You can run a process for a senior engineer as confidently as for a sales or ops hire, and you know what good looks like in each

 - Offers and contracts: you prepare offer slides that make candidates excited to say yes, and you draft and manage employment contracts through to signature

 - Candidate experience: every applicant, hired or not, leaves with a good impression of Zeit AI. You own interview guides, scorecards and the debrief rhythm with the hiring team

 - Onboarding: contracts, equipment, accounts and a first week that never feels improvised

 - Payroll and benefits: you run payroll with Project B, handle benefits and insurance, and keep finance up to date on headcount and people costs

 - HR systems and data: you own our People tools and keep employee records accurate and secure. You pull the numbers the founders need, such as time-to-hire, pipeline health and headcount plans

 - Compliance: you keep contracts, policies and processes in line with German and UK employment law and know when to bring in external counsel

 - Visa and relocation: you guide international hires through work permits, visas and moving to Munich if needed

 - People processes: you design how we run feedback, performance conversations and the operating rhythm, together with the founders

 - Team and culture: you lead offsites, team events, the office

 - Automation: you find the repetitive work in People Ops and automate it rather than just documenting it

Your Skillset - what you bring to the table

 - 2+ years in People Operations, Recruiting, HR Generalist or Talent roles, ideally at a fast-growing startup or scale-up

 - Hands-on recruiting experience with an ATS. Ashby is a plus, but Greenhouse, Lever, Personio or similar count too

 - Solid working knowledge of German and UK employment law, contracts and payroll processes.

 - Very organised with real attention to detail. Contracts, payroll and candidate follow-ups are exactly where details matter

 - Excellent communication. You handle a senior candidate, a new joiner and a founder in the same afternoon and adjust for each

 - Strong ownership and a bias to action. You build the process when there isn't one yet

 - AI-native: you already use AI tools to work faster, and you're excited to automate People processes

 - German and English fluently

 - Munich, or ready to relocate. This role does not work remotely

What We Offer

 - Full trust, maximum support. Full trust, maximum support. You build the People function from scratch

 - Munich is our hub. In-person by design, and we cover your relocation within Europe

 - Regular team offsites

 - Best tools, zero blockers. Daily lunch allowance, dinner covered in the office, Wellpass

 - €5k referral bonus if we hire someone you refer
