jobs.title: People Tech & Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

THE ROLE

As a People Tech & Analytics Engineer on the People team, you will build the systems, data pipelines, and automations behind how Mistral runs People Operations. Reporting to the People Tech & Analytics Lead, you will turn the roadmap into reality: wiring our HR tech stack together, making data flow reliably between systems, and automating people processes with third-party tools as well as Mistral's own models, agents, and APIs.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who loves building. You will spend most of your time in the systems and the data, deep-diving into problems: connecting HRIS, ATS, payroll, identity, and finance tools, standing up the data layer behind our people metrics, and shipping automations that remove manual work from the People team.

If you are a data engineer or people technology specialist who wants to deliver meaningful automation outcomes at Europe's largest AI company, this is the role for you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations and data pipelines across our HR systems (HRIS, ATS, payroll, identity and finance), run data quality checks, and fix inconsistencies at the source.

 - Implement and evolve the Metabase visualisation layer of our people data lake, build the dashboards and self-serve reporting managers and People partners rely on, and run hands-on analyses of workforce trends, retention and organisational health, supporting the move to conversational insights for leadership.

 - Design, build, test and document automated workflows, mainly with Mistral's own models, agents and APIs, with human review wherever decisions affect people, monitor live automations with alerting, error handling, logging and runbooks, and prototype AI use cases on people processes, productionising the ones that prove their worth.

 - Implement configuration changes across the HR tech stack (workflows, fields, roles and permissions, new countries and entities), support testing and rollout of system changes and integrations, and act as first-line troubleshooter for the People team, leading issue resolution through to production with a clear audit trail.

 - Architect end-to-end HR workflows with key stakeholders in HR Operations, Business Partnering and Reward, and implement data governance in practice: quality standards, access controls, retention rules and audit trails for employee data.

 - Provide clear enablement materials in Notion so the People team and managers can use our systems confidently, with strong tier-1 support via a bot.
 
 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience in data engineering, analytics engineering or HR technology, ideally within an HR or People function or working closely with one as a stakeholder.

 - Strong practical SQL and Python skills: you are comfortable building pipelines and transformations yourself.

 - Hands-on experience with HR systems such as Ashby, and integrating them with ATS, payroll, identity and finance tools via APIs, middleware and data pipelines.

 - Real automation experience: you have built and maintained workflows in n8n or similar tools such as Make, Zapier, Workato or Langdock, and you are excited to do the same with Mistral's own models and tooling.

 - Working experience with data warehousing (Snowflake, BigQuery) and the modern data stack (dbt or similar), and with visualisation tools such as Metabase, Looker, Tableau or Power BI.

 - You are low-ego and team-spirited, and you take a prioritised problem and run with it in ambiguity: you would rather build a first version and iterate than wait for a perfect spec. You start from the HR need, not the technology, stay hands-on, and have a track record of building foundations in growing organisations without creating legacy.

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.

PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
THE ROLE:

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Sift, you will bridge the gap between data science and large-scale distributed systems. You won’t just train models in isolation; you will build end-to-end pipelines that extract signals, train custom models per merchant, and serve predictions at production scale with low latency. You will work on an automated machine learning ecosystem that dynamically recalibrates models based on streaming global telemetry data.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Model Development & Refinement: Design, build, and deploy online machine learning models (including ensemble methods, deep learning, transformer architectures and graph-based models) to catch evolving fraud vectors in real time.

 - Feature Engineering at Scale: Engineer high-frequency time-series features from over 1 trillion behavioral events, optimizing for low-latency signal extraction and pattern recognition.

 - Production MLOps: Maintain and enhance our automated model training and deployment infrastructure, ensuring frictionless continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) of newly trained models.

 - System Optimization: Write high-performance code to minimize scoring latency at runtime, ensuring our core ML services scale seamlessly across distributed databases.

 - Collaborative Innovation: Work cross-functionally with Core Infrastructure, Product Management, and Data Science teams to translate business-level fraud patterns into robust algorithmic solutions.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR (REQUIREMENTS):

 - Experience: 4+ years of professional experience building and deploying large-scale machine learning models into high-traffic production environments.

 - Solid Programming Foundations: Strong proficiency in Java or Scala (for our production backend) as well as Python (for data analysis and model prototyping).

 - Distributed Systems & Big Data: Practical experience with Databricks and big data processing frameworks like Apache Spark, Apache Flink, or Hadoop, and working with NoSQL data stores like Bigtable.

 - Strong Mathematical Foundations: Deep understanding of statistical modeling, probability, and standard machine learning algorithms (e.g., XGBoost, Random Forests, Neural Networks, and Clustering techniques).

 - System Design Mentality: Ability to reason through data consistency, pipeline failures, and performance constraints in a distributed, multi-tenant cloud environment (GCP).

BONUS POINTS (PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS):

 - Experience explicitly in the fraud detection, risk mitigation, or cyber-security domains.

 - Deep knowledge of streaming architectures (e.g., Apache Kafka).

 - Familiarity with containerization and orchestration tools like Docker and Kubernetes.

 - Familiarity with leveraging AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code) to accelerate development and model prototyping

Please note: final stage candidates may be asked to travel for in-person final round interviews.

Global brands rely on Sift to unlock growth and deliver seamless consumer experiences. jobs.title: Founding Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT PROSPER AI

Prosper is building the most advanced conversational AI agents for healthcare: human-like phone agents that handle the administrative work draining the system, including claims status checks, benefit verification, prior authorizations, patient scheduling and balance reminders. Our mission is to eliminate $200B in administrative waste so healthcare professionals can focus more on healing and less on paperwork.

 

Headquartered in New York with an office in Barcelona, we work with dozens of large and enterprise healthcare organizations, and we've raised $30M from top investors including a16z, Base10, YC and Emergence. We're a highly motivated team of 70, ex-MIT, HBS, Bain and Math/CS/Physics olympiad medalists. As we prepare for our next stage of growth, we're looking for ambitious, exceptionally talented people to help scale our team and grow with us.

 

THE ROLE

We're scaling our go-to-market team in New York, and the people we hire there decide how fast we grow. 

As our Recruiter in New York, you'll own hiring with a focus on sales, customer success and revenue operations, and support other teams as we grow, from the first conversation with the hiring manager to the signed offer. 

It's a hands-on role with real ownership. You'll build the pipelines, the interview processes and the relationships with our GTM leaders that let us hire the best people in the market, quickly. 

You'll report to our Head of People and work side by side with our founders, our GTM leaders and our Recruiter in Barcelona. This role is in person in our New York City office.

 
 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run GTM searches end to end: kick-off with the hiring manager, sourcing, screening, interviews, offers and closing

 - Hire across sales, customer success and revenue operations, from SDRs and BDRs to senior account executives

 - Source directly and build pipelines of top performers who aren't looking yet, so most of your hires come from your own outreach

 - Work with GTM leaders to define what each role needs, how we assess it, including role plays and track record, and what a great candidate looks like

 - Close candidates with a clear and honest pitch, including how base, variable and equity work at Prosper

 - Give every candidate a fast and respectful process, working with our Workplace & Culture Manager in New York on scheduling and office visits

 - Keep Ashby up to date and report on pipeline, time to hire and conversion for each search

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years of full-cycle recruiting, mostly for sales and go-to-market roles at a fast-growing tech startup

 - You've hired account executives and SDRs and can walk us through searches you ran from kick-off to signed offer

 - You know how to assess sales talent: quota attainment, deal sizes, sales cycles and how to check them

 - Strong sourcing: you find top performers who aren't looking and get them interested in talking to us

 - You run several searches at once without dropping anything, and hiring managers and candidates never have to chase you for an update

 - You give hiring managers a clear point of view, backed by data, and push back when a process or a profile isn't working

 

Nice to Have:

 

 - Experience hiring for healthcare, health tech or enterprise SaaS sales teams

 - A network in the New York sales and startup community

 - Experience with Ashby or another modern applicant tracking system

 - Spanish

 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - GTM leaders see you as a partner in their searches and trust your read on candidates

 - Most of the people you hire came through your own sourcing

 - The people you hire ramp well and hit their targets

 - Candidates rate our process highly, including the ones we didn't hire

 - Time from kick-off to signed offer goes down, and you can show us the data

 

WHY PROSPER

 - Work on products that are transforming US healthcare operations, at the core of conversational AI

 - Real ownership and impact from day one, alongside a team that has built and scaled a fast-growing Series A company backed by top Silicon Valley investors

 - Significant growth opportunities as the company scales

 - An international team across New York and Barcelona

 - A culture that rewards bold thinking, analytical rigor and tangible results

 - Build the team that takes Prosper to market as we scale in the US

 

INTERVIEWING PROCESS

 1. Initial conversation to understand who you are, what you want to do and where you want to go (30 minutes)

 2. A written exercise at home: how you would run one of our real GTM searches (around 1 hours)

 3. A live session with our Head of People where we go through your exercise and talk about how you work (60 minutes)

 4. Conversation with a co-founder (30 minutes)

 5. Offer stage

 

Prosper AI is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Forward Deployment Engineer
jobs.description:
SingleStore is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to operate at the intersection of solution architecture, technical delivery, and customer partnership. This role combines elements of a solutions architect, technical account manager, and solution engineer, with a strong emphasis on execution. 
 As an FDE, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor and sounding board for customers, helping them design, implement, and scale real-time data solutions using SingleStore. You will work closely with customers to understand their business objectives, translate them into technical strategies, and drive those solutions into production. This role requires a delivery mindset, strong technical depth, and the ability to lead both strategic conversations and hands-on execution. 
 Role and Responsibilities 
 
 Partner directly with customers to understand their architecture, use cases, and business goals, and translate them into scalable technical solutions. 
 Design and implement end-to-end solutions integrating SingleStore into existing application and data ecosystems. 
 Lead whiteboard sessions to shape ideas, define architecture, and convert concepts into technical specifications and execution plans. 
 Act as a proactive thought partner, bringing ideas and guiding conversations rather than reacting to requirements. 
 Own delivery of high-impact initiatives from concept through production, ensuring successful outcomes. 
 Provide hands-on support, including troubleshooting, optimization, and applying pragmatic solutions or fixes when needed. 
 Collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Engineering teams to align customer needs with product capabilities and roadmap. 
 Help customers prioritize and operationalize their data initiatives, balancing ambition with practical delivery. 
 Feed insights from customer engagements back into Product and Engineering to influence roadmap and improvements. 
 
 Your Experience 
 
 10+ years of experience in solution architecture, solution engineering, or technical consulting (pre-sales and/or post-sales). 
 Strong foundation in databases, distributed systems, or software engineering. 
 Proven experience delivering production-grade solutions in customer-facing environments. 
 Experience integrating complex systems across data pipelines, applications, and infrastructure. 
 Ability to translate ambiguous requirements into clear technical plans and drive execution. 
 Experience working with enterprise customers, particularly in financial services or high-tech environments, is highly preferred. 
 Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to guide both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 Demonstrated ability to balance technical innovation with pragmatic delivery and realistic scoping. 
 Alignment with product capabilities and roadmap, ensuring solutions are both impactful and feasible. 
 
 SingleStore delivers the cloud-native database with the speed and scale to power the world’s data-intensive applications. With a distributed SQL database that introduces simplicity to your data architecture by unifying transactions and analytics, SingleStore empowers digital leaders to deliver exceptional, real-time data experiences to their customers. SingleStore is venture-backed and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Sunnyvale, Raleigh, Seattle, Boston, London, Lisbon, Bangalore, Dublin and Kyiv. 
 Consistent with our commitment to diversity & inclusion, we value individuals with the ability to work on diverse teams and with a diverse range of people.

Salary is based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location, and is just one part of our total compensation and benefits package. Certain roles are also eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases and annual bonuses.

 What You Bring

 A proven record of building high-performing new-logo teams and generating outbound pipeline in complex enterprise markets. 
 Strong operating discipline and fluency with activity metrics, pipeline coverage, conversion analysis, forecast inspection, CRM, and reporting. 
 A hands-on coaching approach grounded in call review, discovery inspection, deal inspection, and measurable behavior change. 
 Experience coaching sellers on prospecting, discovery, champion building, executive engagement, business value, and competitive selling.

 Executive presence, sound judgment, high standards, and the ability to balance urgency with trust. 
 Willingness to travel regularly across the Americas for customers, partners, team engagement, and company events. 
 
 How Success Will Be Measured 
 
 Consistent, qualified regional pipeline creation and coverage 
 Improved outreach-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion 
 Strong discovery quality, champion development, and multi-threaded opportunities 
 New-logo attainment, win rate, sales-cycle velocity, and first production workloads 
 Accurate forecasts, clean CRM, timely reporting, and visible activity inspection 
 Seller productivity, coaching impact, retention, and talent development

jobs.title: Perception Engineer, Autonomy (Air Domain)
jobs.description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Perception Engineer, you will help build the perception layer of an autonomy stack for uncrewed air vehicles. The team turns noisy, intermittent data from many sensors and teammates into a reliable picture of the airspace. 

This role spans classical state estimation and tracking, sensor fusion, and learning-based prediction. Increasingly, those models adapt online during an engagement from limited and delayed feedback. The engineer will design and implement real-time C++ algorithms, build the tooling and simulation studies that show whether they work, and carry ideas from research prototypes into deployable software. We need someone fluent in both estimation theory and machine learning, rigorous about measuring results, and comfortable working at the line between research and production.

 

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Develop, integrate, and adapt cutting-edge AI/ML algorithms running on the perception autonomy stack to collect relevant information across a suite of platform sensors

 - Create interfacing software to autonomously control sensors (e.g., EO, IR, acoustics, radar, and RF)

 - Collaborate across the sensor, tracking, and autonomy teams to ensure seamless deployment of heterogeneous platform swarms in on-site DoD testing and demonstration events

 - Deploy containerized solutions to embedded Linux devices, leveraging computer-in-the-loop testing and profiling, and efficiently collecting performance data

 - Interact with the DoD customer to understand their use cases, requirements, and triage needs during field events to deliver a superior customer experience
 

WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - BS/MS in Electrical, Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, plus 3+ years building perception or estimation software for autonomous systems.

 - Strong modern C++ (17/20) for real-time, performance-critical code on Linux. Comfortable with linear algebra libraries (e.g. Eigen) and profiling.

 - Solid grounding in state estimation: Kalman filter variants (EKF/UKF), multiple-model filters (IMM), and covariance and uncertainty handling.

 - Experience with multi-target tracking and sensor fusion: data association, track management, and fusing heterogeneous sensors that report intermittently and with noise.

 - Working knowledge of machine learning for prediction, including sequence models (RNN/LSTM, transformers), training pipelines, and evaluating models on held-out data.

 - Python for data pipelines, analysis and visualization of logged and simulated runs.

 - Experience validating algorithms in simulation and with recorded data: designing experiments, defining metrics, and reading results honestly.

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Vision, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field2+ years of experience in industry.

Security Requirements:

 - Must be a U.S. Citizen

 - Must hold or be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance

For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here https://www.state.gov/securityclearances.

NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with online, real-time learning: models that adapt during operation, not just offline training.

 - Background in adaptive control or learning-based estimation (e.g. concurrent learning, Lyapunov-based learning, Bayesian or recursive least-squares parameter estimation).

 - Experience learning from intermittent, delayed or sparse feedback, where ground truth arrives late or only sometimes.

 - Behavior and intent prediction for other agents, including models of non-cooperative or adversarial actors.

 - Deploying small neural networks in C++ without heavy ML frameworks, under tight latency and compute budgets.

Base salary is a single component of the total compensation package, which may also include equity in the form of options and/or restricted stock units, comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance coverage, 401k retirement benefits with employer match, learning and wellness stipends, and paid time off. Note that benefits are subject to change and may vary based on jurisdiction of employment.

jobs.title: Enterprise Sales Development Representative - London
jobs.description:
BUILDING A MORE RESILIENT WORLD

When things go wrong, insurance has one job: get people and businesses back on their feet. Too often, it doesn't. At ClaimSorted, we're changing that, and building a more resilient world where people and businesses have the confidence to go after bigger opportunities.

We're creating the company that will define how claims are handled for the next generation. The world's largest insurers and Fortune 500 companies already trust us to handle their claims and manage their risk.

And we're moving fast. We grew 10x in the past year, raised one of the largest InsurTech rounds of its kind, and are backed by Y Combinator, Atomico and Eurazeo. We ship, learn and improve every week, never settling for "how it's always been done."

We're just getting started. There's never been a better time to join.

THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Sales Development Representative to join our founding GTM team and create a steady pipeline of qualified leads for our Strategic Account Executives (SAEs). You’ll be the first conversation most of our future customers have with ClaimSorted, finding the right people at the largest insurance and Fortune 500 companies in the world and giving them a reason to listen.

You’ll be measured on two things:

 - Volume: a high level of prospecting across email, LinkedIn, phone and other channels

 - Conversion: a high prospect-to-qualified-meeting rate, so every meeting you hand to an SAE is worth their time
 
 

What you’ll do:

 - Research accounts, identify the right stakeholders, and build targeted lead lists at the largest insurance and Fortune 500 companies

 - Run high-volume outbound across email, LinkedIn, phone and whatever else cuts through with people who get pitched constantly

 - Treat outreach as a structured process, using AI tools to research, personalize and scale your prospecting without losing quality

 - Qualify relentlessly, so every meeting you book is a real opportunity and not noise

 - Own top-of-funnel end to end, from first touch to a booked, qualified meeting handed to an SAE

 - Refine our outbound messaging as you go, feeding what you learn from hundreds of conversations back into how we message and target

 - Work directly with Claims and Product, so what you hear from prospects shapes how we position what we build next

We love working together in the office, so this is a full-time, in-office role in our London office. We’re a high-intensity team and often put in significant time and effort, because we believe great outcomes come from doing the work well.

WHO YOU ARE

You have at least a year in a communications-heavy role, ideally in sales or something adjacent (SDR/BDR, recruiting, customer success, account management or similar), and you’re ready to step up into a high-growth enterprise sales environment.

 - Great written and spoken communicator: you can get a stranger to reply to a cold email or pick up the phone, and you keep sharpening your messaging when the data says it isn’t landing

 - A sharp researcher: you can quickly work out who the relevant people are at a large organization and what would make them care

 - AI-fluent: you use AI tools to do better prospecting, and you treat outreach as a structured, repeatable process rather than ad hoc effort

 - Built for volume: you stay sharp and motivated through a lot of “no” on the way to “yes”

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
SingleStore is looking for an accomplished sales professional to join our Sales Team. AI is moving from experimentation into production, and this role is an opportunity to break into AI while doing meaningful enterprise selling. 
 As an Account Executive, AI Hunter, your job is simple: create new SingleStore customers. You will find companies building AI applications where data access, real-time context, memory, retrieval, or operational scale is becoming a constraint—and turn those challenges into new SingleStore customers. You will own a broad territory, build a majority self-sourced pipeline, create demand in an emerging category, and close greenfield enterprise opportunities. 
 This is a true hunting role. You will engage customers before they have a defined project, develop customer-specific points of view, create urgency around business and technical problems, work with technical experts to land first production workloads, and build a measurable new-logo business with broad ownership. The ideal candidate is a measurable enterprise hunter who is competitive, curious, technically credible, resilient, and able to sell business outcomes. Direct AI sales experience is valuable, but proven selling ability and technical curiosity matter more than a narrow “AI seller” title. 
 Role and Responsibilities 
 
 Build and execute a territory strategy for net-new customer acquisition. 
 Prospect fearlessly across a broad account universe using proactive, persistent outbound, account-based, partner, and market-education motions; stay resilient and effective through rejection and ambiguity. 
 Form account hypotheses, map the buying center, and earn first meetings with relevant points of view tailored to the customer. 
 Engage executive, business, technical, security, and procurement stakeholders. 
 Lead great business-first discovery, connect AI and data challenges to fundable goals, and build quantified ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases. 
 Build and develop champions, multi-thread the buying group, earn executive and economic-buyer access, and maintain stakeholder alignment; own the stakeholder plan, mutual action plan, close plan, value case, stage gates, forecast, and commercial outcome. 
 Lead complex sales cycles through technical validation, security, legal, procurement, negotiation, and close. 
 Partner with Solutions and Forward Deployment Engineers and cross-functional teams to validate technical fit and establish the first production workload. 
 Navigate competitive displacement and maintain disciplined activity management, CRM hygiene, reporting, qualification, forecasting, and opportunity management; showcase clear metrics such as pipeline created, meetings, conversion, quota attainment, and new-logo performance. 
 Be AI fluent: use AI and research tools productively and responsibly while applying judgment, validating outputs, and separating facts from hypotheses. 
 Travel within the assigned territory as required. 
 
 Required Skills and Experience 
 
 5+ years of quota-carrying B2B enterprise software sales experience, ideally selling to large or technically sophisticated organizations; experience in data, cloud, analytics, AI, or adjacent technical domains is a plus. 
 Repeated, quantified quota success with clear ownership of new-logo wins and self-sourced pipeline. 
 Experience closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals involving executives, technical evaluators, security, legal, finance, procurement, and partners. 
 Ability to sell measurable business outcomes and build ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases. 
 Technical fluency in an adjacent domain such as databases, data infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML, cloud, Kubernetes, developer tools, cybersecurity, observability, or open-source software. 
 Strong qualification, account planning, forecasting, CRM, negotiation, and deal-management skills. 
 Learning velocity and coachability, demonstrated through specific behavior change after feedback; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to technical and executive audiences. 
 Executive presence, customer trust, resilience, intellectual honesty, and excellent communication skills. 
 B.A., B.S. degree or equivalent in a related field. 
 Experience with Fortune 500 or security-sensitive organizations, cloud ecosystems, open-source or consumption-based products, or emerging categories is preferred.

SingleStore is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company. SingleStore values individuals for their unique skills and experiences, and we’re proud to offer roles in a variety of locations across the United States. Salary is based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location, and is just one part of our total compensation and benefits package. Certain roles are also eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases and annual bonuses. For candidates residing in the EEA, UK, and Switzerland, please see our EEA, UK, and Swiss Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

The Dev Platform team builds the internal platform that Kraken's engineers use to build, ship and run software. Within Dev Platform, the AI Gateway is Kraken's company-wide LLM gateway: a single, governed entry point that gives teams self-service access to leading models from providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, with visibility into usage and cost, configurable budgets and rate limits, and routing across models and providers for efficiency and resilience.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the reliability, availability and performance of the AI Gateway as a production-critical service used across the company, including SLOs, error budgets and on-call practices

 - Design the gateway's resilience: multi-provider routing, failover, retries, rate limiting and graceful degradation when an upstream model provider is slow or unavailable

 - Set the technical direction for gateway architecture, capacity planning and scaling as LLM traffic grows and more workloads move onto the gateway

 - Build observability for LLM traffic, covering latency, errors, token usage and cost, attributed by team and use case

 - Partner with Security, Finance and AI governance stakeholders to put access controls, budgets, audit logging and data-handling requirements into the platform

 - Lead incident response and blameless post-incident reviews, and turn what you learn into lasting reliability improvements

 - Automate operations through infrastructure as code, safe deployments and progressive rollouts

 - Mentor engineers and raise the operating standard across Dev Platform

SKILLS YOU SHOULD HODL

 - Extensive experience in site reliability, infrastructure or platform engineering, with a track record of owning high-traffic, business-critical services in production

 - Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes, a major cloud provider and infrastructure as code (for example Terraform)

 - Strong command of SLOs, observability and incident management, and the judgment to know which reliability work matters most

 - Proficiency in a language such as Rust or Python, and comfort reading and contributing to a production service's codebase

 - Experience with API gateways, reverse proxies or traffic management: load balancing, rate limiting, failover and caching

 - Experience with Consul and Vault for service discovery, configuration and secrets management

 - Working knowledge of authentication and authorization mechanisms for internal platforms and APIs, such as OAuth 2.0/OIDC, JWT, mTLS and API keys, and how to apply them to a multi-tenant service

 - Experience with model evaluations: building or operating eval pipelines to compare models, prompts and agents, and to catch quality regressions before and after rollout

 - Familiarity with coding agents and agent harnesses (for example OpenHands, Claude Code or similar), including running them safely in sandboxed environments for engineering teams

 - Experience with agent memory systems and the databases behind them (vector stores, search, relational and key-value stores), and operating them reliably

 - Staff-level influence: you set direction across teams, write clear design documents and bring others with you

 - Good judgment balancing reliability, cost and developer velocity for internal customers

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience operating LLM gateways or integrating LLM provider APIs at scale (streaming, token-based rate limiting, model routing, caching)

 - Experience designing, developing and maintaining Kubernetes controllers and operators (for example with controller-runtime or kubebuilder), including CRDs, reconciliation loops and safe upgrades

 - Experience with cost attribution, budgeting or FinOps for usage-based services

 - Background in security-sensitive or regulated environments such as financial services or crypto

 - Contributions to open-source gateway, proxy or observability projects

jobs.title: Founding BDR
jobs.description:
Interfere is building the self-healing layer of the internet: software that detects broken product experiences, understands what caused them, and helps teams fix them before users notice.

Modern teams have logs, dashboards, traces, and session replay. They still find out about too many problems from their users. We exist to close that gap for engineers, PMs, designers, and founders who care how their product actually works in the real world.

The product surface is large. The category is still being defined. The people who join now will help shape how the company grows.

We've raised $5.1M from Y Combinator, Vercel Ventures, Hummingbird, Designer Fund, and others. We're in person in New York City.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're hiring our founding BDR to build outbound at Interfere from the ground up. You'll be our first dedicated outbound hire, with real ownership over how we generate pipeline, what we test, and how we build a function that can scale well beyond one person.

This is a hands-on role. You'll spend your days researching accounts, prospecting, writing outreach, following up, and booking meetings. You'll work directly with our Head of Strategy and Growth, with significant autonomy over how you operate. We want someone who brings ideas, moves quickly, and takes responsibility for making outbound better every week.

The systems you build and the lessons you learn will shape how we hire and scale the team from here. You'll get exposure to the full sales process, see how deals get done, and have the opportunity to take on significantly more responsibility as Interfere grows. For someone genuinely ambitious and early in their career, there's a lot of room to run.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Generate pipeline. Research target companies, identify decision-makers, build prospect lists, write outreach, run campaigns across email, LinkedIn, phone, socials, and other channels, and consistently generate qualified meetings.

 - Figure out what works. Test targeting, messaging and channels, track what's converting, and iterate quickly. Double down on what works and change what doesn't.

 - Build the outbound function. Develop the sequences, workflows, prospecting processes, reporting and systems needed to make outbound repeatable. Use AI and automation wherever they can meaningfully improve our output.

 - Understand our customers. Learn Interfere's product and the problems we're solving. Understand what matters to CTOs and engineering leaders, and use that understanding to make outreach more relevant and effective.

We expect you to bring proven experience, learn fast, take ownership, and continuously improve how we operate. We're not looking for someone who needs a playbook - we're looking for someone who can help build one.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for someone who's already proven they can succeed as a BDR and is ready for significantly more ownership.

 - You know how to generate pipeline. Ideally 1–3 years in an outbound-focused BDR/SDR role at a B2B SaaS company, preferably selling developer tools or into engineering teams. You have a proven track record of generating qualified pipeline, know what good looks like, and can hit the ground running.

 - Sharp, personable, and commercially aware. You can get your head around a technical product quickly, communicate clearly, and hold credible conversations with senior engineering leaders. Strong judgment matters as much as raw intelligence.

 - You want more than another BDR job. You're willing to put in the repetitive work, handle rejection, and keep pushing when things aren't working. You're competitive, genuinely ambitious, driven to deliver results, and motivated to progress quickly in your career.

 - You figure things out. You don't wait to be told what to do every day. When something isn't working, you identify the problem, try alternatives and learn from the results. You're comfortable operating without a fully established playbook.

 - You want to build something that lasts. You care about building better processes, improving conversion, and finding ways to make the operation more effective. If something works, you want to understand why and figure out how to repeat it.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - $80,000–$90,000 base salary + $30,000 target commission ($110,000–$120,000 OTE)

 - Equity compensation

 - Direct exposure to leadership and the full sales process

 - Significant ownership over how our outbound function is built and operated

 - Opportunity for accelerated career progression and increasing responsibility as Interfere grows

You'll be joining early, doing real work from day one, and helping build a function that could become a major part of how Interfere grows.

If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

When things go wrong, insurance has one job: get people and businesses back on their feet. Too often, it doesn't. At ClaimSorted, we're changing that, and building a more resilient world where people and businesses have the confidence to go after bigger opportunities.

We're creating the company that will define how claims are handled for the next generation. The world's largest insurers and Fortune 500 companies already trust us to handle their claims and manage their risk.

And we're moving fast. We grew 10x in the past year, raised one of the largest InsurTech rounds of its kind, and are backed by Y Combinator, Atomico and Eurazeo. We ship, learn and improve every week, never settling for "how it's always been done."

Success in this role goes well beyond closing deals. You’ll need to deeply understand each customer’s business, challenge their thinking, and work with them to build tailored solutions that fundamentally change how they work.

jobs.title: Talent Acquisition Manager
jobs.description:
At Parallel, we build AI agents that help healthcare organizations automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.

Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost to manual, repetitive administrative tasks. Legacy software hasn't helped: it has made work slower, more complex and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change this. Our technology combines large language models with system-level automation to do real work inside existing hospital tools. No integration, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding and frees up time for medical teams to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024 and already have 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people. We are backed by top-tier investors (Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI), and this is just the beginning.

The future of healthcare isn't just digital, it's automated. Come help us build it!

THE ROLE

CONTEXT

This role is open to support an ambitious hiring goal: growing the team by 50%.

You will join a team of three recruiters, alongside Léa, our Talent Lead, with whom you will work hand in hand. The priority of the role is hiring tech profiles: Senior Fullstack Engineers, Forward Deployed Engineers and AI Engineers.

MISSIONS

Hire the best tech talent

 - Gather hiring needs with Hiring Managers, co-build scorecards, then write and publish job offers.

 - Source active and passive candidates through multiple channels, with a strong focus on headhunting (LinkedIn Recruiter, referrals, events).

 - Assess candidates and run hiring processes end to end in Ashby, through to the offer.

 - Ensure a high-quality candidate experience at every step.

Support Hiring Managers

 - Be their point of contact and help them define their team strategy through hiring.

Contribute to the recruiting team

 - Contribute, alongside Léa, to improving our hiring processes and our employer brand.

In your first months, you will have made your first hires and improved time to offer through your continuous improvement proposals.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 2 to 4 years of recruiting experience.

 - You have solid sourcing experience, especially for tech profiles, ideally gained at a SaaS company with a strong technical component.

 - In-house recruiting experience is a plus.

 - You have a sales mindset and the drive to win.

 - You are very rigorous, including in writing.

 - Ideally, you have a good level of English.

OUR VALUES

 - Play to Win: we're not here to just take part, deliver something "good enough" or simply enjoy the startup ride. We want to win. That means caring about results, moving fast and bringing the right intensity when it matters.

 - High Trust, High Standards: trust is our starting point. If you join us, it's because we believe you can own your scope and make good decisions. We don't want a company built on approvals, control and micromanagement. But trust comes with accountability: the more freedom you have, the higher the bar.

 - Low Ego, Hands-On: at Parallel, no one is above the work. No title, seniority or past success exempts anyone from getting involved in the actual work. Leading means taking responsibility, not distancing yourself from execution.

 - Don't Take Yourself Too Seriously: we take our mission very seriously, not ourselves. Building a company is intense. We want Parallel to remain a place where people enjoy spending time together, laughing, celebrating and giving energy to others. High standards and a good atmosphere aren't opposites: we want both.

HIRING PROCESS

 1. Call with Léa, Talent Lead (30 min)

 2. Interviews at our Paris office with Chris and Paul, the founders (2 hours)

 3. Reference checks

WHY JOIN US?

 - Real impact: every hire directly contributes to Parallel's growth.

 - A structuring role: you help build our hiring processes and employer brand.

 - Real traction: seed and Series A ($20M with Index Ventures) closed in less than a year, 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people.

 - Strong investors and founders: Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI; founders who come from Meta, McKinsey and Hublo.

 - A complete package: competitive salary and equity (BSPCE), Alan health insurance, Swile meal vouchers, Apple equipment, 50% of public transport covered.

 - A close-knit team: a team event every month and two offsites a year.

 - Our office: Paris 2nd arrondissement.

 - Flexibility: on average one day of remote work per week and one week of remote work per year.

 
 
 

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.
If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

jobs.title: Founding Research Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAINDROP

Raindrop http://raindrop.ai/ is the monitoring platform for AI agents. Engineering teams at Fortune 100s and the fastest-growing AI companies (Vercel, Speak, Clay) use it to catch silent failures in production. When an agent misbehaves, Raindrop alerts the team, links to the trace, and surfaces the root cause so they can fix it fast. With Raindrop 2.0 (Self-Healing Agents) https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/introducing-raindrop-2/, the loop closes itself: your coding agent fixes it, and the fix becomes an eval to prevent regressions.

WHY IT MATTERS

AI agents fail constantly in ways both hilarious and terrifying. Regular software throws exceptions. But AI agents fail silently, leaving engineers with almost no visibility into how their agents are actually performing.

The current status quo is sifting through millions of logs and trying to debug flaky evals that just aren't matching real world results. Evals are like unit tests, they confirm your model got specific test cases right. But in the real world agents call thousands of tools, run for hours, and encounter millions of unpredictable actions.

That’s where Raindrop comes in. It learns the unique shape of each AI agent’s issues. Starting from presets like Laziness, Forgetting, or Task Failure, to automatically tuning itself to each agent and discovering unknown unknowns.

With one click of a button, AI engineers start tracking issues or topics across 100% of their production data. They can see frequency over time, how many users are affected, relevant properties and more.

In order to process hundreds of millions of events, we gradually train small, custom models, private to each company, that learn to uniquely understand how their product is used.

As part of the early team, you’ll play a fundamental role in shaping the company - from making strategy and product decisions, to helping scale the team, to shaping the future of AI agents.

OUR INVESTORS

We've raised $50M total https://www.raindrop.ai/blog/series-a/, led by CRV, with backing from Lightspeed, Figma Ventures, Vercel Ventures, and the founders of Replit (Amjad Masad, Michele Catasta), Cognition (Walden Yan), Framer (Koen Bok, Jorn van Dijk), Speak (Andrew Hsu), and Notion (Akshay Kothari).

About the role:

We’re looking for a founding Research Engineer to study how AI agents behave in production. You’ll join an early team, set the research agenda, and publish what we learn.

Your Focus:

 - Agent behavior: Discover how agents fail and respond to different conditions in the real world, and what that means for monitoring and safety.

 - Simulations: Advance how we simulate agents and the situations they face before they reach users.

 - Detection: Develop new methods for finding issues no one has defined yet.

 - Open questions: High-upside bets on questions about agents we haven’t thought to ask yet.

Your responsibilities:

 - Set Raindrop’s research agenda and run the experiments behind it.

 - Design evaluations and metrics for problems where the ground truth is unclear.

 - Publish findings as papers, blog posts, and talks.

 - Prototype new methods, and bring the ones that work into the product when it makes sense.

 - Help define what research looks like at Raindrop as the team and product grows.

Ideal Candidate:

 - You make complex ideas clear through strong written and communication skills.

 - Care about sharing your research through publications, open-source work, or public write-ups.

 - Deep expertise in an area such as interpretability, evals, AI safety, anomaly detection, or representation learning.

 - Good judgment about which experiments are worth running and when a result is real.

 - You ship experiments and build prototypes 

 - Use and build AI agents and tools

Job Summary

Etched is seeking a Test Infrastructure Engineer to build and run the infrastructure behind factory testing of our AI systems, from new product introduction through mass production.

You will join a new, small central team that owns making factory testing reliable, repeatable, and scalable. A factory test floor looks a lot like a small datacenter: hundreds of boards, servers, and racks under test at once, all running our test software and reporting results back. You will own that layer: the systems that provision and run test stations, move test results and logs into one reliable source of truth, and roll out new test software safely across factories. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, software, and production teams, and with our contract manufacturing partners.

Key Responsibilities

 - Provision and manage the Linux fleet on the factory floor: OS imaging and network boot, configuration management, and lifecycle automation for test stations and systems under test.

 - Design and maintain the networking that test stations and racks depend on, working with factory partners on site.

 - Build data pipelines that reliably capture every test run, its logs, and hardware genealogy into a central view of test history, yield, throughput, and unit history.

 - Own versioned release, canary, and rollback of factory test packages so new test software reaches production safely and traceably.

 - Build monitoring and alerting across factory infrastructure, and lead debugging when infrastructure issues block production.

 - Integrate with contract manufacturers' factory systems (MES/SFIS) and with shared internal data platforms.

You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)

 - Strong Linux administration skills: boot process, package management, systemd, storage, and debugging from the command line.

 - Solid networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, VPNs, and how networks are laid out in server rooms or datacenters.

 - Experience with distributed systems: services that run across many machines and keep working when some of them fail.

 - Strong coding skills in Python, C++, or Rust. You build real tools and services, not only configuration.

 - Willingness to work onsite in San Jose or Taiwan and travel to manufacturing partners as needed.

Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)

 - Bare-metal server fleets, lab or datacenter automation, or HPC clusters (e.g. PXE, Slurm).

 - Server management interfaces such as BMC, IPMI, or Redfish.

 - Manufacturing test infrastructure, test automation platforms, or factory software (MES, SFIS).

 - AI servers, GPU or accelerator systems, or other high-performance compute platforms.

 - Working with contract manufacturers; Mandarin is a plus for Taiwan-based candidates.

 - Bringing first-generation hardware into production at a fast-paced startup.

Benefits

How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Research Engineer at Mercor, you’ll work at the intersection of engineering and applied AI research. You’ll own benchmarking pipelines, evaluation systems, and failure analysis workflows that directly inform how we train and improve frontier language models.
Your work will define how we measure tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. You’ll design and run evals, build rubrics and scorers, and turn failure analysis into actionable improvements for post-training, RLVR, and data pipelines.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Failure analysis: Run systematic failure analysis on model outputs (e.g., wrong tool use, reasoning errors, safety/alignment issues); categorize failure modes, quantify prevalence, and feed findings into reward design, data curation, and benchmark design.

 - Rubrics and evaluators: Create and refine rubrics, automated evaluators, and scoring frameworks that drive training and evaluation decisions; balance rigor with scalability (human vs. model-as-judge, calibration, agreement).

 - Data quality and usability: Quantify data usability, quality, and impact on key benchmarks; use evals and failure analysis to guide data generation, augmentation, and curation.

 - Cross-team collaboration: Work with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and data producers to align evals with training objectives and to prioritize benchmarks and failure analyses that matter most.

 - Ownership in a fast-paced environment: Operate in a high-iteration research setting with strong ownership of benchmarks, evals, and failure-analysis workflows.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and backend systems.

 - Excitement to work in person in San Francisco five days a week in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

jobs.description:
About us

We’re a fast-growing fintech on a mission to redefine how Latin America manages its finances and this is your opportunity to be a crucial part of that transformation. Join a team of top talent from the world’s leading fintech and tech companies, and help build a cross-border financial system that’s modern, accessible, and built to scale.

Who we’re looking for

We are looking for a Chief Compliance Officer to lead ARQ’s US investment compliance functions, serve as CCO for our SEC-registered investment adviser, and act as the proposed CCO for our introducing broker-dealer through its FINRA New Member Application (NMA) and launch. You will bring prior CCO experience across both SEC-registered RIAs and FINRA broker-dealers, with a strong understanding of digital investment platforms and clearing broker relationships.

This is a hands-on role. You will oversee the RIA’s compliance program, help lead the broker-dealer application, and build the supervisory framework for launch. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, the BSA/AML Officer, and the outsourced FINOP to embed effective controls in ARQ’s investment offering.

What you’ll do:

 1. RIA program ownership: Administer the RIA’s compliance policies, risk assessment, monitoring, testing, and documented annual review. Maintain the compliance calendar and report material risks and remediation progress to leadership.

 2. FINRA application and launch: Help lead the NMA with FINRA, counsel, and internal teams. Develop written supervisory procedures, prepare supporting materials, respond to information requests, participate in the membership interview, and verify compliance readiness before launch.

 3. Broker dealer supervision: Build and lead the compliance and supervisory framework for a fully disclosed introducing broker offering self-directed trading. Establish assigned supervisory responsibilities, account and transaction reviews, supervisory testing, escalation processes, and required annual reporting.

 4. Digital investment advice: Oversee compliance controls for automated, non-discretionary recommendations, including client questionnaires, risk profiles, portfolio methodology, algorithm testing, change management, and ongoing monitoring. Maintain clear disclosures and separation between advisory recommendations and independent customer trading.

 5. Marketing and communications: Review investment marketing, performance presentations, promotions, app content, and customer communications against applicable SEC and FINRA standards. Maintain approval records and electronic communications supervision.

 6. Disclosures and registrations: Manage Form ADV, Form CRS, Form BD, relevant amendments, and client delivery obligations. Coordinate individual registrations, continuing education, advisory agreements, and customer disclosures.

 7. Conflicts and conduct: Maintain the code of ethics and controls for personal trading, outside business activities, gifts and entertainment, and affiliate conflicts. Oversee fiduciary-duty controls and assess custody implications, fees, and collateral arrangements.

 8. Clearing and brokerage operations: Oversee compliance with introducing and clearing responsibilities, including account opening, order handling, applicable best execution obligations, transfers, and customer complaints. Coordinate with the clearing broker and outsourced FINOP on operational controls and regulatory obligations.

 9. Records and customer protection: Maintain compliant books and records, communications retention, privacy and safeguarding controls, and complaint handling. Work with Security and Engineering on incident response and customer notification processes.

 10. Examinations and coordination: Lead SEC and FINRA examinations and inquiries, coordinate audits and remediation, and train employees. Partner with the BSA/AML Officer on investment-related financial crime risks and clearly document responsibilities across teams.

What you’ll need to succeed

 - 10+ years of progressive securities compliance experience, with prior service as CCO for an SEC-registered investment adviser or FINRA broker-dealer.

 - FINRA Series 24 qualification required.

 - Direct experience supporting or leading a FINRA NMA, including supervisory procedures, regulatory responses, membership interviews, and preparation for launch.

 - Strong knowledge of the Investment Advisers Act, Securities Exchange Act, SEC adviser requirements, and FINRA rules covering supervision, communications, records, registrations, and customer protection.

 - Experience with fully disclosed introducing broker-dealers and clearing firms, including the division of compliance and operational responsibilities.

 - Hands-on experience administering RIA annual reviews, marketing reviews, conflicts controls, codes of ethics, regulatory filings, and examinations.

 - Experience with digital investment platforms, automated advice, and self-directed brokerage, including translating requirements into product and technology controls.

 - Ability to coordinate effectively with a dedicated BSA/AML Officer and outsourced FINOP while maintaining clear ownership of the securities compliance program.

 - Sound judgment, strong writing, and the confidence to engage regulators, challenge decisions, and explain practical solutions to senior leadership and technical teams.

Why join us?

 - Competitive salary and equity - you share in our success

 - Hybrid working role

 - Flexible PTO and a “trust-first” culture

 - Sign-on equity bonus

 - Access to the latest tech and a modern tool stack

 - Work with a high-calibre team building the future of finance across LATAM

Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

ABOUT THE ROLE

Applied Intuition's Digital Proving Grounds (DPGs) give the Department of War a vendor-neutral place to test autonomous systems from many companies together, against a real mission, before they reach the field. A DPG covers the full path from software-in-the-loop (SIL) simulation to hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), live-virtual-constructive (LVC), and live exercises. Teams find integration problems in simulation, where fixes take hours, instead of at a live event, where they take weeks.

DPGs run on Axion, Applied's defense toolchain, with Axion Sim at the core. Applied ran VREX for the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, a DPG that put air, surface, and undersea vehicles from different vendors on one mission. CDAO then selected Applied to build the platform for Autonomy Factory, which brings this approach to programs across the Department of War on autonomy.mil http://autonomy.mil.

The technology works in programs. The next step is a product that program offices, test organizations, and mission engineers choose, adopt, and come back to, without Applied engineers supporting events. As the Product Manager for Digital Proving Grounds, you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and requirements for DPGs and Axion Sim. This is an individual-contributor role. You will work as the product peer to the engineering lead for Axion Sim and drive outcomes through influence across engineering, design, business development, and delivery.

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL

 - Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for DPGs and Axion Sim. Decide what becomes repeatable product and what stays program-specific work.

 - Find product-market fit. Run discovery with program offices, test and evaluation organizations, mission engineers, and autonomy vendors. Learn who buys, what they need to prove, and what brings them back for the next event. Work with business development and capture to turn what you learn into offers that win programs.

 - Define the sim-to-live workflow. Shape how a team goes from a mission and its concept of operations to test scenarios, then to SIL at scale, HIL rig checkout, LVC, and live events, with results that carry across each stage.

 - Set the simulation roadmap with engineering. Make the calls on fidelity versus speed, sensor and communications modeling, scale to hundreds or thousands of agents, co-simulation with government tools, and a self-serve experience in the cloud and on accredited networks.

 - Build on shared platform components. Work with other Axion product leads so DPGs use common pieces (simulation, campaigns, metrics, jobs) instead of separate versions.

 - Write clear requirements and define success metrics. Make the scope trade-offs that keep engineering on the work that matters most for upcoming programs and events.

 - Shape the experience with design. Partner with design on the tools that test planners, vendors, and government evaluators use every day.

 - Represent the product. Communicate strategy, status, risk, and trade-offs to Applied leadership and to customers. Present at test events, program reviews, and industry events. Expect to travel about 25% of the time to customer sites, test ranges, and events.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - A bachelor's degree in a technical field (Computer Science, Engineering, or related) or equivalent experience.

 - 8+ years of product management experience shipping complex technical products, including end-to-end ownership of a simulation, test, or engineering platform used by technical teams.

 - Deep technical fluency in simulation. You can discuss fidelity, sensor models, determinism, distributed sim at scale, and HIL with engineers, and you know when a sim result is good enough to trust.

 - Strong customer research skills. You have learned a new domain by talking to users and watching how they work, including users who are hard to reach (regulated industries, cleared environments, field teams). You turned what you learned into a prioritized roadmap.

 - A track record of taking a technical product from custom, per-customer deployments to a repeatable product that customers adopt and renew.

 - Comfort as an IC who owns a whole product and drives cross-functional outcomes through influence, not direct reports.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with engineers and with senior government and industry leaders.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with modeling and simulation standards and government tools, such as DIS, HLA, AFSIM, NGTS, or co-simulation frameworks.

 - Experience planning or running LVC, rang

jobs.description:
FOUNDING MEMBER, GTM & PARTNERSHIPS

New York City · In-person (5 days)

ABOUT ARGON

The next decade belongs to biology. Bio foundation models are turning experimental guesswork into prediction, and the industry built on that science is set to produce more medicine, faster, than at any point in history.

The bottleneck for bringing these medicines to patients will be everything downstream of the science: clinical & regulatory strategy, portfolio decision making, governance reviews, and launch planning. That work is still done by smart people manually assembling context from a hundred sources, and it moves at the speed of headcount.

Argon builds the AI workforce to support all the tasks that happen downstream of discovery. Our work has touched 100s of drugs across oncology, immunology, cardio, infectious diseases, and more with purpose-built AI for biopharma's commercial and clinical teams, specialized from the data model up.

We're an early-stage YC-backed company founded in 2024, working with top-tier pharma and several of the largest life sciences consultancies. We're a small team with outside output, in-person in NYC, and growing quickly, with 7-figure ARR up 7x year-to-date.

Join us if you want to be productive, move fast, and shape the future.

WHY THIS ROLE

We have strong proof-points of Argon from top-20 pharma companies. Our users leverage the platform on a daily-basis, and we’re seeing massive acceleration in our ability to spin up new workflows and complete work end-to-end.

We’ve achieved growth up to now through word of mouth, a strong product, and founder led sales. The Founding Member, GTM & Partnerships will be the first hire dedicated to turning our early traction and strong proof points into a repeatable growth machine.

Initially this role will require you to roll up your sleeves and lead all aspects of GTM: product marketing, top of funnel growth, and complex deal management. With mastery of the process, you’ll build a playbook to hire and build our commercial team.

We are looking for an industry expert with first-hand experience navigating pharma’s portfolio strategy, CI, Market Research and Insights team, and commercial operations

Concretely, you will spend your time:

 - 80% building the commercial function. Hunting net-new partnerships and account growth opportunities and building out the foundation for our next phase of growth. Attending industry events, mapping key accounts, and executing a strategy to bring new deals into the sales funnel and managing them towards a pilot and final close.

 - 20% special projects. Working with the team to think through pricing, new product launches, and running growth experiments. Every week might bring up a new challenge and opportunity, and you’re excited to roll up your sleeves and help us win.

This is a founding role. There is no playbook, no established territory, and no one above you who will know this domain better. You'll write the playbook and help to build this function from the ground up.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 6+ years in biopharma and life sciences sales or partnerships.

 - Deep working knowledge of pharma's budgets and structure with direct experience navigating deals.

 - Experience closing complex multi-stakeholder engagements that span over months.

 - Genuine comfort operating without structure. The most common way this role fails is someone excellent who needs a defined process to work inside.

 - You already use AI tools in your own work and personal life.

 - Clear communicator and organized.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Drive business development efforts including attendance of industry events and leading client conversations for tailored use cases of Argon’s platform.

 - Lead deals from first conversation through pilot and enterprise contracts.

 - Help shape the sales book and materials and constantly invent new ways of providing value to current and potential partners.

jobs.title: IP Rights Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As an IP Rights Manager on the IP & Licensing team, you will own the operational backbone of how Mistral manages rights, obligations, and restrictions across the datasets we license. This role sits at the intersection of copyright, data protection, and AI, and exists because the volume and complexity of our data agreements have outgrown manual processes. You will work closely with the colleagues who negotiate our agreements commercially and legally, translating their work into systems, workflows, and databases that keep us compliant and scalable.

The IP & Licensing team is responsible for all content and data licensing at Mistral. Your work will directly determine whether we can use the data we acquire, how we track what we are allowed to do with it, and whether our clients and partners stay within the rights we grant them. You will build the infrastructure that makes legal analysis repeatable, not just advisory.

Your scope spans the full lifecycle of data-related agreements: clearing inbound data usage requests, codifying contract terms into structured metadata, tracking ongoing compliance obligations, and automating reporting. You will also design and run AI-powered workflows that handle contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and renewal alerts, turning legal judgment into scalable operations.

What You Will Do

 - Clear inbound data usage requests by researching rights status, scope, obligations, and restrictions before data enters Mistral systems.

 - Review data-related agreements and codify their key terms into structured metadata, maintaining the team's template library and playbook alongside Legal.

 - Determine whether specific AI use cases are covered by third-party agreements, identify gaps, and recommend contract amendments.

 - Build and maintain a central database as the single source of truth for every signed data-related agreement, covering permitted uses, confidentiality, and re-use permissions.

 - Track ongoing compliance obligations and automate reporting, including renewal alerts and master licensing partnership administration.

 - Develop and run AI workflows for contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and compliance monitoring.

 - Verify provenance, ownership, and consents for acquired data, flagging obligations that must be tracked.

 - Monitor that Mistral clients and partners operate within granted rights, administering the approval system that enforces legal restrictions.
 
 

What We're Looking For

 - A bachelor's degree in law, publishing, information science, business, or a related field.

 - 2 to 5 years of experience in copyright, permissions, licensing, legal operations, or contract administration, ideally in an AI, tech, or data-driven environment.

 - Solid working knowledge of EU and US copyright law and contract administration, with demonstrated ability to interpret contracts independently.

 - Strong attention to detail and discretion when handling confidential agreements.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain legal constraints to non-lawyers.

 - A legal-ops mindset: you take initiative, anticipate needs through ambiguity, and think about how to operationalize legal analysis at scale.

 - Comfort building agentic AI workflows in a complex enterprise environment; you are an AI power user, not just a consumer.

 - Fluency in French, German, Spanish, or another European language is a plus, as is experience with CLM tools like Ironclad, prior work setting up AI workflows in a legal team, or contracting experience with publishing houses.

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.

PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

You’ll own new business and expansion, partner with Solutions Engineering and Customer Success, and help shape how we sell as the company grows.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own enterprise sales from discovery through close. Build relationships with technical and executive buyers, connect customer needs to a clear business case, and navigate procurement, custom contract terms, and negotiation.

 - Build pipeline through prospecting, account planning, and collaboration with SDRs and Growth. Keep a clear forecast, identify deal risks, and coordinate the next steps needed to move opportunities forward.

YOU’RE PERFECT FOR THIS ROLE IF…

 - You’ve closed complex, six-figure enterprise deals involving technical champions, executive sponsors, procurement, and custom contract terms. You know how to build credibility for an emerging startup and create a compelling reason to buy.

 - You communicate credibly with engineering leaders, understand the software development lifecycle, and enjoy learning how technical products work. Developer-tools sales experience is strongly preferred; adjacent products such as analytics, BI, and infrastructure are also relevant.

 - You’ve succeeded in an early-stage environment with limited support and changing priorities. You can turn an unclear opportunity into a plan, manage your own work, and follow through.

 - You work well across teams and keep complex customer work moving. You bring clear communication, curiosity, sound judgment, and accountability to your relationships with customers and colleagues.

 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience selling automated testing, observability, or infrastructure products.

 - Experience as an early AE at a company with fewer than 100 employees, helping establish an enterprise sales motion.

 - Experience closing expansion deals across additional teams or business units.

 

ABOUT US
