You'll have real autonomy. Many of the day-to-day calls on recruitment, study readiness and customer questions will be yours to make in real time. This role suits someone who wants high ownership and a hand in shaping how the world's largest brands run research with AI.

Note: This role will begin remotely but eventually will be 4 days a week onsite. 

Responsibilities 

 - Consult on study design and content. Review discussion guides, screeners and study setup alongside customers and our research team. Flag risks and recommend improvements before a study goes live.

 - Manage participant recruitment for your customers' studies. Scope feasibility, decide on the right panel partner and approach, manage quotas and timelines, and solve hard-to-reach audience challenges.

 - Build deep relationships and expertise with our panel partners. Work within our centrally managed partnerships to become the go-to person on what works in UK and European markets.

 - Be a trusted advisor to customers' research and insights teams. Help them navigate the platform, troubleshoot issues and get the most out of AI-moderated research.

 - Create best-practice guides and help center content. Collaborate with CSMs on customer workshops and enablement sessions.

 - Act as the team's eyes and ears in the UK. Bring customer insights, market context and feedback back to the broader Outset team, so that product, GTM and operations stay aligned across time zones.

 - Design and improve processes using automation and AI. Streamline our internal workflows, stay on top of new platform capabilities, and work out how to help customers adopt them and do more themselves.

 - Bring commercial awareness to your accounts. Spot expansion opportunities and risk signals early, and partner with Account Directors to act on them.

Qualifications

 - 3–5 years' experience in research operations, market research, fieldwork or panel management, expert networks, consulting, or an adjacent field.

 - Hands-on experience with participant recruitment, ideally across global markets

 - Experience with client-facing work and managing and communicating with external stakeholders

 - The ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy. You make sound decisions without waiting for sign-off, and you know when to escalate.

 - Experience building or improving processes, not just following them.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication. You can adapt your message for audiences from insights leaders to engineers.

 - You pick up complex software quickly and can explain it simply to non-technical users.

 - Strong organisational skills and comfort managing multiple workstreams in parallel.

 - Nice to have: additional European languages.

jobs.title: Thermal Lab Lead
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

Job Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated person to join our team as Thermal Lab Lead where you will help build and maintain a world class thermal lab to support the testing of all the thermal assemblies of our high-performance data center products. You will play a key role in the development lifecycle of Etched products, interfacing with engineers and enabling the testing and validation of cutting edge thermal designs. You will also work closely with lab operations on future lab build outs and deployment of CDUs and liquid cooled racks. You will interface with thermal technicians, plan, and delegate tests to meet aggressive timelines. This position requires very high hands-on ownership, attention to detail, and excellent organizational skills to support continuous high speed growth.

Key responsibilities

 - Lead day-to-day thermal lab operations, including test benches, equipment, and consumables inventory.

 - Develop test plans and procedures in partnership with thermal engineering.

 - Own test setup, instrumentation, execution, data-quality review, and reporting against agreed objectives and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop, maintain, and validate automation tools for test execution, data acquisition, and data reduction and analysis.

 - Coordinate testing requests across multiple teams, establish priorities with stakeholders, and forecast equipment, capacity, and staffing bottlenecks.

 - Lead thermal technicians, assign testing activities, provide technical guidance, and review completed work.

 - Maintain lab procedures and coordinate equipment maintenance, calibration, and safe operating practices with lab operations.

 - Partner with lab operations to plan future lab capabilities, equipment, and infrastructure.

 - Assist with the installation, integration, and commissioning of primary and secondary cooling loops in partnership with facilities, lab operations, equipment vendors, and qualified contractors.

 - Assemble thermal test vehicles, including wiring and soldering of PCBs and heaters.

 - Commission CDUs and liquid-cooled racks to support lab testing.

 - Assist in the design and buildout of Etched thermal labs in Taiwan.

You may be a good fit if you have

 - Relevant technical education—such as an associate’s degree, technical diploma, or bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, mechatronics, instrumentation, or a related field—or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - Hands-on experience testing single-phase liquid-cooled assemblies, including cold plates, manifolds, quick disconnects, and CDUs.

 - Experience selecting, installing, and troubleshooting instrumentation such as flowmeters, thermocouples, and pressure transducers, as well as operating chillers and liquid-cooling test equipment.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently build and troubleshoot test setups, assess measurement quality, and document reliable results.

 - Working knowledge of heat transfer and fluid flow sufficient to interpret test results and troubleshoot thermal-fluid systems.

 - Experience developing, debugging, and validating test automation and data-analysis workflows.

 - Experience coordinating competing testing priorities and providing technical direction to technicians.

 - Excellent organizational and documentation skills.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.

Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
 
 - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification

How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.title: Pre-Sales Engineer (Berlin)
jobs.description:
- Location: Berlin, Germany (On-Site)

 - Contract Type: Full Time

 - Comp Range: 80-120K OTE
 
 

About Kombo

Kombo is the unified API for HR, payroll, Assessment, LMS and recruiting systems. Instead of spending months building integrations one by one, companies integrate once with Kombo and connect to 250+ platforms instantly.

Since Y Combinator (S22), we’ve grown to 8-figures in revenue, 80+ team members, and raised $30M+ from YC, Volition Capital, and Acadian Ventures. 

The Role

We’re hiring our Europe-based Pre-Sales Engineer to own the technical relationship with customers — from first sales call through to successful implementation.

You’ll be the technical expert prospects and customers rely on to understand how Kombo fits their stack, design their integration approach, and get them live. You’ll work closely with our Sales team, and our CRO to close deals and with Product/Engineering to turn customer insights into product improvements.

This is a builder role. You’ll help establish our European solutions team, create repeatable playbooks, and shape how we work with customers.

What You’ll Do

Own the technical sales cycle

 - Lead discovery and demos, translating customer requirements into integration designs

 - Create technical proposals covering architecture, security, and implementation approach

 - Partner with AEs to close complex deals with engineering and executive stakeholders

Drive implementations to go-live

 - Own the technical relationship from POC to signed contract through production deployment

 - Build implementation plans, troubleshoot API issues, and unblock customers directly

 - Serve as the escalation point until customers are live and successful

Build the technical toolkit

 - Create demo environments, code samples (Python, Node.js), and Postman collections

 - Write integration guides, architecture diagrams, and troubleshooting documentation

 - Develop sales collateral: security questionnaire responses to technical one-pagers

Scale the European solutions function

 - Document repeatable playbooks for discovery, scoping, and implementation

 - Feed customer insights to Product/Engineering to shape the roadmap

 - Help define hiring and onboarding as we grow the team
 
 

What We’re Looking For

 - 4+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or technical customer-facing roles at a B2B SaaS company

 - Hands-on experience with APIs — you can read documentation, write sample code, and debug integration issues

 - Track record working complex deals with technical and non-technical stakeholders — consistent deal value of €100k-150k+

 - Strong communication skills: you can whiteboard architecture with engineers and explain value to executives

 - Comfort with ambiguity and building things from scratch
 
 

How We Work

Ownership end-to-end. A customer isn’t “handed off” when the contract is signed — you own the relationship from first technical call through successful go-live and beyond. Problems that surface in implementation are your problems to solve, not someone else’s.

Written thinking. We use long-form documents to make decisions and share context. You’ll write implementation plans, technical briefs, and customer-facing documentation that help the whole team move faster. If you prefer talking through everything in meetings, this isn’t the right fit.

High-performance, high-support. We’re a small team of people who are exceptional at what they do. Ex-founders, and operators who’ve built at scale before. We hold a high bar and give you the autonomy to meet it. We also celebrate wins together (roughly once a week for big releases, closings, or milestones).

Bias Towards Action, and high agency: We are building — if we need a resource, we create it. If a process needs improvement, we refine it. We take the initiative and ownership on everything we own, and don’t wait for permission.

In-person by default. We believe the best work happens together. This role is on-site in our Berlin Mitte office 5 days per week.

Not a Fit If

 - You prefer fully remote work

 - You want a purely post-sales or purely pre-sales role

 - You need extensive structure and hand-holding to be effective

jobs.title: Founding Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
HELP BUILD THE NEXT CATEGORY-DEFINING AI COMPANY

AI has transformed how we write (chat), communicate (voice), and build software (code). The next frontier is even bigger: transforming how businesses actually operate (enterprise wide automation). That's what we're building at Sola.

Sola is an AI-native platform reinventing enterprise process automation and disrupting legacy RPA tools. Our AI agents can execute complex workflows across any application, browser, desktop, or legacy system—free from the limitations and fragility of traditional automation tools. Users simply record their screen, and Sola creates a custom agent to run that process at scale.

The opportunity at hand is enormous. Nearly every enterprise, across every industry, runs on processes that are still painfully manual. We're building the technology to change that. And we're just getting started.

We're hiring a small group of Founding Solutions Engineers to help bring Sola to the world's largest enterprises and build the foundation of our go-to-market organization.

This isn't a role where you inherit a playbook. It's an opportunity to help write one.

 

WHY SOLA? WHY NOW?

 

A MASSIVE MARKET READY FOR REINVENTION.

Enterprise automation is one of the biggest opportunities in AI. Legacy RPA platforms have been constrained by rigid rules, complex implementations, and brittle workflows. Sola is changing that with AI agents that can reason, adapt, and execute work across enterprise systems: the next generation of a massive software category.

 

REAL TRACTION. SERIOUS MOMENTUM.

We've grown the business 10x in 2026, deployed across 20+ enterprise customers—including Fortune 500 companies—and demonstrated rapid expansion, with customers growing 2–5x in their first year. We've closed seven-figure enterprise deals, all with a lean, primarily founder-led sales motion. The product is proven. The market is responding. Now we're building the team to scale it.

 

BUILD ALONGSIDE LEADERS WHO'VE DONE IT BEFORE.

You'll report directly to our CRO, Alex Latraverse, who spent seven years at Flock Safety helping scale the business from $5M to $500M+ ARR and growing the AE organization from two sellers to more than 200.

You'll work closely with Alex and Sola's founders to shape our sales strategy, playbook, culture, and team. This is an opportunity to learn from experienced operators while having a direct voice in how the company grows.

 

EARLY-STAGE OWNERSHIP. EXCEPTIONAL UPSIDE.

Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Conviction, and Y Combinator, Sola has raised more than $20M to build the future of enterprise automation.

We're still early enough that individual contributions can meaningfully influence the company's trajectory. You'll own a largely greenfield opportunity, participate in the equity upside, and shape the organization you could one day help lead.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Founding SE, you'll own the full enterprise sales cycle while helping define how Sola goes to market.

 - Win new enterprise customers. Support AEs in closing complex six and seven-figure opportunities.

 - Land and expand. Help establish new customer relationships, prove value quickly, and grow accounts across business units.

 - Sell transformative technology. Help enterprise leaders reimagine how their organizations operate with AI.

 - Build the playbook. Partner directly with the CRO and founders to refine our positioning, sales process, and go-to-market strategy.

 - Help build the team. Shape the standards, culture, and practices that will define Sola's sales organization.

You'll have the autonomy to operate like an owner, direct access to leadership, and the opportunity to make an outsized impact from day one.

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for exceptional enterprise SEs who combine a track record of winning with the ambition to build something from the ground up.

You'll likely be a strong fit if you have:

 - Approximately 5+ years of Solutions Engineering experience in enterprise SaaS or technology sales, or an equivalent track record of success.

 - A proven ability to work with Account Executives to win net-new enterprise business.

 - Experience navigating complex sales cycles and winning the technical decision for six-seven figure deals.

 - A history of exceeding targets and performing at the top of your team.

 - An entrepreneurial mindset and excitement for the pace, ownership, and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

Experience selling AI, automation, data, security, or software into finance, operations, IT, legal, or risk teams is a plus.

We care more about what you've accomplished and what you're capable of building than where you've worked or how your résumé looks.

 

COMPENSATION

We believe exceptional performance deserves exceptional rewards.

 - Base salary: $157,500-210,000 annually

 - On-target earnings: $225,000-300,000 annually (70% base / 30% variable)

 - Uncapped commissions unlimited earning potential

 - Equity participation as a founding member of our GTM team

On-target earnings reflect base salary plus target variable compensation at 100% quota attainment and are not guaranteed. Actual compensation depends on job-related qualifications and experience. Commissions and bonuses are subject to applicable compensation plans.

 

BENEFITS

We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) matching, daily meals together in the office, flexible PTO (4 weeks per year), and relocation support for candidates not already based in NYC or Atlanta.

 

LET'S BUILD SOMETHING EXCEPTIONAL

The best career decisions come at moments of inflection—when a market is changing, a product is gaining momentum, and a small team has the opportunity to build something much bigger. Sola is now in one of these moments.

If you're an exceptional enterprise SE who wants to help define a category, build alongside experienced leaders, and participate meaningfully in the value you create, we'd love to meet you.

Come help

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
OUR VISION

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10–20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $31M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.

OUR VALUES

We hire and grow everyone against the same four values. Each one comes from a real Vitalize story—interview with us to hear them!

 - 🚗 Push the Car. Step in regardless of role. We help wherever we're needed, own problems end to end, and don't stay in our lane. People can count on us.

 - 🏥 Premier 1K. We show up for our customers, always. Nearly everyone visits a customer site in their first month, and customer feedback informs everything we do.

 - 🗣️ Run Towards the Ugly. Name the ugliest truth first, then propose the fix. Candor over comfort—we call out what's broken, and never get complacent. This shapes our craft.

 - 💡 Think Bigger Fridays. See the gap, fill it—no permission required. Every decision is an experiment: we run it, let the results decide, and drive real impact from day one.

ABOUT VITALIZE'S DESIGN TEAM

Design at Vitalize is grounded in a deep understanding of the people and systems that power healthcare. We spend time in hospitals, learn how work happens from the frontline to the C-suite, and use those insights to design products that make complex operational decisions easier. We care deeply about craft, but we believe great design starts with getting the workflow right—not just the interface. As a small team, we work closely with Product and Engineering, share work early, challenge each other’s thinking, and stay close to the customers using what we build.

THE ROLE

You’ll be the third product designer at Vitalize, joining at a stage where you’ll have significant ownership and room to shape the product. You’ll lead design for complex product areas from early discovery through launch, working alongside product managers and engineers to turn ambiguous problems into clear, intuitive experiences. You’ll design across data-dense and AI-powered workflows, contribute to our growing design system, and help establish a consistently high bar for the experiences we ship as Vitalize scales.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own product design from discovery through launch—partner with Product and Engineering to understand problems, explore solutions, prototype ideas, and ship high-quality experiences

 - Design complex, workflow-heavy product experiences—make data-dense operational tools intuitive for users ranging from central staffing teams and unit managers to frontline clinicians

 - Work directly with customers—visit hospitals, observe real workflows, participate in research, and translate what you learn into better product decisions

 - Bring strong product thinking to the work—question the underlying workflow, identify opportunities beyond the immediate request, and connect design decisions to customer and business outcomes

 - Design thoughtful AI-powered experiences—help determine where AI can meaningfully improve workflows and how its recommendations, reasoning, and actions should appear in the product

 - Contribute to and evolve our design system—create reusable components and patterns, improve consistency across the product, and partner with engineering to ensure designs translate effectively into production

 - Raise the quality of the work around you—participate actively in critique, share thoughtful feedback, and contribute to the practices that help our small design team do its best work

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years of product design experience, ideally designing complex, workflow-heavy B2B SaaS products, with a portfolio demonstrating meaningful ownership from problem definition through shipped product

 - Strong product instincts and design craft—you look beyond the immediate UI, question whether the underlying workflow is right, and turn complicated problems into intuitive experiences

 - A customer- and outcomes-oriented mindset—you’re comfortable observing operational workflows firsthand, translating customer insights into product decisions, and connecting your work to measurable outcomes

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration skills—you form and articulate a point of view, incorporate evidence and feedback, and work through disagreement effectively with product managers and engineers

 - Experience contributing to design systems—you understand reusable components and patterns and care about building consistency and quality into the product as it scales

 - AI fluency—you’ve designed AI-powered experiences or have a strong understanding of how AI changes product interactions, with a thoughtful perspective on where AI should and shouldn’t be part of a workflow

BENEFITS

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Flexible PTO

 - Unlimited travel budget to visit customer sites

 - Twice-yearly company off-sites

 - Free meals in-office

 - $5,000 relocation bonus for eligible employees

 - Desk setup reimbursement

 - Commuter benefits

 - Monthly gym/wellness stipend

 - An awesome office in Jackson Square, steps from the water

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer (Query Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Amplitude is the leading AI analytics platform, helping over 5,200 customers—including Atlassian, Burger King, NBCUniversal, and Square—build better products and digital experiences. With powerful AI Agents embedded across our platform, teams can analyze, test, and optimize user experiences faster than ever. Ranked #1 across multiple categories in G2’s Winter 2026 Report, Amplitude is the best-in-class solution for product, data, and marketing teams. Learn more at amplitude.com http://amplitude.com.

As an organization, we deliver for our customers by living our values. We operate from a place of humility, take ownership of problems and successes, approach challenges with a growth mindset, and put our customers at the center of everything we do.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're entering a world where AI agents don't just assist product teams, they ship features, run experiments, and make prioritization calls autonomously. What makes that possible is agents' ability to verify their work against real product data continuously. Our in-house OLAP engine, Nova, processes trillions of events in real time, turning raw behavioral data into fast, trustworthy answers that power decisions for tens of thousands of agents and product teams worldwide.

That makes Nova the critical infrastructure in the loop, and as non-stop agents become the main source of queries, the demand on Nova's throughput, correctness, and operational rigor grows dramatically.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer who wants to go deep on the engine internals and the infrastructure underneath. You'll own significant components of a modern OLAP system, across query execution, columnar storage, distributed compute, caching, and cloud infrastructure, and drive meaningful improvements to performance, cost-efficiency, and reliability. This role is ideal for someone who finds real satisfaction in making a complex distributed system faster, cheaper, and more reliable — and who wants to do that work on a system that directly powers the product experience for thousands of enterprise customers.

 

THE IMPACT YOU WILL DELIVER

Build the next generation of Nova

 - Own core components across query execution, columnar storage, and distributed compute.

 - Design elastic query infrastructure for AI agents as first-class clients, targeting 10× query throughput with predictable performance and lower cost per query.

 - Solve deep performance problems across engine internals and cloud infrastructure, from JVM and memory optimization to distributed execution.

 - Own production reliability through on-call, incident investigation, and architectural improvements that prepare Nova for its next stage of growth.

Shape what comes next

 - Set technical direction for major initiatives and lead them from proposal through production, with clear milestones and measurable results.

 - Decide what to build, what to adopt, and how to evolve Nova for its next order of magnitude in scale.

 - Work across engineering and product to set priorities and resolve trade-offs between capabilities, complexity, and cost.

 - Help senior engineers take on larger technical problems through design reviews, debugging, and shared ownership.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a systems-minded engineer who:

 - Gets energy from working inside complex distributed systems, finding bottlenecks, and making meaningful improvements.

 - Has built or significantly extended a query engine, storage engine, or distributed data processing system.

 - Makes sound trade-offs across performance, cost, correctness, and reliability, and builds support for technical decisions across teams.

 - Helps engineers take on harder problems through design reviews and debugging, while staying open to new ideas and learning from others.

REQUIREMENTS

 - 8+ years of industry experience in backend or infrastructure engineering, with depth in distributed data systems.

 - Hands-on experience building or extending analytical or OLAP systems: query engines, columnar storage, large-scale data processing or streaming frameworks, or equivalent.

 - Track record of leading multi-month, cross-team technical projects from design through production, including significant cost or performance wins on cloud infrastructure.

 - Strong computer science fundamentals: distributed systems (partitioning, replication, consistency, failover), data structures and algorithms, concurrency, performance optimization.

 - Demonstrated technical influence beyond your immediate team: leading design discussions, driving cross-team alignment, mentoring engineers.

 - Proficiency in Java, C++ or Python.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with query or OLAP systems such as Druid, ClickHouse, Presto/Trino, Spark, BigQuery or Snowflake.

 - Experience with SQL planning and optimization, or with building SQL layers over heterogeneous storage.

 - Familiarity with open table and columnar formats (Iceberg, Parquet, Arrow, ORC) and warehouse-native architectures.

 - Familiarity with product analytics, experimentation platforms, event-driven data systems, or serving data to LLM and agent workloads.

 

OUR VALUES:

At Amplitude, our values guide how we show up for one another and for our customers:

 - Humility: We operate from a place of empathy and openness, seeking to understand many points of view.

 - Ownership: We take the initiative to solve problems that drive our shared company success.

 - Growth Mindset: We’re tenacious in the face of challenges and seek feedback in order to grow ourselves and others.

 - Customer Centricity: We put the customer at the center of everything we do and are deeply committed to their success.

We care about the well-being of our team: We offer competitive pay and benefits packages that reflect our commitment to the health and well-being of our Ampliteers.

Some of our benefit programs include:

 - Excellent M edical, D ental and V ision insurance coverages, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employee Medical, Dental, Vi

jobs.title: Founding GTM Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Our vision is to become the marketplace for everything expensive, specialized, and difficult to move. We’re building the infrastructure that powers the procurement and disposition of assets across America’s essential industries, automating everything from discovery and payments to freight, warranty, and financing. Today, Garage operates in cities and towns across all 50 states and has surpassed $100M+ in annualized transaction volume on the platform.

Our mission is to save local governments and essential services businesses time and money. We started with fire departments two years ago and have since expanded into EMS and heavy-duty, launching new verticals while growing revenue >10x last year.

If you move fast, hold a high bar, and want meaningful ownership in building a category-defining company, Garage is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Founding GTM Recruiter, you will help build the Growth, Marketing, and Ops teams behind Garage’s next stage of growth. You’ll partner closely with the CEO and GTM leaders to identify the people who can help scale a complex, mission-critical marketplace and deliver an experience that customers love.

This is a hands-on role for someone who treats sourcing as a craft. You will own searches end to end, build targeted pipelines from scratch, run a fast and thoughtful process, and help Garage raise the bar with every hire.

 - Own full-cycle hiring across GTM functions, partnering closely with the CEO and hiring managers to attract, assess, and close exceptional talent.

 - Build and execute creative sourcing strategies across outbound, referrals, communities, and networks to develop strong talent pipelines.

 - Track hiring funnel performance and continuously improve recruiting processes using data and insights.

 - Champion Garage’s mission and values in the talent market and deliver an exceptional candidate experience.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Lab & Protein Data
jobs.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll build out the data science layer of Adaptyv's foundry — the work that turns tens of thousands of raw, messy experimental readouts into clean, trustworthy, structured data that our customers, our models, and our own scientists can rely on. Binding (BLI/SPR), developability, biophysical, and functional assays all produce data at scale; your job is to make that data correct, comparable, and useful.

This sits at the intersection of three things: data quality (is this number real, or an artifact?), bioinformatics (linking experimental results back to sequence, structure, and protein design), and dataset building (turning foundry output into the kind of high-quality, benchmarkable data that frontier AI labs actually want). You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the lab scientists who run the assays, the software team who own the pipelines, and the customers who train models on what we produce. This is a hands-on build role, not a management one.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the scientific logic of data quality across the foundry: define what "good data" looks like for each assay type — expected signal ranges, control thresholds, failure modes, edge cases — and turn it into automated checks.

 - Build anomaly detection and QC models that catch bad data the eye would miss: assay drift, instrument variability, plate effects, false passes and false fails — and distinguish real signal from noise statistically.

 - Work with the software and ML teams to specify, review, and improve the automated data pipelines that process instrument outputs, feeding back precise requirements for what to flag, auto-reject, or route to human review.

 - Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other.

 - Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models.

 - Apply real statistical rigor to multi-condition data at scale — thousands of samples across hundreds of simultaneous experiments — and make the results interpretable and comparable across runs.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong data science / bioinformatics background — you're fluent in Python (pandas, numpy, the scientific stack) and comfortable owning messy, real-world experimental data end to end.

 - Genuine biology grounding — you understand proteins, assays, and sequence/structure/function well enough to know what the data means, not just how to process it. You don't need to be a bench scientist, but you can't be biology-blind.

 - Statistical maturity — process control, anomaly detection, handling variability and batch effects; you can tell drift from noise and defend the call.

 - Prolific builder with the receipts to prove it. You've shipped a lot — pipelines, tools, models, datasets — and can point to concrete things you built end to end and put into real use, not prototypes that died in a notebook. You move fast, systematize what works, and have no patience for babysitting a fixed dashboard.

 - AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

 - Interdisciplinary by instinct. You're energized working across the lab bench, software, and ML, and you treat automation and data infrastructure as part of your job.

 - Bonus: experience with protein/sequence-structure data (bioinformatics tooling, structural data), ML on experimental data, or building datasets for model training and benchmarking.

DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP

You are the person who makes sure that does not happen. What is on the shelves, what is on order, what is shipping, and what is about to break — that is yours, and you will run it. This is a hands-on, in-the-lab role, working closely with our Lab Manager and with the scientists whose experiments depend on you getting it right.

This is a good role to be early in your career in. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year and multiplying the throughput of the lab, and the person who does this job well will not be doing the same job in two years. We are looking for someone who fixes things rather than reporting them.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Keep the lab stocked. Receive deliveries, unpack them, get them into the right freezer at the right temperature, and make sure our inventory system reflects what is actually on the shelf. Flag what is running low before anyone else notices.

 - Run the day-to-day ordering. Place the orders, chase the ones that are late, and sort out the ones that arrive wrong.

 - Handle shipping, in and out. Customer samples, reagents, equipment. Cold chain, dry ice, customs paperwork, and the courier relationships that make it all land on time.

 - Support the science team hands-on. Reconstituting and aliquoting target proteins, buffer prep, plate handling, and tracking materials in our lab software. You will be at the bench for part of your week.

 - Look after the instruments. Coordinate servicing, calibration, and repairs with vendors, keep the maintenance schedule honest, and get an engineer on site fast when something breaks.

 - Keep the lab safe and organized. Chemical inventory, waste disposal, safety compliance, and the general war against entropy in a shared space.

 - Keep the office and the team running. Supplies, workspace, new-starter setups, and the occasional team event.

 - Help build the new lab. We are expanding into new space. You will be involved in setting it up.

 - Some hands-on lab experience. A degree, an apprenticeship, a technician role, or a couple of years in a research or biotech lab. We care much more about whether you are competent and reliable in a lab than about how many years you have logged.

 - You notice things before they break. The best people in this role are the ones who spot that we are three weeks from running out of a reagent, and quietly fix it, rather than the ones who report the stockout.

We want someone who has set these systems up before and can do it again here, with their own hands. Phage, ribosome, mRNA, yeast, cell-free: which one fits depends on the library and the target, and part of the job is making that call and then building it rather than writing a recommendation.

This is a build role, not a service role. For your first months you are making libraries, running selections, working out why a round collapsed, and turning what works into something the automation team can run without you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the libraries. Oligo pools, combinatorial assembly, barcoding. More campaigns fail here than at selection.

 - Run selections end to end, including the call on whether a round enriched real binders or just fast growers.

 - Pick the platform per campaign and stand it up. Based on the library and the target, not on what you happened to use last.

 - Own the sequencing analysis. You don't need to be a bioinformatician, but you can't be waiting on one.

 - Hand off to automation. A protocol that only works when you personally run it isn't finished.

 - Close the loop. Selected designs get expressed and measured on BLI and SPR by the team next door. That tells you whether the selection worked.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MSc / PhD in molecular biology, protein engineering, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years running display and selection yourself.

 - You have set up a display platform, not just used one. This is the core requirement. Built the library, got the selection working, and produced binders that held up in an independent assay. Managing outsourced CRO campaigns is not the same thing.

 - Depth in at least one display format and working literacy across the rest. We are not fixed on which one.

 - High-diversity cloning, and an understanding of where bias enters a pool and what it costs you later.

 - NGS as a routine tool, and FACS if you have it.

 - Enough Python or R to analyze your own data without joining a queue.

 - You use AI tools seriously. It's 2026 and we run on Claude Code across the company. You also need the judgment to check what comes back.

 - A self-starter. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue. You decide what to build, build it, and tell us what you learned.

 - Startup speed, not academic pace. Campaigns run against customer deadlines. A working platform with known limits beats an elegant one next year.

 - You want your protocols automated rather than manual forever.

If your instinct is that a campaign is finished once you have ten good clones, we will frustrate each other. We want data, not a hit list.

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

 - Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

 - Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

 - Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

 - Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

 - Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

 - Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our lab is a factory. DNA goes in, characterized proteins come out, and a customer gets results in days rather than the months a CRO would take. Everything that machine consumes — synthesized genes, reagents, consumables, biosensors, catalog proteins — is something we buy, on lead times we do not control. It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. One thing makes it harder than a typical procurement job: our assay portfolio keeps expanding, and every new assay brings new reagents. You are not optimizing a static supply chain, you are building one that flexes with the science. How far the role goes from there is up to you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot.

 - De-risk the supply chain. Too much of what we depend on has exactly one supplier. Find second sources, qualify them properly with the science team, and keep them warm, so that switching is a decision we make rather than an emergency we react to.

 - Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

 - Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

 - Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

 - Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

 - Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after.

 - Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter.

 - Own COGS with Finance. Procurement and finance are the two halves of gross margin, and you are the procurement half.

 - Automate the whole thing. Ordering, tracking, and reconciliation should mostly run themselves.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You have worked in supply chain or procurement in a physical, technical business. Biotech, a CRO, or another life science company is ideal, and you understand reagent categories — enzymes, antibodies, media, resins, plasticware — and how they are actually sourced. Hardware manufacturing or another high-mix production setting translates well. Buying software licences does not. You do not need to have run a supply chain organization before; you do need to be ready to own one.

 - You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up.

 - You are technical enough to talk to scientists. You do not need a degree in biology, but you will be qualifying an alternative supplier for a reagent that a protein biochemist depends on, and you need to be able to have that conversation properly rather than forwarding it.

 - You can negotiate. Comfortable sitting across from vendors who have been selling into labs for thirty years, and comfortable walking away.

 - You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. Some of our largest suppliers still require a human to upload a spreadsheet to a portal, and we consider that a bug rather than a fact of life. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are building the most automated lab in the world, and that does not stop at the bench. A company that AI agents can run experiments in has to automate everything around the experiment too — procurement, hiring, admin, and finance. Finance is one of the most automatable functions in any company and almost nobody has actually done it. We intend to.

That is the job: build an AI-powered finance stack. Our ledger, billing, cards and payroll all expose APIs, and we already close the books against them programmatically rather than by hand. You would take that much further, to where the model, the close, the cash view and the margin analysis largely run themselves, and your week goes on the decisions instead of the reconciliation.

You would be our first finance hire, and it is hands-on. You will build the forecast, run the close across two entities, own cash, and be the person who can say what a protein actually costs us to make.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the forecast. Both directions: bottom-up from lab capacity, throughput and price per protein, and top-down P&L, burn and runway.

 - Own gross margin. What does an experiment actually cost us — DNA, reagents, consumables, instrument time, labour? Which products and which customers lose us money?

 - Own pricing, with commercial. What we charge, why, and where the floor is. Pricing at a lab company is a finance question wearing a sales hat.

 - Own the close. Group consolidation and intercompany management. Make it fast, make it correct, make it boring.

 - Own cash. Bank and card accounts across Switzerland and the US, AP runs, AR collection, payment timing. Know where the money is and where it is going before anyone asks.

 - Keep us compliant. Tax, VAT, audit, payroll, and the external firms we work with. You are not a lawyer or an accountant, but you know when to call one.

 - Investor reporting, fundraising support, and treasury management.

 - Equipment leasing and asset management. The lab runs on millions of francs of instruments. Lease or buy, how we finance it, what it does to the balance sheet, and keeping the asset register honest as we expand.

 - You have built a finance function, not just worked in one. Several years in finance at a startup that actually scaled, and ideally you were early enough to have set things up rather than inherited them.

 - You can build a real model. Not a template. A model that ties operational reality — throughput, yield, capacity, headcount — to cash, and that survives someone pulling on it.

 - You write code, or you are visibly about to. SQL at minimum, Python ideally. This is the hard requirement most finance candidates will fail, and we mean it. We run on Claude Code across the company, and every system finance touches has an API behind it. You’ll be the person who makes sure the work we do translates to cash. Working closely with our Accounts Recievables team and reporting directly to our Head of Revenue Operations, you’ll own the full invoice-to-cash cycle: assembling invoices, delivering them, managing customer-billing relationships, and finding ways to optimize the workflow. 
It’s a core seat in Revenue Operations. You’ll interact with customers every day, work closely with Sales and Operations, and help build the systems we’ll use to scale. This isn’t data entry. Invoice-to-cash, end to end

Whatever finance needs

 - Excellent written and spoken English. Additional European languages are a strong plus.

 

GERMAN LANGUAGE EXPECTATIONS

 - Native-level or full professional fluency in German (written and spoken), with the ability to conduct complex sales conversations and negotiations.

 - Establish and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, work with CSMs to drive upsell opportunities and manage existing accounts ongoing

 - Value having leadership that has tenure and a track record of success

 - Thrive working with A Players as cross-functional partners across GTM

 - Understand the importance of selling a product that is market validated and can deliver on its technical promise

 - Believe there should be no cap to upside and want control of account up-sell potential

 - Are passionate about what Deepgram is building and how we are changing what is possible with speech

IT’S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE

 - Proven experience in a technical full-cycle sales role

 - Experience building your own pipeline from scratch and closing accounts

 - Consistent overachievement against sales targets in past experiences

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills

 - Empathy and a unique ability to understand customer needs

Our Mission

Reflection’s mission is to build open superintelligence and make it accessible to all.

We’re developing open weight foundation models for individuals, agents, enterprises, and even nation states. Our team of AI researchers and company builders come from DeepMind, OpenAI, Google Brain, Meta, Character.AI http://Character.AI, Anthropic and beyond.

Role Overview

As a Strategic Finance Manager, you'll help build the core muscles of our capital allocation, forecasting, and planning processes. You'll work across the business — spanning GTM, compute, R&D, and corporate finance — building models and analyses that inform how we allocate resources, evaluate opportunities, and plan for growth. The work will vary depending on where you focus, but the common thread is connecting ground-level business activity to rigorous financial thinking.

 - Build financial models across a range of contexts — deals and partnerships, product and channel economics, cost structures, and investment decisions

 - Support the corporate financial model with bottoms-up inputs, and maintain that connection as the underlying business evolves

 - Partner cross-functionally — with sales, GTM, engineering, research, and finance leadership — to translate business activity into financial frameworks

 - Develop cost and investment models (compute, infrastructure, headcount, R&D) to inform resource planning and tradeoff decisions

 - Identify financial risks and opportunities early, and help structure decisions that balance growth with returns

 - Improve the templates, assumptions libraries, and processes used across the team

 - 5+ years of experience in strategic finance or FP&A at a high-growth technology company, management consulting, investment banking, or similar

 - Strong financial modeling skills – build clean, auditable models from scratch

 - Experience with deal economics, revenue modeling, or commercial finance at a technology company

 - Comfort with cost-side modeling: you understand how compute, headcount, and infrastructure costs behave

 - Ability to work cross-functionally with sales, GTM, engineering, research, and finance leadership without losing rigor

 - Comfortable with ambiguity: takes initiative, operates independently, and brings structure and curiosity to open-ended problems.

WHAT WE OFFER:

We believe that to make intelligence open and accessible to all, you need to start at the foundation. Joining Reflection means building from the ground up as part of a talent-dense team. You will help define our future as a company, and help define the future of open foundational models.

We want you to do the most impactful work of your career with the confidence that you and the people you care about most are supported.

 - Sponsorship support: We sponsor visas to help exceptional talent join our team and support long-term immigration pathways where applicable.

 - Team building: We have regular off-sites, happy hours, and team celebrations.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

 

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Mechanical Engineer to join our team and help transform complex designs into reliable, high-power data center products. As a Mechanical Engineer at Etched, you will be integral to the development of high-performance data center products, from initial concept through to production. You will collaborate closely with both internal and external design engineers, including JDM (Joint Design Manufacturer) partners. Your expertise in mechanical design, particularly for data center chassis and high-power systems, will ensure our products meet rigorous performance, reliability, and manufacturability standards.

 

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop and refine mechanical designs for high-power data center products, ensuring robust performance and reliability. Manage the transition from appearance models to production-ready designs.

 - Work closely with internal design teams and external partners, including Joint Design Manufacturers (JDMs), to ensure seamless integration of mechanical designs with overall product architecture.

 - Lead the design of data center chassis and enclosures from concept through production, focusing on meeting high power, cooling efficiency, and ruggedness requirements.

 - Oversee and manage the development of both soft and hard tooling to support mass production, ensuring that all tooling meets strict quality and consistency specifications.

 - Ensure that mechanical designs comply with manufacturing requirements, including shock and vibration standards, to guarantee durability and performance in demanding data center environments.

 - Translate industrial design concepts into manufacturable designs, effectively converting appearance models into production-ready mechanical solutions.

 - Apply DFM principles to optimize designs for cost-effective manufacturing, assembly, and maintenance, ensuring high efficiency and reduced production costs.

 

You maybe a good fit if you have

 - A Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field is essential. Advanced degrees or certifications in mechanical design or manufacturing are a plus.

 - A minimum of 10 years of experience in mechanical engineering with a focus on high-power data center products, including a proven track record in designing and managing chassis and enclosures for data centers, is required.

 - Strong expertise in mechanical design and engineering principles is necessary, along with hands-on experience in transforming industrial design concepts into production-ready models.

 - Extensive experience in data center chassis design, with a deep understanding of high-power and cooling requirements, is important.

 - Proficiency in mechanical CAD software and tools such as SolidWorks, Creo, FX, CATIA, or similar is required.

 - A deep understanding of tooling processes, including both soft and hard tooling, and their impact on product design and production, is critical.

 - Familiarity with manufacturing requirements and standards, including shock and vibration testing, is expected to ensure that designs are durable and meet industry expectations.

 - Excellent problem-solving skills and a keen attention to detail are essential to ensure that every aspect of design work is meticulously considered.

 

Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
 
 - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch + dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification

 

How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

 

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

 - Manage our recruiting team and partner with leadership on hiring strategy and process improvements

Astro Mechanica is looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer focused on power electronics and power systems development to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is excited about designing cutting-edge power electronics in high reliability applications and has a proven track record of quickly bringing concepts to life. You will be responsible for the full product life cycle, from initial concept to delivery and operation. WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Develop high-performance, high-density, high-reliability power converters

 - Own system trades, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, layout, bring-up, debugging, manufacturing, and test

 - Support hardware through prototyping, characterization, ground testing and flight

 - Work closely with other engineering disciplines to design, develop and optimize high-power propulsion and generation systems
 
 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - BS, MS, or PhD with focus on power electronics or equivalent

 - 5+ years of experience designing, building, testing, and shipping power converters

 - Ability to develop component and system trade studies through high degrees of ambiguity

 - Experience bringing at least two products through full lifecycle, from concept to production

 - Experience working on high voltage (up to 1000V) and/or high power (>10kW) converters

 - Expertise in various DC-DC and DC-AC power conversion topologies, preferably with high frequency multilevel architectures

 - Intimate understanding of electric machines and motor control methodologies

 - Expertise in optimizing switching power loops to optimize converter performance and minimize EMI

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Head of Tax
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARQ

ARQ is one of the fastest-growing fintechs in the world. Our mission is to redefine how people interact with money across borders, building the infrastructure to move value seamlessly. We're still early in our journey, which means every person who joins shapes the future of our product, culture, and growth. If you're excited by big challenges, global impact, and the chance to grow fast with a world-class team, ARQ is the place to do it.

THE ROLE

In the role of Head of Tax, you will serve as both strategic safeguard and functional architect. Rather than simply overseeing filings, you will architect international tax frameworks that dictate how capital moves across borders, including the US and Latin America. Partnering with Product and Engineering teams, you will embed automated tax calculation and withholding engines into our ecosystem. Managing complex operational scale, you will allow ARQ to expand rapidly while staying fully compliant with evolving tax regulations and transfer pricing rules.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Tax strategy and governance
 
 - Define and own the group’s global tax strategy, aligned with business goals, risk appetite and expansion plans.
 
 - Build and maintain a tax risk management and governance framework, including policies, controls, approval thresholds and documented positions.
 
 - Report regularly on tax matters, exposures and planning opportunities to the CFO, executive team, Board and Audit Committee.
 
 - Monitor legislative and regulatory changes in every jurisdiction where the group operates and assess their impact.

 - Corporate income tax and compliance
 
 - Oversee timely, accurate corporate income tax filings and payments for every entity, whether done in-house or through external advisors.
 
 - Manage the global tax compliance calendar and make sure no deadlines are missed in any jurisdiction.
 
 - Oversee estimated and advance tax payments, withholding tax obligations and tax refund claims.
 
 - Maintain an up-to-date entity register with each entity’s tax registrations, residency status and filing obligations.

 - International tax and transfer pricing
 
 - Design, document and maintain the group’s transfer pricing policy for intercompany services, IP, financing and cost-sharing arrangements.
 
 - Prepare or oversee Master File, Local Files and Country-by-Country Reporting where required.
 
 - Manage permanent establishment risk, tax residency and substance requirements for each entity.
 
 - Apply double tax treaties, minimize withholding tax leakage and manage foreign tax credits.Review http://credits.Review intercompany agreements, cash repatriation, dividend flows and cross-border financing so they are tax-efficient.

 - Indirect taxes
 
 - Oversee VAT/GST and other indirect tax compliance, such as Brazil’s PIS/COFINS/ISS, Argentina’s IIBB and Mexico’s IVA, wherever applicable.
 
 - Define how indirect taxes apply to the group’s products and services, including financial services exemptions, digital services and cross-border supplies.
 
 - Monitor and implement major indirect tax reforms
 
 - Make sure e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements are met in every jurisdiction.

 - Financial reporting and accounting
 
 - Own the tax provision process (current and deferred taxes) under IFRS and/or US GAAP and local GAAPs.
 
 - Prepare tax disclosures for consolidated and statutory financial statements.
 
 - Work with Finance and external auditors on tax balances and audit queries.
 
 - Manage the group’s effective tax rate and forecast tax expense and cash taxes for budgeting.

 - Regulatory and fintech-specific tax obligations
 
 - Ensure compliance with financial-account information reporting regimes
 
 - Oversee withholding and reporting obligations on customer transactions, interest, FX gains and payments processed for customers.
 
 - Manage transaction taxes and tax obligations that apply to payment and banking activities in each country, such as Argentina’s tax on bank debits and credits.
 
 - Support regulatory license applications and audits where tax compliance is assessed.

 - Team and advisor management
 
 - Build, lead and develop the tax team (in-house and regional tax managers).
 
 - Select, manage and evaluate external tax advisors and service providers in each jurisdiction, and control their fees and the quality of their work.
 
 - Train non-tax teams (Finance, Product, Sales, Legal) on relevant tax matters.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - Background in a Big 4 tax advisory practice focused on financial entities, combined with in-house leadership at a scale fintech or neobank

 - Deep knowledge of Latin American tax structures and regulations, and international double-taxation treaties

 - Solid background addressing split-payment mechanics, cross-border value flows, and digital transaction withholdings

 - Ability to convert complex legal tax requirements into actionable technical logic for engineering execution

 - Experience structuring cross-bordering tax strategies for high-growth tech firms approaching public transitions

NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Advanced degree in Tax Law, Accounting, or a related field

 - Familiarity with tax treatment for multi-currency products and digital assets

BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary

 - Sign-on stock options bonus, so you become part of the success of the company

 - Discretionary performance bonus (stock options)

 - Paid annual leave

 - Private health insurance

 - Latest technology to work with

 - Strong team that will help you improve your skills

jobs.title: Senior Test Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is seeking a Senior Test Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is someone who is capable of designing, fabricating, operating, and improving on complex mechanical, electrical, and fluid systems for conducting rigorous testing of our innovative jet engine and subsystems. Your work at Astro Mechanica will keep test operations running smoothly, while constantly expanding and improving test capabilities.

In this role, your mission will be to create and operate test infrastructure for hardware research and development. You will have firsthand responsibility that every new design is rigorously tested to ensure quality and performance metrics are met prior to aircraft integration before leaving the ground. You embody the test-like-you-fly philosophy.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Architect test stand design and documentation (engineering drawings, P&ID, electrical schematics, test procedures) for testing components to integrated systems

 - Maintain test facility operations and maintenance, troubleshoot problems, site cleanliness

 - Implement robust data and video recording infrastructure

 - Analyze data for equipment activation, calibration, and operation

 - Diagnose stand problems efficiently and perform corrective actions

 - Continually improve facility capabilities to increase test throughput and reliability

 - Harness assembly (crimping/soldering terminals, cable lacing, troubleshooting)

 - Operate manual machine shop equipment (drills, cutting tools, mills, lathes)
 
 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 5+ years hands-on experience with fluidic and mechanical systems, test operations

 - Experience with hazardous environments (flammables, high voltage, pressurized systems) and safety mitigations

 - Knowledge of fluid systems hardware and instrumentation (pressure, temperature, load cells, relays, solenoids, pneumatics)

 - Familiarity with data acquisition and control systems, PLC hardware, computer networking, and software interfaces

 - Proficiency with PLC and data processing software (Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW)

 - Takes initiative for continuous improvement (not just completing assigned tasks)

 - Flexibility to work in fast-paced environment

 - Attentive to detail and maintain a high level of quality in all work
 
 

PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment

 - Company-funded perks, including weekly team lunches and Astro Mechanica swag
 
 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Bonus points if you

jobs.title: Principal Electrical Engineer, Power Systems
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is looking for a Principal Electrical Engineer focused on power systems development to join our growing team. You will be working across aviation and ground power teams to enable Astro Mechanica’s ground power product, a 13 MW aeroderivative generator, built to deliver fast, on-site power for data centers and industrial sites that can't wait years for grid capacity. In this role, you will be responsible for the medium-voltage electrical system that turns aircraft engines into ground power plants. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role where you will set the architecture, run the studies, specify the equipment, lead validation and commissioning, and be the technical authority on electrical safety. You will work closely with mechanical, controls, and manufacturing teams and represent the product with customers, utilities, and certification bodies. If you want to build a real power product rather than a slice of one, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Translate product requirements into electrical specifications, one-line diagrams, schematics, and BOMs

 - Own the electrical architecture and design of the plant including transformers, switchgear, cabling, protection, and grounding

 - Perform and review power system studies- load flow, short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, grounding, harmonics, and transient analysis

 - Ensure compliance with NEC, IEEE, IEC, UL, NFPA 70E, and utility interconnection requirements; own electrical safety and certification for the product

 - Mentor engineers, review designs, and serve as the technical interface to customers, utilities, and suppliers

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - BS, MS, or PhD with a focus on electrical engineering

 - 10+ years of experience designing, building, testing, and shipping electrical power systems

 - Deep experience with medium-voltage systems (1–38 kV): generators, transformers, switchgear, protective relays, and paralleling/grid-interconnect schemes

 - Strong command of power system analysis (symmetrical components, fault calculations, protection coordination, arc flash) and proficiency in ETAP, SKM, or EasyPower

 - Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards (NEC, IEEE, IEC, UL, NFPA 70E) and experience taking a product through certification

 - Hands-on field experience commissioning and troubleshooting MV equipment and generator control systems

 - Track record of owning a complex electrical product from concept through production with cross-functional teams

 - Familiarity with power electronics (inverters, rectifiers, excitation systems) and controls integration (SCADA, PLC, communication protocols) is a plus

PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment

jobs.description:

Kastle is building the AI employee for banks. We work with some of America's financial institutions, helping them scale their contact center and compliance operations using autonomous AI Agents that process payments, originate loans, and help customers get a world class experience during the biggest financial decisions of their lives. We've processed over $2 billion in transactions and are backed by Insight Partners and Y Combinator. If you are interested in building AI that is applied in the real world where precision, reliability, and performance matter and redefine access to credit across the world, apply below.

 

We just raised a $24M Series A and are growing fast!

About the role

We are seeking a highly skilled, results-driven GTM Recruiter to identify, attract, evaluate, and place top technical talent. The ideal candidate has a strong background in full-cycle recruiting, candidate sourcing, relationship management, and navigating fast-paced hiring environments.

This is a contract to hire role.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Full-Cycle Recruiting: Manage the end-to-end recruiting process, from intake meetings and sourcing through screening, interview coordination, offer negotiation, and placement.

 - GTM Talent Sourcing: Proactively identify and engage qualified candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, applicant tracking systems (ATS), job boards, referrals, professional networks, and other sourcing tools.

 - GTM Recruiting Expertise: Recruit for a variety of GTM positions, including Enterprise Account Executive, Sales Managers, SDR's, Sales Operations and more.

 - Candidate Assessment: Conduct thorough phone and video screenings to evaluate technical experience, relevant skills, communication abilities, employment history, compensation expectations, and overall fit.

 - Hiring Manager Partnership: Collaborate with hiring managers and account teams to define job requirements, establish candidate profiles, prioritize requisitions, and provide regular pipeline updates.

 - Pipeline Management: Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines, develop talent pools for recurring roles, and maintain consistent engagement with active and prospective candidates.

 - Interview Coordination: Facilitate interview scheduling, prepare candidates, collect feedback, and maintain communication throughout the selection process.

 - Offer Management and Closing: Present opportunities effectively, address candidate concerns, negotiate within approved compensation parameters, and secure candidate commitments.

 - Recruiting Metrics: Track submissions, interviews, placements, time-to-fill, candidate conversion rates, and other key performance indicators.

 - Market Intelligence: Stay informed about technical skill demand, candidate availability, compensation trends, and competitive hiring practices.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of GTM experience at well established tech company or start up

 - Demonstrated success sourcing, screening, and placing technical professionals in contract or project-based positions.

 - Proven experience with LinkedIn Recruiter, applicant tracking systems, candidate databases, and online sourcing platforms.

 - Excellent candidate assessment, interviewing, communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.

 - Ability to manage multiple open requisitions and changing priorities in a deadline-driven environment.
