jobs.description:
ABOUT ABUNDANT

Abundant is an applied research lab focused on scaling reinforcement learning for safe and reliable agentic capabilities. We are an extremely talent-dense team of researchers, roboticists, founders, and operators whose work includes the Waymo Driver.

 

THE ROLE

Frontier labs test their models in environments like ours, which means we are the first to see novel model behavior. You will make sure that alignment is baked into everything the do: the code we deploy, the runbooks we write, and the papers we publish.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Run experiments on how our environments shape behavior: reward hacking, cheating the task, unsafe use of tools, deception over long runs. Then change how we build them.

 - Break our own graders. Find the ways to score well without doing the work, close them, and keep the attacks as tests everyone runs.

 - Build the tools that watch agents: monitors over trajectories, red team harnesses, and safety benchmarks that stay hard as models improve. On real runs, not toy ones.

 - Keep our environments sealed. Network isolation, escapes, credentials, and how much damage an agent can do when it turns on us. Last summer’s failures came from here.

 - Choose a research question about oversight, control, or long-horizon autonomy, answer it, and publish. This is part of the job, not something you do at night.

 - Decide what we will not build. Tell partners plainly what they get from us is and is not safe for.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You are an engineer first. You build your own test pipelines, learn strange codebases quickly, and find the bug in the log.

 - You know LLM safety in depth: attacks, red teaming, monitoring and control evaluations, reward hacking.

 - You can turn a vague worry about a model into an experiment, run it, and say what the result does and does not prove.

 - You read transcripts closely. You catch the small thing that makes the whole result wrong.

 - You have put research into production systems, especially post-training, distillation, or evaluation that something depends on.

 - You write clearly enough that your results change what other people do.

 - You can decide fast with incomplete evidence and defend the call with data.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Published work on control, dangerous capability evaluations, oversight, or interpretability.

 - RLHF or RLAIF experience, and a view on how training choices show up in behavior.

 - You built or ran a public benchmark or agent task suite.

 - You have run many agents at once: sandboxes, containers, logging.

 - You have advised on AI safety or governance policy.
 
 

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$250,000 - $450,000

Cash Bonus

Sizable performance bonus tied to project and company milestones

Equity

Generous early-stage grant

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

jobs.title: QA & Authorisation Handler
jobs.description:
TURNING RISK INTO OPPORTUNITY

Human progress runs on a single trade: risk for opportunity. Every venture worth doing - a new business, a new home, an exciting trip - means accepting the chance it goes wrong. Insurance is what lets us take those chances anyway, and the claim is the moment it either delivers on that promise or fails to.

We're rebuilding that moment. ClaimSorted is an AI-native claims solution for insurers and large corporates that resolves claims faster, fairer, and more reliably than the industry ever has. Handle risk that well, and people are free to take on more of it - that's how you push society toward opportunity: not by eliminating risk, but by making recovery so fast and certain it stops being a reason to hold back.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a confident, analytical and detail-focused QA & Authorisation Handler to join our Technical Claims Support Team.

You will provide a key technical control across our claims operation, completing Quality Assurance reviews and reviewing claim settlements at the authorisation stage.

As the final line of defence before a claim settlement is approved, you will be responsible for independently reviewing the claim, evidence, policy coverage and settlement calculation before making the decision to authorise, pass back or escalate.

This requires confidence and strong technical judgement. You must be comfortable making decisions, challenging claim assessments where something does not look right and clearly explaining the reasoning behind your decision.

The role goes beyond identifying individual errors. You will use findings from QA and authorisations to identify potential financial leakage, recurring handling issues, process and control gaps and emerging trends across the claims operation.

You will be comfortable using data to understand where issues are occurring, identify root causes and turn findings into practical improvements to processes, controls, guidance and training.

As ClaimSorted works across a range of insurance products and partners, you will need to be adaptable and confident moving between different products, policy wordings, processes and priorities while maintaining consistently high standards.

As part of the wider Technical Claims Support Team, you will also support other technical claims activities where required.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Review claim settlements at authorisation stage across all ClaimSorted products, acting as the final line of defence before payment is approved.

 - Independently review policy coverage, supporting evidence and settlement calculations, making confident decisions to authorise, pass back or escalate.

 - Complete Quality Assurance reviews across all products, ensuring claims are handled accurately, fairly and in line with policy, partner and internal requirements.

 - Identify and prevent financial leakage, incorrect settlements and other customer or financial risks.

 - Provide clear, constructive and evidence-based feedback to Claims Handlers, confidently challenging decisions where required.

 - Use QA, authorisation and leakage data across products to identify trends, recurring errors, training needs and process or control gaps.

 - Support improvements to claims processes, guidance and controls based on findings and root-cause analysis.

 - Maintain accurate records of decisions and findings while effectively managing and prioritising QA and authorisation workloads.

 - Build and maintain the technical knowledge required to work confidently across all ClaimSorted product lines, partners and processes.

 - Work collaboratively across Claims Operations and the wider Technical Claims Support Team.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

 - +2 years experience completing claim authorisations within an insurance claims team is essential, with responsibility for reviewing and making decisions on claim settlements.

 - +3 years experience working across two or more of the following product lines within a claims role: Pet, Travel, Property, Auto, Gadget or similar insurance products.

 - Strong technical claims knowledge, with the confidence to independently review, challenge and make evidence-based decisions.

 - Excellent attention to detail, particularly when reviewing policy coverage, supporting evidence and settlement calculations.

 - Strong analytical skills, with experience identifying financial leakage, trends, recurring errors and process or control gaps.

 - Able to confidently provide clear, constructive feedback and explain the rationale behind decisions.

 - Highly organised and able to prioritise a varied workload based on risk, value and urgency.

 - Adaptable and comfortable learning new products, policy wordings and processes in a fast-paced environment.

MISSION

To act as a final line of defence within the claims settlement process, ensuring claim outcomes are accurate, fair and supported by policy and evidence before settlement is authorised.

The QA & Authorisation Handler will use strong technical judgement and independent decision-making to protect customer outcomes and financial performance, identifying errors, potential leakage and operational risks before they result in incorrect settlements.

Through Quality Assurance, data analysis and trend identification, the role will also identify wider knowledge, process and control gaps and help turn individual findings into sustainable improvements across Claims Operations

jobs.title: DevRel (SF Events)
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRIGGER.DEV

Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is an open source platform used by developers to build production-grade AI agents. It's an SDK and the infrastructure to run agents reliably at scale, so teams can focus on the product instead of the plumbing.

Our Cloud product is a managed service where we deploy our users' code and auto-scale from zero to millions of executions. With the rise of AI, being able to offload async tasks reliably is a key part of any developer's toolkit - we're building the infrastructure to make that a reality.

ABOUT THE POSITION

We're looking for someone based in San Francisco whose entire job is turning up to events, meeting developers, advocating for Trigger, and being brilliant. This role is deliberately narrow: it's 100% events, not product education, content strategy, or general marketing.

The work breaks down into three things: showing up to existing events (meetups, AI Tinkers, YC events, conferences) and being visibly excellent in the room; getting speaking slots at those events and delivering awesome talks; and, over time, organizing our own events or co-hosting them with other big tech names, like joint hackathons at the YC offices.

The goal is pure awareness. You might not even mention Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev by name at most events - the point is being visibly excellent and well-liked in the rooms where developers already are, so that a groundswell of Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev mentions builds naturally across the SF ecosystem over time.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

You'll do a variety of things including:

 - Turn up to events, meet developers, advocate for Trigger, be brilliant - attending SF developer events, meetups, AI Tinkers, YC events, and conferences, and building genuine relationships across the SF developer and founder ecosystem

 - Get speaking slots at existing events, deliver awesome talks - pitching yourself for talks and panels, and showing up polished and memorable when you get the slot

 - Organize our own events (or co-host them with other big tech names) - running Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev meetups or talks, and exploring joint events like hackathons co-hosted at spaces such as the YC offices

 - Optionally writing blog recaps or producing short YouTube clips of talks, where it's a natural byproduct of the work rather than the focus

 - Working largely independently - you'll be on your own in SF a lot, so being deeply self-motivated is essential

 - Reporting back on activity: number of events attended, video of any talks given, and a written recap of who you met

REQUIREMENTS

You really need to have:

 - Genuine stage presence and charisma - we'll want to see video evidence of you speaking, presenting, or performing (YouTube is the bar)

 - A developer background; you should be credible and comfortable in a room of engineers

 - High self-motivation - this role has little day-to-day oversight and a real risk of isolation, so you need to thrive working independently

 - Genuine belief in what Trigger.dev http://Trigger.dev is building, since you'll be representing us informally in every room you're in

You'll be an amazing fit if you:

 - Are an ex-YC founder, giving you access to YC-only events and community

 - Existing relationships or an existing audience within the SF/AI developer or founder scene

 - Been an early-stage founder yourself, or are very early in your career and highly self-directed

 - A track record of speaking at or organizing developer events

 - Have a social media presence

ABOUT THE TEAM

 - We are a small team with a flat hierarchy

 - We encourage continuous learning and personal development

 - Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help

 - We care about our customers and the open-source community

 - Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge

WORKING AT A COMMERCIAL OPEN SOURCE SOFTWARE COMPANY IS MORE THAN JUST YOUR DAY JOB

 - We have an active community on Discord and GitHub. Everyone on the team helps customers, reviews PRs, and creates issues

 - Great documentation matters more than ever, both for humans and for the AI tools that read it. Everyone here keeps docs up to date

 - We are a product-led growth company so everyone is expected to get involved in creating content like code examples, blog articles, videos and tweets
 

BENEFITS

 - Generous, transparent compensation and equity - We hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity as a way to ensure everyone is invested in the success of the company.

 - Async working - Need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!

 - Home office - We will help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

 - Generous vacation - We believe it's important to take time off. We encourage you to take your 25 days vacation excluding national holidays, plus sick leave and generous parental leave.

 - Training budget - An annual budget to contribute towards learning such as purchasing books, an Audible subscription or online courses.

 - Pension and 401k contributions - Enroll in our company pension scheme or we'll contribute directly to your private pension.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.description:
WHY CASCA?

Casca is building AGI for banking. We’re replacing decades-old legacy systems with AI-native technology that automates 90% of the manual work humans once had to do. 

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Our customers are FDIC-insured banks. Every one of them puts us through security review, control questionnaires, pen test results, and third-party risk assessment before we touch production. Then they hand us borrower tax returns, bank statements, and the data behind credit decisions on their own balance sheet.

So security isn't a compliance checkbox here. It's a precondition for the company existing. Every deal we win depends on it, and one bad breach ends the business.

The surface area is large and getting larger: a multi-tenant AI platform, a cloud estate under bank data-handling requirements, agents that read and act on customer data, and an engineering team shipping into all of it every day. Nobody can review their way across that. You build the guardrails, defaults, and tooling that scale past you.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Software. Detections, libraries, policy-as-code, automation, CI/CD checks — reviewed, tested, and deployed like any other service.

 - Design reviews and threat models on what actually matters: auth, tenant isolation, data handling, anything touching borrower PII.

 - The AI attack surface. Prompt injection, tool-use abuse, exfiltration paths through agents, and the evals that tell you whether your controls hold.

 - Incidents, end to end, including the write-up and the fixes that follow.

 - Bank security reviews and audits, turned into engineering work that improves the system rather than paperwork that describes it.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - Several years of experience in AppSec, with specifics you can walk us through: bugs you found, incidents you ran, systems you hardened, tooling you shipped.

 - You write production code. We work primarily in TypeScript/Node.js and Python.

 - You know where security boundaries break in multi-tenant systems, and why it's usually authorization.

 - You can explain risk to an engineer in engineering terms and get the fix shipped without escalating.

 - You can sit across from a bank's security team, take hard questions honestly, and leave them more confident than when you walked in.

 - Steady during incidents. Honest afterward.

 - You'd rather build leverage than become a bottleneck.

HELPFUL, NOT REQUIRED

 - Securing LLM or agentic products in production.

 - Standing up a security function at a fast-growing company.

 - Working inside or selling into regulated financial institutions: SOC 2, GLBA, FFIEC guidance, third-party risk, exam support.

WHAT YOU'LL GET: 

 - Impact & Ownership: A unique opportunity to shape the future of banking through AI, owning end-to-end product initiatives.

 - Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a talented and passionate team that values continuous improvement and knowledge sharing.

 - Competitive Compensation: Includes salary, benefits, and potential equity in a fast-growing startup.

 - Professional Growth: Access to resources and mentorship to expand your skill set, influence strategy, and accelerate your career.

 - Culture of Innovation: We encourage risk-taking, learning from failures, and pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in fintech.

As an early-stage company building at the frontier of AI, we work with high intensity and commitment. While schedules can vary by role/team, many weeks will demand extra focus, flexibility and time particularly during major launches and high impact sprints. We're seeking those who are aligned to and able to commit to that expectation.

jobs.title: Senior Lead Full Stack Python Engineer

Founded by Silicon Valley engineers and former Tesla leaders, we are a profitable, fast-growing company with teams in the US, China, Taiwan, Vietnam and Europe.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our customers are moving from a handful of cameras per plant to fleets of hundreds, and our largest accounts are on the path to thousands of OV cameras across factories in China, Vietnam, Europe and the Americas. Deploying, updating, monitoring and supporting cameras at that scale needs real products, not scripts and shared drives.

We are looking for a Senior Lead Full Stack Python Engineer to lead our Internal Tools team and own the products that make deploying thousands of AI cameras globally repeatable and reliable. You will take over OV Pro Tools, a suite of services that already runs in customer plants today: OV Vault (data storage), OV Fleet (fleet monitoring), OV Train (GPU-accelerated training) and OV Hub (Git-based recipe versioning and sharing). Your job is to turn these into one coherent platform, decide what gets built next and ship it.

This is a hands-on lead role. You will spend most of your time building, from React and TypeScript interfaces down to the Python services behind them, while leading a small team (one engineer today, more as we deploy more systems around the world) and setting the technical direction. You will also work on the frontier: LLM-powered assistants and agent builders that sit on top of our vision system.

About half your time will be spent in China, in the factories where our cameras run at scale (Nantong, Haiyan, Shenzhen and others), deploying, supporting and learning from the people who use the tools every day. The rest is product development from our Taipei base, working closely with the R&D team there.

You will operate with high autonomy: you pick the approach, ship quickly and iterate with real users.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead the Internal Tools team. Set the roadmap, priorities and engineering standards for the team. Mentor and grow the engineers on it, run planning and reviews, and hire as the scope grows. Stay hands-on: you ship code every week.

 - Build the fleet deployment platform. Own the products that let us and our customers deploy, configure, update and monitor thousands of cameras across many sites: device management, recipe versioning and distribution, staged and canary updates with rollback, fleet health monitoring and alerting, telemetry and log tooling.

 - Own the OV Pro Tools suite end to end. Scale OV Vault, OV Fleet, OV Train and OV Hub from working v1 services into a reliable, modular platform that can be deployed independently or as a suite, including in air-gapped factory networks with no internet access.

 - Build GenAI applications. Design and ship LLM-powered tools that make monitoring and deploying large fleets of cameras easier.

 - Full-stack web tools. Own tools end to end, from React/TypeScript frontends to Python backends, APIs and MCP servers.

 - Integrate with the edge-AI stack. Connect the tools to the camera fleet, inference outputs, recipes and firmware so they work against real inspection data, not toy examples.

 - 0 to 1 product building. Prototype quickly, get tools in front of users, and iterate. Turn rough ideas into shipped products, then sharpen them based on real usage.

 - Deploy and support in the field. Travel to customer factories in China for installations, upgrades and critical support. Train customer teams, troubleshoot integrations with existing factory systems, and bring what you learn back into the product.

 - Quality and craft. Sweat performance, reliability and UX. These tools are how customers and colleagues experience Overview; they should feel fast, clear and trustworthy. Code quality needs to be pristine: we use agents to write code, but you understand and own the final design and solution.

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.

WHY APPLY

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives.

Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers.

The AfterQuery Research Scholar program is a semester-long collaboration for students pursuing ambitious, publishable work in one of AfterQuery’s focus areas:

 - Data quality and data mix

 - Post-training research, including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning

 - Agent and foundation-model evaluation

 - Public benchmarks in coding and specialized domains such as medicine, finance, law, and STEM

Projects are shaped around each scholar’s interests, with the goal of producing a joint publication. Scholars receive weekly mentorship and hands-on support with engineering, datasets, human annotation, and compute resources. jobs.title: Account Manager - Dental - International
jobs.description:
ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/ and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

About the Role

The Account Manager will be instrumental in helping grow and retain Clipboard's existing markets. Healthcare providers are core to the Clipboard marketplace — the Account Manager is in charge of nurturing and expanding relationships with current users, going deep with those users to understand their needs, and ensuring they're consistently successful on the platform. There's no ceiling to what you can achieve in this role — if you're highly motivated to go above and beyond, a diligent executor, and a strong written/verbal communicator, Clipboard is the place for you to excel.

Responsibilities

 - Managing and growing relationships with an existing portfolio of healthcare providers and dental offices

 - Clearly articulating the value proposition of the app to current users to drive continued engagement and expansion

 - Going deep with healthcare providers and dental offices to uncover their evolving needs, understand their challenges, and find ways to genuinely help them succeed on the platform

 - Establishing credibility and rapport with providers, which includes demonstrating a strong understanding of the app

 - Being the go-to point of contact for users that need help navigating the app, resolving issues, and getting the most out of the platform

 - Helping fill new and urgent shifts in your assigned markets

Qualifications

 - Willingness to hustle / lack of fear

 - Experience texting, emailing, and talking with English-speaking clients and prospects

Requirements

 - Stable high-speed internet connection

 - A computer workstation (laptop or desktop)

 - Internationally located (not in US, CA, UK, NZ, or AU)

 - Availability to work US working hours

 - Fluency in English speaking and writing

Beyond the Basics — What Will Make You Successful

 - Noticing & Curiosity — You pick up on things others miss and ask "why" more than once because the first answer is rarely the whole story. You dig to understand the root of a problem or situation rather than accepting things at face value, and you're constantly updating your understanding of the customers you serve.

 - Initiative & Persistence — You have a bias for action. You know that our customers are dealing with real problems today, and you don't wait for perfect information before making a move. You're scrappy and self-reliant, you find ways through obstacles rather than around them, and you bring solutions instead of asking "what should I do?"

 - Ownership — The buck stops with you, no matter what anyone else did or did not do. You take full responsibility for your results, fix problems when you see them — even outside your immediate area — and put processes in place to make sure those problems don't happen again.

 - Customer-Centric — You feel your customers' situations genuinely and care about improving their lives, not just hitting a number. Talking to customers and solving their problems isn't a task on your list — it's the job.

 - Humble — You're low ego and care about getting to the best outcome, not about being right. You readily admit when you don't know something, you actively seek out feedback, and you're always looking to become a better version of yourself.

Benefits

 - Do great work that matters for customers who could really use your help

 - Competitive pay

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Fully Remote

Estimated annual compensation: $12,000–$15,600 USD. Each candidate's compensation offer within this range will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, and geographic location.

Quick Note on Scammers: 

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO 

Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure.

Role at a Glance

Gecko Robotics is seeking a Software Engineering Intern to join RoboSPLAT within Field Infra in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.

RoboSPLAT builds software and tools that help teams develop, deploy, debug, and operate Gecko’s robotic and ultrasonic testing (UT) collection systems. You will work primarily in C/C++ and Python on a defined project that improves system integration, diagnostics, testing, or development workflows.

What you will do

 - Develop C/C++ and Python software for a defined software project under the guidance of experienced engineers.

 - Build or improve tooling, diagnostics, tests, or workflows that reduce friction in developing, debugging, and deploying software on robot hardware.

 - Work across software and system boundaries by integrating services or hardware-facing interfaces, investigating system behavior, testing solutions, and documenting findings.

 - Use version control, code review, and structured debugging practices to produce maintainable code.

 - Collaborate with RoboSPLAT and partner teams, communicate status and tradeoffs clearly, and deliver a final demonstration and handoff.

Technologies We Use (If Applicable)

C/C++, Python, Git, Linux, networking, and ROS 2. Depending on the project, you may also work with the Yocto Project, NVIDIA Jetson Orin, cloud infrastructure, or Electron, React, and TypeScript.

About You

You are a hands-on engineering student who wants to understand how software behaves on real hardware. You work methodically, seek out missing knowledge, communicate clearly, and care about building tools and systems that others can use.

Required Skills

 - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related engineering discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.

 - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.

 - Foundational programming experience in C/C++ and Python, including object-oriented programming.

 - Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.

 - Understanding of basic computer networking.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain findings and tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.

 - Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with ROS 2.

 - Familiarity with embedded Linux systems or platforms such as the Yocto Project or NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

 - Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP.

 - Experience building applications with Electron, React, or TypeScript.

 - Exposure to embedded communication protocols, microcontrollers, or real-time operating systems is a plus.

 - Ability to work with basic electronic systems, read simple schematics, and use common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and programmable power supplies.

WHO WE ARE

At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. 

Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact.

Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

Who we’re looking for

We're seeking a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to train domain-specific language models and provide technical leadership to the team. You'll own critical parts of our training infrastructure, mentor engineers, and drive technical decisions from data preparation through production deployment. You have deep hands-on experience training language models at scale, lead by example through rigorous experimentation and high-quality code, and are motivated by seeing your work deployed to millions of users. You thrive in fast-paced environments where you balance technical depth with practical business impact.

What you’ll do

 - Analyze model performance and training data, formulate hypotheses, design and execute rigorous experiments to systematically improve model quality, training and inference efficiency, and downstream task performance

 - Drive technical decision-making for model architecture, training strategies, and infrastructure choices

 - Provide technical leadership and mentorship to ML engineers and interns, conducting code reviews, sharing best practices, and accelerating team growth

 - Train large language models through continued pre-training and full parameter fine-tuning on proprietary datasets

 - Build and optimize distributed training infrastructure across multi-node GPU clusters using frameworks like DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron-LM, or Axolotl

 - Own large-scale data preparation: filtering, quality assessment, deduplication, and data mixture strategies for training corpora at 100B+ token scale

 - Generate and curate high-quality synthetic data for instruction fine-tuning and capability enhancement

 - Debug training stability issues, optimize training and inference throughput (quantization, distillation, serving optimization), and monitor model performance throughout long-running distributed jobs

 - Build robust evaluation frameworks and establish metrics to measure model quality and guide decisions

 - Write production-grade, well-tested code and set engineering standards for the team

Minimum qualifications

 - 7+ years of ML engineering experience

 - Technical leadership experience: mentoring engineers, conducting code reviews, making architecture decisions, and delivering projects with measurable business impact

jobs.title: Senior Pre-Sales Engineer (NYC)
jobs.description:
Location: New York City (On-Site, 5 days) 

ABOUT KOMBO

Kombo is the unified API for ATS, HRIS, LMS and payroll systems. Instead of spending months building integrations one by one, companies integrate once with Kombo and connect to 200+ platforms instantly.

Since Y Combinator (S22), we've grown to 8-figures in revenue, 80+ team members, and raised $30M+ from YC, Volition Capital, and Acadian Ventures. We're tripling the team and revenue this year. And we move upmarket, with larger, more complex deals and sophisticated buying committees.

THE ROLE

We're hiring our US-based Pre-Sales Engineer to own the technical relationship with customers, from first sales call through successful implementation. The role is roughly 70% pre-sales / 30% post-sales, but the split is about time, not identity: We need someone who instinctively runs discovery and shapes deals, not someone who's comfortable in a technical conversation and happens to also do pre-sales.

You'll work closely with our Sales team, and our CRO to close deals and with Product/Engineering to turn customer insights into product improvements.

This is a builder role. You'll help grow our US GTM function and create the playbooks, while carrying deals yourself.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the technical sales cycle

 - Run technical discovery that uncovers the business objective behind a request, not just the request itself, including in domains we haven't fully mapped yet, where you'll need to hold credibility without pretending to have answers you don't

 - Create technical proposals covering architecture, security, and implementation approach

 - Partner with AEs on complex, multi-stakeholder deals with engineering and executive stakeholders

Drive implementations to go-live for complex projects

 - Own the technical relationship from POC through signed contract through production deployment

 - Create the supporting technical assets as you go: demo environments, Postman collections, integration guides, troubleshooting documentation
 

 Help Build the US Pre-Sales Function

 - Document repeatable playbooks for discovery, scoping, and implementation

 - Feed customer insight back to Product/Engineering in a way that shapes the roadmap without overpromising on it

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role at a B2B SaaS company, with genuine pre-sales ownership (discovery, champion-building, deal shaping) - not just implementation with some pre-sales overlap

 - Track record working complex deals with technical and non-technical stakeholders - consistent deal value of $100k-150k+

 - Strong communication skills: you can whiteboard architecture with engineers and translate value to executives

 - Hands-on with APIs - you can read documentation, ideally write sample code, and debug integration issues

 - Comfort with ambiguity and building things from scratch

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS

 - You've built and closed with at least one genuine technical champion in an enterprise account, not just a friendly technical contact

 - You've built real credibility with AEs and prospects in a domain (e.g. HRIS, ATS) you likely didn't know deeply on day one

 - You've built at least one reusable playbook, template, or asset (e.g. discovery framework, POC scoping doc, demo narrative) that other people on the team now use without you

 - You can point to your influence on ARR, deal velocity, or conversion

 - You're a trusted second read for AEs on deal strategy, and go far beyond just a technical resource they loop in when asked

HOW WE WORK

Ownership end-to-end. A customer isn't "handed off" when the contract is signed - you own the relationship from first technical call through successful go-live and beyond. Problems that surface in implementation are your problems to solve, not someone else's.

Written thinking. We use long-form documents to make decisions and share context. You'll write implementation plans, technical briefs, and customer-facing documentation that help the whole team move faster. If you prefer talking through everything in meetings, this isn't the right fit.

High-performance, high-support. We're a small team of people who are exceptional at what they do. Ex-founders, and operators who've built at scale before. We hold a high bar and give you the autonomy to meet it. We also celebrate wins together (roughly once a week for big releases, closings, or milestones).

Bias Towards Action, and high agency: We are building - if we need a resource, we create it. If a process needs improvement, we refine it. We take the initiative and ownership on everything we own, and don’t wait for permission.

In-person by default. We believe the best work happens together. This role is on-site in NYC 5 days per week.

NOT A FIT IF

 - You prefer fully remote work

 - You need extensive structure and hand-holding to be effective

 - Your instinct is to answer the question you were asked rather than find out why it's being asked in the first place

WHY THIS ROLE IS EXCITING

 - Work at the frontier: Integrating edge AI cameras into high-speed automation is still new. You’ll help set the standard.

 - Talent density + fast feedback loops: You’ll work with world-class AI, embedded, firmware, and product teams—and your field learnings directly change the product and deployment playbooks.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

MECHANICAL INTEGRATION

 - mounting design, stability, alignment, adjustability, service access, environmental protection, cable routing/strain relief

 - Review machine builder CAD (2D/3D) and sign off on designs that meet Overview.ai http://Overview.ai integration standards.

 - Provide direct, practical feedback to machine builders to improve designs before metal is cut:
 
 - reduce vibration sensitivity, protect optics, ensure repeatable alignment, avoid thermal drift, improve maintainability

 - Specify integration requirements and best practices:
 
 - mounting interfaces, bracket designs, tolerances, datum strategy, access clearances, protective enclosures, contamination management

 - Anticipate long-term failure modes and design them out:
 
 - loosening fasteners, wear points, cable fatigue, lens contamination, shock/vibration, misalignment, fixture flex

 - Own commissioning readiness: ensure mechanical design supports stable triggering, repeatable imaging, and rapid service.

FIELD APPLICATIONS ENGINEERING (PRODUCTION OUTCOMES)

 - Support new line deployments and maintain/optimize systems already installed at customer sites.

 - Diagnose issues that look “AI” but are actually mechanical/system integration problems:
 
 - intermittent image quality, drift over time, vibration blur, occlusion, part presentation variability, contamination

 - Train customer teams and machine builders on integration best practices and basic troubleshooting.

 - Document field learnings and turn them into repeatable standards, checklists, and reference designs.

WHO YOU ARE REQUIRED

 - Strong mechanical/systems integration background in automation equipment or industrial machines

 - Ability to read and review machine design CAD and provide actionable design feedback (SolidWorks/Creo/AutoCAD or similar)

 - Experience integrating components into machines with attention to:
 
 - tolerances, alignment, vibration, serviceability, cabling, environmental protection, repeatability

 - Comfort in factory environments: commissioning, troubleshooting, and working hands-on

 - Willingness and ability to be based in Taipei, with regular travel to customer sites across Taiwan.

 - Mandarin fluency (native or near-native)

 - Working English for technical collaboration with global teams

 - High ownership mindset: you take problems personally and drive them to closure

STRONG PREFERENCES

 - Experience with high-volume manufacturing lines (electronics, automotive, connectors, battery, packaging, assembly)

 - Experience working with machine builders/integrators and managing design iteration loops

 - Comfort partnering with controls engineers on timing/triggering and line sequencing constraints

WHY OVERVIEW.AI http://Overview.ai (WHY TOP CANDIDATES JOIN)

 - Extreme growth + real-world impact: We’re not building demos. We’re deploying AI systems on real production lines, at scale.

 - Talent density: You’ll work with world-class engineers and operators across AI, embedded systems, and enterprise deployment.

 - Front-row seat to the AI manufacturing wave: This is one of the biggest transformations happening in industry right now.

 - Ownership: In this role, your work directly changes the trajectory of the company. Great hiring = winning.

 - Global exposure: You’ll work with advanced customers and factories across Taiwan and the broader APAC region.

Insurance is what lets us take those chances anyway, and the claim is the moment it either delivers on that promise or fails to.

We're rebuilding that moment. ClaimSorted is an AI-native claims solution for insurers and large corporates that resolves claims faster, fairer, and more reliably than the industry ever has. Handle risk that well, and people are free to take on more of it - that's how you push society toward opportunity: not by eliminating risk, but by making recovery so fast and certain it stops being a reason to hold back.

You will investigate the underlying claim, gather and review supporting evidence, prepare clear and robust responses, and work closely with our insurance partners to ensure regulatory requests are handled accurately and on time.

You will act as a subject matter expert for complaints, using complaint outcomes and trends to identify opportunities to improve claims handling and customer outcomes.

As part of the wider Technical Claims Support Team, you will also support other technical claims activities where required, including Quality Assurance, Fraud, Recoveries and Payment Authorisations.

 - Complete root-cause analysis and recommend improvements to claims processes, controls and customer communications.

 - Provide constructive feedback to Claims Handlers and operational teams where complaint investigations identify quality or knowledge gaps.

 - Maintain knowledge of relevant insurance complaint-handling requirements.

 - Support the development and maintenance of complaint procedures, templates and internal guidance.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

 - Must be APA or CIP qualified

 - Experience investigating complex claims and complaints and reaching fair, evidence-based conclusions.

 - Excellent attention to detail, particularly when reviewing policy wording, claim documentation and regulatory correspondence.

 - Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple complaints and regulatory deadlines simultaneously.

 - Ability to identify root causes and use complaint findings to recommend improvements to claims processes and customer outcomes.

jobs.title: Customer Success Lead (San Francisco)
jobs.description:
ABOUT GIGA

Giga has recently raised a $61M Series A and is working with Fortune 500 customers to deploy the next generation of customer experience - real-time AI agents that can understand emotion, resolve issues instantly, and scale across the world's largest enterprises.

Industry leaders like DoorDash trust Giga with their most complex support and operations workflows across voice, chat, and email, in high-stakes regulated environments where accuracy and compliance matter. We're at an exciting inflection point.

While we've found real commercial success, our ambitions are larger: to become the go-to AI platform for all enterprise automation, powered by our voice superintelligence. The work affects millions of people every day, and our team has the autonomy to make true impact - with brilliant founders, a clear path forward, and the kind of momentum that defines generational companies.

If being part of that resonates with you, we'd love to hear from you!

 - Voice AI startup Giga raises $61M Series A https://fortune.com/2025/11/05/voice-ai-giga-raise-61-million-customer-service-series-a/

 - DoorDash and Giga Partnership https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7391576181009018883/

 

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Customer Success Lead to own consumption across a book of Giga's enterprise production customers. Every enterprise contract we sign carries a minimum usage commitment. Your job is to get each customer to that commitment and past it: more conversations on the agent, more intents live, more channels and business units on Giga. You carry a number for it. You'll own each customer's timeline for getting there, and you'll push on it from both sides: externally, when the customer's team is slow to expand scope or route volume, and internally, when a product bug or a missing capability is what's holding them back. You sit between our Forward Deployed Engineers, who build and tune the agents, and our Enterprise Sales Representatives, who close the deals. You're the quarterback in the middle.

This is the first hire in a function we intend to build. You report to the CEO, you'll work directly with the founders and the revenue leadership team, and you'll define how customer success works at Giga before anyone else joins it.

This is not an FDE role and it's not a renewals desk. You won't be digging through tickets to find the root cause; the FDEs do that. You will know that something needs fixing, what it's costing the customer, and when it has to be done, and you'll drive it there. You'll also be the one telling customers what we're shipping and where the next use case is. When that turns into a real deal, the Enterprise Sales Representative comes back in to run it with you. You own usage and the timeline, they own paper.

 

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

A few examples from our current roadmap:

 - Consumption plans for every account in the book: Build the per-account plan from go-live to the annual minimum and beyond: which intents and channels go live in which month, what volume each one carries, and what has to be true on the customer's side and ours for each date to hold. Track it weekly and act when a week goes flat.

 - Quarterbacking the timeline, both directions: Externally, keep the customer's team moving on scope expansion, volume routing, and the approvals that slow them down. Internally, when a product bug or a missing capability is blocking a customer's next step, get it prioritized with FDEs and Product, hold the date, and tell the customer the truth about it. You don't investigate the ticket. You make sure it gets fixed on time.

 - Escalations at the right altitude: When something breaks in production, you're the customer's single point of contact. You know what's broken and what it's costing them, you pull in the right FDE, you own the communication up to the customer's executive, and you stay on it until volume is back.

 - Evangelizing what's next: Pitch customers on what we're shipping and where the next use case is in their operation. Mine conversation data, Agent KPIs, and their queue metrics to find it, quantify the savings, and get their operating leader interested. When it turns into a real opportunity, bring the Enterprise Sales Representative back in and run it together.

 - Executive cadence: Run monthly value reviews and quarterly business reviews with the customer's VP or SVP of Customer Care, Operations, or CX, with our CEO and founders in the room when it matters. The output is a bigger volume plan with dates on it, not a satisfaction score.

 - Making consumption visible: Work with RevOps to get usage against commit, and the blockers behind it, in front of the whole revenue org in Salesforce every week.

As the first Customer Success hire at Giga, you'll be expected to build the playbook, not inherit one, and to show the CEO what the function should look like at 30 customers.

 

HOW YOU'LL BE MEASURED

You own a defined book of production customers and you're paid on two things: every customer in it reaching full value on their commitment, and the book growing past it.

 - Gross revenue retention. Every customer in your book consumes their full contracted commitment and renews at or above it. This is the floor, and it's most of the variable.

 - Net revenue retention. Usage above commit, new intents, new channels, new lines of business. You find it, quantify it with the customer, and hand a qualified opportunity to the Enterprise Sales Representative to close. They carry the quota credit, you get NRR credit when it lands.

 - Leading indicators we watch with you: time from production go-live to run-rate consumption, weekly usage against the ramp plan, and executive engagement on each account.

Compensation is $200,000 to $250,000 on-target earnings depending on experience, split 75% base and 25% variable, plus equity. Variable is paid quarterly, weighted 70% gross revenue retention and 30% net revenue retention across your book, with accelerator

jobs.title: QA Engineer
jobs.description:
At some point in the future, every business will answer their phone with voice AI. We are building the platform that makes it possible, and we’re making sure the experience of using it doesn’t suck.

Phonely builds conversational voice AI agents for high volume phone workflows. Our customers use us to qualify leads, book appointments, route calls, and resolve real customer conversations in production. We are growing fast and just getting started.

About the Role

We’re hiring a dedicated QA engineer. You’ll be the last set of eyes on a feature before it ships, responsible for testing what engineers build for both correctness and UI/UX quality.

A big part of this role is automating yourself out of the repetitive parts. You’ll be the primary owner of our automated end to end test suite and you’ll expand and maintain it as the product grows.

This is an early-career role with a lot of room to grow. You’re the first QA hire, which means you’re not inheriting a process, you’re building one. No specific prior experience is required.

What You’ll Do

• QA new features and bug fixes across Phonely’s product, testing happy paths, edge cases, regressions, and general UI/UX quality

• Build automated tests to cover every non-human part of your job

• Own, maintain, and expand our automated end to end test suite

• Reproduce bugs reported by customers and internal teams, then write them up clearly enough that an engineer can fix them without a follow-up call

• Push back when something isn’t good enough to ship

• Build the QA process from scratch as our first dedicated QA hire

What We’re Looking For

• Some experience building or testing software: QA, software engineering, solutions/FDE, or similar

• Enough technical depth to inspect logs, HTTP requests, and browser behavior, and the instinct to use AI to move faster doing it

• AI native. You reach for the model before you reach for the manual

• User empathy and real opinions. You’re the last touchpoint before a feature ships, so you need to notice when something is bad and have the chutzpah to say so

• A technical background. A degree in CS or engineering is preferred, or equivalent hands-on experience

• Significant overlap with North American working hours

Nice to Have

• Experience with Playwright, Cypress, or similar E2E frameworks

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and running tests in them

• Any exposure to voice, telephony, or real-time systems

Why Join Phonely

We’re super cool. Our team is a group of ex-athletes, founders, and builders with low egos, and a high belief that life is not about taking the easy road, but challenging ourselves to find the most we can be. Working at Phonely feels like family, we eat most meals together as a team (the company pays for food), we go on runs, hikes and surf together when we’re not working. Also we rent out Airbnbs in cool places (Rocky Mountains, Costa Rica) for our annual offsite so you can still see the world while on the grind.

Interview Process

1. 15-min intro call

2. Deep dive on your experience with a member of the engineering team

3. Practical exercise: find the bugs in a live feature and write them up

4. Final conversation with leadership

jobs.title: Founding GTM
jobs.description:
ABOUT PROOF OF HUMAN

Proof of Human is building the global standard for human verification across the internet. As the line between human and machine behavior becomes harder to discern, establishing who or what is behind every interaction is becoming foundational to the integrity of a digital world. Founded by Princeton PhD scientists, Mayank Agrawal and Matt Hardy, Proof of Human is a research and technology company developing the science, products, and infrastructure required to meet that challenge at global scale. As a public benefit corporation, we treat this work as both a technical frontier and a public responsibility, advancing the field while shaping the standards and governance for how human verification systems are developed, deployed, and used.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Founding GTM to join us to build the next phase of how Proof of Human goes to market. You’ll work directly with the founders and staff across sales, growth, and market development: generating pipeline, leading customer conversations, advancing deals, and turning both your intuition, your research, and what you learn on the front lines into sharper positioning, stronger systems, and clearer strategic direction. This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who wants to create the playbook while running it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Market Development: Test new industries, buyer personas, use cases, messages, and acquisition channels to determine where Proof of Human has the strongest opportunity to win. Use what you learn to recommend where the company and product should focus.

 - Pipeline Generation: Build targeted pipelines across our existing market and select new verticals through thoughtful outbound, warm introductions, events, partnerships, and other distribution channels you identify, to create a steady flow of growth opportunities.

 - Customer Discovery: Lead early conversations with prospective customers to understand their problems, priorities, urgency, decision process, and willingness to commit. Clearly communicate Proof of Human’s value to both business and technical stakeholders.

 - Deal Execution: Own opportunities from initial outreach through discovery, demos, pilots, pricing conversations, close and commercial follow-up, working closely with the team to move qualified deals toward close while maintaining a consistent momentum throughout.

 - Sales Enablement: Create the materials that help deals move forward for you and the team, including tailored follow-ups, pitch decks, business cases, pilot proposals, objection handling, case studies, and vertical-specific narratives for the buyer and use case.

 - Growth Experimentation: Run lightweight, measurable experiments across audiences, messaging, distribution channels, and conversion points. Use the results to determine what should be scaled, changed, or stopped, and turn tests into repeatable programs
 .

YOU’LL BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - Nobody has to hand you a map. There’s no established process yet for much of what this role touches. You find a starting point, try something, learn from the result, and build the next version without losing momentum as conditions change.

 - You’re curious across disciplines. Whether you’re speaking with an academic, engineer, or business executive, or entering an unfamiliar market, you want to understand the substance and communicate in the language of the person across from you.

 - You move fast once you see what needs to happen. You don’t wait for the perfect moment or someone’s blessing. You take ownership, bring other people along, and keep pushing through ambiguity, friction, and setbacks until the work is finished.

jobs.title: Founding Product Manager
jobs.description:
At some point in the future, every business will answer their phone with voice AI. We are building the platform that makes it possible.

Phonely builds conversational voice AI agents for high volume phone workflows. Our customers use us to qualify leads, book appointments, route calls, and resolve real customer conversations in production. We are growing fast and just getting started.

About the Role

This is our first product hire. You will be helping drive the direction of Phonely. Our customers are pretty good at telling us what hurts right now, and much less so at telling us what they are going to need in six months to a year from now. That's where you'll come in. You will spend a lot of your time sitting between engineering and customer success, pulling everything together into a roadmap the team believes in, and then staying with it until it's shipped and people are actually using it.

We think of this as a revenue generating role. What you choose to build determines which deals we can win and which customers grow with us, and you will be measured on that alongside the rest of the go-to-market team.

What You'll Do

- Own the voice AI product end to end, from the first customer conversation through launch, adoption, and iteration
- Talk to customers constantly. Sit on calls, read transcripts, dig through tickets and feature requests, and use that evidence to decide what deserves to get built
- Translate what customer success and sales are hearing into a roadmap with clear priorities and tradeoffs
- Work shoulder to shoulder with engineering and design through the whole build
- Define what success looks like before you ship and then go check whether you were right
- Partner with sales, marketing, and customer success on positioning, launches, and enablement so the thing you built actually gets used
- Build the product function itself: how we prioritize, how we document, how we run launches, and how we measure what worked
- Argue with us. You will be working alongside people who have strong opinions of their own, so bring one, back it with evidence, change your mind when someone has a better one, and then commit
- Set the vision for where the product goes over the next year and make the case for it

What You'll Bring

- At least three years in product management, including something you took from a vague idea all the way to a product people love
- Experience owning a real business outcome and comfort being measured on it
- Exceptional organization and follow-through
- Excellent writing and communication. You are the connective tissue between engineers, customer success, sales, and the founders, and most of that job is making complicated things clear to people who are not in the weeds with you
- Enough technical fluency that you can talk with engineers about APIs, latency, and model behavior

Bonus Points

- You have shipped AI or LLM-based products into production
- You have worked closely with a customer success or support team before
- You know the world of call centers, contact centers, or high volume phone operations
- You have been the first PM somewhere and have opinions about what you would do differently the second time

Why Join Phonely

We are a team of ex-athletes, founders, and builders who are deeply passionate about the problem we're solving. We're a curious, driven, low ego group that finds joy in hard challenges. As we grow the team, we are being extremely intentional about the culture we're building. We care far less about a person's pedigree than we do seeking out smart people with grit and genuine kindness. If this resonates with you, please reach out!

Also we have some nice benefits:

- Full health and dental coverage
- 401k with 4% match
- Unlimited PTO
- Meaningful equity
- Wellness stipend
- Race/tournament stipend (so you can go compete in cool stuff!)
- Breakfast, lunch, and dinner provided
- Annual offsites in fun locations (costa rica, the rockies)

Interview Process

1. Fifteen minute intro call to see if there's a fit
2. A deeper conversation about your product experience with someone on the team
3. A case study where we hand you a real problem off our roadmap and you walk through how you would approach it with one of our engineers and customer success managers
4. Final conversation with leadership

ABOUT OVERVIEW.AI http://Overview.ai

Overview.ai http://Overview.ai brings the cutting edge of AI computer vision to manufacturing, solving inspection problems that traditional machine vision could not handle. We build GPU-powered smart cameras, deploy them on production lines around the world, and operate the platform that keeps those fleets running.

Our customers love the product because it works: high accuracy, fast deployment, and an operator-friendly experience that makes real factory rollouts possible (not just pilots).

THE ROLE

As a Junior IIoT Engineer, you will help bring our systems live at customer sites: connecting smart cameras to line PLCs, building the logic that runs the inspections, and making sure everything runs reliably on the factory floor.

You will be mentored and grow into someone who can own an entire deployment. We provide structured training in Node-RED, camera inspection-recipe building, and English. We do not expect you to master these tools on day one, but we do expect you to already have a solid industrial-field foundation (see Requirements), which we build on to make you a fully capable engineer.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

DEPLOYMENT AND COMMISSIONING

 - Deploy and commission Overview.ai http://Overview.ai vision-inspection systems on customer production lines, on-site.

 - Create and tune camera inspection recipes for each product (regions of interest, models, pass/fail criteria).

 - Set up and troubleshoot on-site: cameras, industrial networking and switches, and connectivity issues, using our existing internal diagnostic tools.

INTEGRATION

 - Build and maintain integration logic in Node-RED (data flow between cameras, PLCs, HMIs, and dashboards).

 - Integrate cameras with factory PLCs over I/O, EtherNet/IP, and Profinet: triggering, handshake signals, and result reporting.

CUSTOMER SUPPORT AND TEAMWORK

 - Support customers on-site: basic training, issue resolution, and clear written and photo documentation of each deployment.

 - Work closely with the team, escalating complex problems while steadily taking on more independence.

REQUIREMENTS

 - A diploma or degree in Electrical, Automation, Mechatronics, or a related industrial field. A Computer Science or software background is also fine if paired with hands-on factory experience.

 - A working foundation in industrial fundamentals, which we expect you to have on day one:
 
 - Basic concepts of PLCs and industrial automation (signals, I/O, trigger and handshake logic).
 
 - A basic understanding of common manufacturing processes.
 
 - The ability to read and clarify on-site requirements, turning customer needs into actionable inspection and integration specs.
 
 - Solid troubleshooting instincts: systematically pinpointing what went wrong and why.

 - A strong hands-on drive and problem-solving mindset: you like to dig into why something is not working and fix it.

 - Basic English reading and writing, with a genuine willingness to improve.

 - Able and willing to travel frequently across China and Southeast Asia, with a valid passport.

 - Reliable, communicative, and comfortable working directly in a live factory environment.

NICE TO HAVE (NOT REQUIRED, WE WILL TRAIN YOU)

 - Hands-on experience with specific PLC brands or industrial protocols (Keyence, EtherNet/IP, MQTT, or similar).

 - Any scripting or programming experience (JavaScript, Python), or low-code tools such as Node-RED.

 - Familiarity with machine vision, industrial cameras, or industrial networking.

 - Basic SQL or dashboard tools.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - A clear training path: Node-RED and camera-recipe building training, plus English training by an external instructor (two-year program).

 - On-the-job training and mentorship: you learn by doing on real projects.

 - Fast, real ownership: you will be commissioning live systems at major manufacturers.

 - A growth track from Junior IIoT Engineer to IIoT Engineer to Senior IIoT Engineer.

jobs.title: AI Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT GREENBOARD

At Greenboard, we're building the future of financial compliance. Greenboard is the unified, AI-native compliance operating system for RIAs, fintechs, private funds, hedge funds, and more. It replaces the fragmented mix of legacy tools and automates more than previously possible. By centralizing data and workflows, Greenboard helps firms reduce regulatory risk, simplify their technology stack, modernize how they run compliance, and save money.

Our founding team includes engineers who have scaled products at Amazon, Google, and multiple unicorn startups. We're backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Base10, and other top-tier investors, and have raised over $20M to date. Brand-name financial institutions already rely on Greenboard, and we're growing fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be our first dedicated Automation engineer. Our customers are regulated financial institutions, which means a missed bug is not just a bad user experience. It can mean an incomplete books-and-records archive, a marketing review that never routed for approval, or an attestation that quietly failed to send. Quality is part of the product we sell.

You'll own how we test: the framework, the automated suites, and the release process, built from scratch and then embedded with the engineers who ship. You'll also help us solve something most automation engineers have never had to solve, which is how to test AI systems whose output is not deterministic.

There is no existing playbook here. If you like defining the standard rather than enforcing someone else's, this is the seat.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The foundation. Test framework, automated regression suites, and QA practices built from zero, with your call on tooling

 - The critical paths. Message archiving and supervision, marketing review routing, employee attestations, and audit trails, which are the flows that cannot break

 - Testing the AI. How we evaluate AI-driven detection and review, including golden datasets and quality bars for output that is not deterministic

 - Data integrity at scale. End-to-end validation from ingestion of tens of millions of messages a day through to what a compliance officer sees on screen

 - The release gate. Bug triage, release sign-off, and the definition of deployment-ready at Greenboard

WHO ARE YOU?

 - Love to move fast and build things

 - Looking for deep ownership over the quality of everything we ship

 - Obsess over the customers you're building for

 - An excellent communicator

 - Value collaboration

 - Located in NYC

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years testing software where being wrong has consequences beyond a bad review: fintech, healthtech, payments, or anywhere an audit followed a bug

 - Able to test a system you cannot fully see from the UI. Comfortable with REST APIs and querying the database directly, because verifying a feature here means checking what landed and what the retention policy did with it, not just what rendered

 - Write Playwright or Cypress suites that survive a redesign, with opinions about selectors, fixtures, and what belongs in an integration test versus an end-to-end one

 - Can read a feature spec and name the states nobody thought about: the employee who left mid-attestation, the message that arrives out of order, the marketing piece edited after approval

 - Have held a release before, explained why to someone who wanted it out, and been right

NICE TO HAVE

 - Tested a system where output is not deterministic and had to define correct as a threshold rather than an exact match

 - Worked in a Node JS and React codebase on AWS, or debugged a queue-based ingestion pipeline

 - Been through a SOC 2 audit and know what evidence a test suite can produce for one

 - Sat with a compliance officer, an advisor, or a back-office team and watched them work

 - Interest in the financial industry is a plus, but not necessary

BENEFITS

 - 401(k) with 5% company match

 - Medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - 15 days PTO + 11 company holidays + flexible sick time

 - 2 additional PTO days for each year of service (up to 10 additional days)

 - 10 remote days per year plus additional around the holidays

 - Bi-annual off-sites and team retreats

 - Front-row seat to building the operating backbone of modern finance

jobs.title: Customer Service Associate
jobs.description:
THE PROBLEM

36 million businesses in America need insurance—it's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.

Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflows—by building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.

We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this year—and that's why we're hiring.

Small business owners are used to their insurance broker never calling back. You're the reason ours do.

THE THESIS

Insurance is the one bill a small business owner can't afford to get wrong, and most brokers make them work for it—voicemail, dead ends, a week of silence. Being the opposite of that is a real competitive advantage, and it's the entire point of this team. When someone calls Harper, they reach a person who finds their account, tells them exactly what's happening next, and then makes it happen.

That doesn't come from software. It comes from people who genuinely enjoy this kind of work: fast on the phone, dozens of open threads held in their head, and real satisfaction in taking a full list down to zero. It's a craft, and the people who are great at it become the customer's favorite part of doing business with us. There are real paths from this seat into service, sales, and operations.

THE ROLE

You're on the phone with business owners all day—inbound and outbound—from our office in downtown San Francisco. Two shifts cover the day: an early one for East Coast customers and a later one through the West Coast close. You'll be assigned to one based on business need.

Inbound, you're the first person a customer talks to. You pull up the account, work out what they actually need, and tell them exactly when they'll hear back. Outbound, the list is yours: payments, documents, renewals, and the follow-ups that keep somebody's coverage from lapsing. The volume is real—back-to-back calls and long lists—and the people who love this job love that part.

You don't need an insurance background to start. We'll teach you the systems, the playbooks, and the vocabulary. What we're hiring for is judgment on the phone: hearing the difference between confused and genuinely upset, catching the thing the customer didn't say, and knowing exactly who to pull in when a problem is bigger than the call. Quoting and coverage advice belong to a licensed seller, so you'll never be asked to advise on a policy—everything else, you carry as far as it goes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Pick up and take it personally — You're the first human a business owner reaches; find their account fast, get to the real ask, and tell them precisely when they'll hear back

 - Keep every promise you make — A callback time is a commitment; no customer should ever have to chase Harper to find out what happened

 - Take the list to zero — Payments, documents, at-risk cancellations, renewals; an empty list at the end of your shift is the whole game

 - Chase it like it's yours — Three attempts across three days on a standard follow-up, up to seven touches on a payment issue by phone, text, and email; you stop when it's solved, not when it's hard

 - Own the whole answer — Track down the document, the payment link, or the one person who can unblock it; nothing gets closed just because it got called

 - Leave a clean trail — Log what happened and what's still open, so the next teammate picks up mid-story and the customer never repeats themselves

 - Get the right specialist in fast — Financing, coverage, and genuinely complex problems have owners; pulling them in quickly is part of great service, not a handoff

 - Turn a rough call around — Frustrated customers become the most loyal ones when somebody finally levels with them and delivers

 - Make the next call easier — Spot the same problem happening over and over and flag it, so we fix the cause instead of the symptom

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF...

 - You like talking to people all day and end the day energized by it, not drained

 - You show up on time, every day, and take that seriously

 - You can talk and type at the same time—notes get written while the call is happening

 - You finish what you start; an open item bothers you until it's closed

 - You'd rather ask than guess when you're unsure

 - You're organized enough to work a list of 80 calls without losing your place

 - You're steady with frustrated people

REQUIREMENTS

 - Strong phone communication—clear, professional, patient

 - Basic computer comfort: spreadsheets, email, a phone system, and internal tools

 - Ability to work full-time, Monday–Friday, on-site in downtown San Francisco

 - Reliable attendance and punctuality

 - Legally authorized to work in the United States

NICE TO HAVE

 - Call center, collections, dispatch, front-desk, or high-volume customer service experience

 - Bilingual (Spanish)

 - Any insurance, brokerage, or financial services exposure

 - Experience working from call lists or a CRM

COMPENSATION

 - Pay: $23 - $26/hour

 - Type: Full-time, hourly, non-exempt (W-2)—overtime eligible

 - Location: San Francisco, in-office (425 Market Street)

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, in-office. Early shift (East Coast coverage) or late shift (West Coast coverage), assigned based on business need. Overtime available.

 - Start date: Immediate

BENEFITS

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Commuter benefits

THE PROCESS

 1. Application screen — We review daily and most candidates hear back within 48 hours

 2. Phone screen — Short conversation; we'll listen to how you handle a call

 3. On-site day — Meet the team, see the floor, work through real scenarios

TO APPLY

We need people on the phones now. If you're dependable, good with people, and want steady
