jobs.title: Scriptwriter
jobs.description:
LA MISSION DE FINARY

Notre mission : rendre le pouvoir aux investisseurs. Le bon conseil financier a toujours existé, mais il était réservé à ceux qui dépassaient un certain seuil de patrimoine. Nous changeons la donne en construisant la plateforme d'investissement tout-en-un, propulsée par l'IA : suivre ses actifs, gérer son budget, investir et se former, au même endroit. Une idée simple et ambitieuse nous guide : mettre un banquier privé dans la poche de chacun.

Mounir https://www.linkedin.com/in/mounirlaggoune a lancé Finary en 2021, et plus d'un million de personnes nous confient aujourd'hui leur vie financière. Nous lançons des produits de pointe avec une touche de plaisir, et nous sommes exigeants sur l'expérience, la performance et la simplicité.

 

POURQUOI MAINTENANT ?

Une nouvelle génération d'investisseurs émerge : ambitieuse, impliquée, débarrassée des tabous autour de l'argent. Nous croyons en un monde où investir permet à chacun de vivre la vie dont il a toujours rêvé. Pour accélérer, nous avons levé 40M€ auprès de Hedosophia, Y Combinator et Speedinvest, aux côtés de fondateurs et d'opérateurs comme Steve Anavi et Alexandre Prot (Qonto), Matthieu Rouif (Photoroom), Eric Demuth (Bitpanda), Axel Weber (ancien président d'UBS) et Harsh Sinha (CTO de Wise).

En juillet 2026, l'AMF nous a accordé l'agrément MiCA, qui s'ajoute à notre agrément d'Entreprise d'Investissement : nous sommes l'une des très rares plateformes françaises à détenir les deux, avec actions, ETF et crypto réunis sur une seule plateforme régulée, au moment même où l'Europe se consolide autour des acteurs agréés. Il n'y a jamais eu de meilleur moment pour nous rejoindre.

 

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

Nous sommes 70 builders qui aimons profondément ce que nous faisons : de vraies responsabilités dès le premier jour, un package salaire et equity au meilleur niveau du marché, des bureaux en plein cœur de Paris avec du remote hybride, et des offsites trimestriels qu'on attend vraiment.

Nous recrutons des A-players aussi bienveillants qu'exigeants, des personnes dont les idées transforment notre produit autant que notre façon de travailler et de penser. Notre culture est directe et transparente : on se challenge ouvertement, puis on s'aligne et on exécute. Et sur l'IA, pas de demi-mesure : c'est la compétence la plus importante de la décennie et un vrai critère chez nous. Chacun a repensé sa manière de travailler autour d'elle. Si c'est déjà une seconde nature pour vous, vous trouverez ici des gens qui repoussent cette frontière chaque jour.

Découvrez nos valeurs ici https://app.notion.com/p/About-Finary-2f5919045b5d8060afd1d4e887ac550f?pvs=21.

---

LE POSTE

Finary construit la banque privée de la génération internet. Notre chaîne YouTube est la première chaîne de finances personnelles en France : 880 000 abonné·es et 5 à 10 millions de vues par mois, entièrement produite en interne par une équipe qui traite le contenu comme un produit, c’est-à-dire mesuré, itéré, conçu avec méthode.

Tu prends en charge tout ce qui s’écrit chez Finary Media, de bout en bout : recherche, script, packaging, vérification des faits, livraison. Les mots t’appartiennent, de la première idée au montage final.

Tes deux terrains de jeu principaux :

 - La chaîne YouTube Finary. Des vidéos longues qui mêlent storytelling, économie et investissement, regardées par des centaines de milliers de personnes. Ton point de repère : nos meilleures vidéos dépassent le million de vues.

 - Finary One. Le contenu de notre offre de gestion de patrimoine, destiné à des investisseur·ses averti·es disposant de plus d’un million d’euros de patrimoine. C’est l’écriture aux enjeux les plus élevés chez Finary : moins de vues, mais des conséquences bien plus importantes.

Tu écris aussi pour tous les formats qui gravitent autour : la préparation du podcast Finary Talk, et tout ce qui a besoin de mots. Si c’est écrit et que ça compte, c’est pour toi.

Deux éléments distinguent ce poste de tout autre métier de scénariste :

 - Tu passes devant la caméra. Tu présentes toi-même tes scripts. Ce n’est pas une option, cela fait partie du métier ici.

 - Tu travailles nativement avec l’IA. Notre système de production repose sur des workflows LLM, des skills sur mesure et de l’automatisation. Tu ne te contenteras pas d’utiliser ces outils, tu construiras les tiens. La personne idéale pour ce poste a déjà construit des choses : prompts, agents, bases de connaissances, petits scripts.

À QUOI RESSEMBLE LA RÉUSSITE

 - Une de tes vidéos dépasse le million de vues dans tes trois premiers mois

 - À partir du troisième mois, ton contenu Finary One génère 100 M€ d’encours prospects chaque mois

 - 90 % de tes scripts sont validés en un seul tour de relecture, et tes délais de production baissent

TU ES FAIT·E POUR CE POSTE SI TU AS

 - Une maîtrise experte de l’investissement et des finances personnelles : tu peux aller en profondeur, sans notes, sur le private equity, l’immobilier, les enveloppes fiscales et la structuration patrimoniale

 - Une expérience d’écriture éprouvée face à un vrai public (YouTube, presse, newsletter, blog), avec des résultats à montrer

 - Une rigueur factuelle sans faille : aucune erreur de données, de chiffres ou de concepts, jamais

 - La concision comme réflexe, à l’écrit comme à l’oral

 - Une autonomie totale : tu gères ton propre système, tu tiens tes délais, et personne n’a besoin de te relancer

 - Une pratique native de l’IA : tu construis avec les LLM et l’automatisation parce que c’est ta façon de penser

 - De l’aisance face caméra, ou l’envie d’y arriver vite

LES PLUS

 - Tu as écrit pour des chaînes YouTube performantes, ou tu as la tienne

 - Un parcours en finance, en gestion d’actifs ou dans la fintech

 - Tu as mené seul·e un petit projet de code, une skill Claude ou un pipeline d’automatisation

Entretiens

Les entretiens avec les candidat·es francophones se déroulent en français. En tant qu’entreprise internationale, nous

AfterQuery https://www.afterquery.com/ is an applied research lab curating data solutions for foundation model development. We serve every frontier AI lab with the mission of delivering the best data to power the best models. In doing so, we can make expertise that once took a lifetime to build available to anyone who needs it. 

Our customers are the ones building the foundation models themselves and our work sits directly in the loop of how those systems improve. This is a rare opportunity to join a company at a defining moment in AI. Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation. We're based in San Francisco and backed by leading investors including Altos Ventures, BoxGroup, and Y Combinator and angels from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and Microsoft AI.

WHY APPLY

Massive Opportunity: Forbes reported that we could be YC's fastest unicorn, reportedly raising at a $3.2 billion valuation, and we're not slowing down.

Founding Impact: You will own and architect core infrastructure systems that power our platform from the ground up.

Equity & Growth: Competitive salary and meaningful equity. As we scale, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the engineering organization and lead major technical initiatives.

Strong Team: Our founding team has experience from Citadel Securities, Meta, Google, Silver Lake, and Morgan Stanley — work alongside world-class engineers and researchers.

OVERVIEW

The world's leading AI labs are racing to build smarter models and the data behind them is the bottleneck. We're looking for a Project Manager to sit at that bottleneck: managing expert teams, shaping dataset specs, and driving high-stakes projects from scoping to delivery for the organizations building the frontier.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Project and client management: Work with the world’s leading AI organizations to build next-generation data solutions that push the limits of model capability, while directly driving revenue.

 - Manage expert teams across domains: Lead and coordinate highly specialized contributors across fields like finance, software engineering, law, and more to create high-quality outputs at scale.

 - Shape how AI systems are trained: Design dataset specifications that directly influence how frontier models are evaluated and improved. Your taste and judgement will shape what foundation models become.

 - Drive high-impact execution end-to-end: Own critical projects from idea to delivery. From scoping, executing, iterating, and shipping in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment, you will touch it all.

 - Gain top tier operational experience: Support the team across a range of operational initiatives that will directly contribute to the future of AfterQuery. You will work across multiple parts of the business in the same week, ranging from building, analyzing, coordinating, and executing where needed most.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of experience at a top-tier management consulting firm (MBB or similar), Big 4 strategy practice, or corporate strategy team

 - Background in business strategy, case analysis, market research, or corporate operations

 - Strong grasp of structured problem-solving, business frameworks, and financial/quantitative analysis

 - High agency and strong work ethic; comfort defining problems and thriving with minimal direction in ambiguous situations

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARTIE

Artie is a fully-managed real-time data streaming platform that replicates production databases into data warehouses and lakes - in real time, with zero maintenance. We make high-volume data replication simple, reliable, and scalable for engineering teams.

Our platform powers mission-critical use cases including fraud and risk monitoring, inventory visibility, customer-facing analytics, and AI/ML workloads.

We’re trusted by teams like Substack, Alloy, and ClickUp, and raised a Series A from top-tier investors including Standard Capital, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Pathlight, and the founders of Dropbox and Mode.

Artie is built for engineers who care about performance, reliability, and operational simplicity - and we’re growing fast.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Solutions Engineer to help scale Artie's pre-sales and post-sales enterprise motion.

This is not a demo-delivery role. You'll go deep with customers on their data architectures, run tight proof-of-value engagements, and be the technical backbone of every enterprise deal. You'll work directly with founders, shape how we position Artie technically, and set the bar for how we win.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the technical win

 - Run structured proof-of-value engagements with clear technical success criteria and mutual action plans

 - Partner with AEs to drive deals forward — from technical discovery through close

 - Be the trusted technical voice in the room with staff engineers, data architects, and platform leads

Go deep on customer architectures

 - Understand how customers move data today — their databases, pipelines, cloud and on-premise infrastructure, and pain points

 - Map those architectures to Artie's capabilities with clarity and confidence (CDC, Kafka, cloud data warehouses, replication patterns)

 - Whiteboard solutions and guide customers through integration design

Deliver compelling technical presentations

 - Translate complex technical concepts — log-based CDC, schema evolution, real-time replication — into business impact

 - Present to mixed audiences: engineers who want to see under the hood and executives who care about TCO and reliability

Be a product and GTM force multiplier

 - Surface field insights to Product and Engineering to sharpen our roadmap

 - Solve many of the manual workflows with AI, constant thought about increasing productivity.

 - Work closely with Engineering post-sale to ensure seamless customer handoffs and support

 - Help define what great looks like for SE at Artie
 
 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience as a Solutions Engineer or Sales Engineer in enterprise or similarly complex environments

 - Deep familiarity with at least one RDBMS (Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, DB2) — you've done basic troubleshooting, understand logging/archiving, and aren't afraid of a query plan

 - Working knowledge of at least one cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, Iceberg, Databricks, Redshift)

 - Comfortable in the data stack — you know where tools like Kafka, dbt, and BI platforms fit and why customers use them

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and enough networking knowledge to hold your own in a technical solutioning conversation

 - Strong communicator — you can adjust depth and frame for a data engineer and a VP of Engineering in the same meeting

 - Structured and rigorous — you run POCs like a project, not a hope

 - Low ego, high curiosity — you'd rather understand the customer's real problem than pitch a canned demo
 
 

TECH STACK YOU'LL WORK WITH

AWS, GCP, Azure, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Kafka, DataDog, RDBMSs (Oracle, SQL Server, DB2, PostgreSQL)

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base $125k - $140k

 - OTE: $175k - $200k

 - Competitive equity package

 - Healthcare, 401(k), unlimited PTO

 - Lunch & dinner provided

 - Visa sponsorship available

jobs.title: Software Engineer, GTM
jobs.description:
THE REALITY

This is a software engineering role that happens to point straight at revenue. You'll write and ship production code, own the systems you build, and be measured by whether the revenue engine runs better because of your work. If your background is engineering that never got to touch the business, this is the role where it finally does. If it's been RevOps where you were quietly the most technical person in the org and nobody ever let you build properly, same.

We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. A company moving this fast catches its own mistakes sooner with the whole team in one room, thinking out loud at a whiteboard.

This will probably be one of the harder jobs you've had. It should also be one of the more interesting ones, because the revenue problems you'll be solving here will be the catalyst for our continued hyper growth.

Excited? Good, we are too!

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales, built across Hyperbound Practice (AI roleplay), Hyperbound Perform (real call scoring and coaching), and Kota, our AI agent that acts on what we find. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.

Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23), we're around 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

THE ROLE

You'll build the systems the go-to-market org runs on: lead routing and enrichment, pipeline and forecasting tooling, scoring and deal-desk workflows, and the data layer that ties it all into one source of truth. This is production engineering: services and code you own, integrated across our CRM, product, and billing data, built to hold up as we scale. Where a no-code tool is genuinely the right call, use it; the bar is that you can build the real thing when that's what the job needs.

There's a part of this job most GTM engineers never get. You'll dogfood Hyperbound on Hyperbound: our own reps run on Practice, Perform, and Kota, so the internal systems you build plug straight into the product we sell, and what you learn building them feeds back into the roadmap. You'll work closely with the founders and GTM leadership, act as part engineer and part systems designer for the revenue org, and have real say in what we build, not just how.

THE TEAM

We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and hunters. We've hired from our competition, brought on former founders, and pulled in early customers who loved the product enough to come build it.

You can feel it when a team actually believes in what it's building, and that's very real here. It's also not a mattress-under-your-desk startup: plenty of people have kids, people leave to make dinner, and they come back the next morning and ship. High standards don't require burnout.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/dc682caf-65e4-456d-8c74-c4a052bd4d85/b05f6011-142d-432f-a5ef-0f52cc293269/team%20jd.png]

We've doubled in size since this photo was taken a few months ago

When we close a real milestone we celebrate for real; after our Series A we took the whole team to Bali.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/dc682caf-65e4-456d-8c74-c4a052bd4d85/4d201e55-fdb6-4e02-a0c6-951c71f1901f/bali.jpg]

OWNERSHIP AND EQUITY

You own the outcome end to end: the systems you build, the revenue they move, and everything that happens after they ship. No process shields you from the responsibility, and none of it shields you from the credit either. Equity here is real, with real secondary opportunities, and we want the people who build this early to end up meaningfully rewarded for it.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Compensation: $160K-$200K+ based on experience + equity

Benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401k

Unlimited PTO

Commuter benefits

Paid lunch and dinner in the office

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Intro call with James, Recruiter (30 min)

 - Call with Sai, Co-Founder (30 min)

 - Take home exercise (1-3 hours)

 - Take home exercise review (45 min)

 - Final onsite with team (60 min)

We move fast, 1-2 week from first conversation to offer.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Hyperbound is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, and we don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
THE REALITY

You'll be closing $100K–$500K+ ACV deals, getting your own calls scored by our own product in the process, in a room where the founders can see the pipeline move in real time.

There's no fully built enterprise playbook waiting for you here. You'll write it as you go: how we handle multi-stakeholder buying committees, how outbound scales past founder-led sales, what a repeatable six-figure deal actually looks like at Hyperbound. If you want a seat that's already been shaped for you, this isn't it. If you've been the person quietly building the playbook other reps just follow, this is that room, finally with your name on it.

The upside: real ACVs, real ownership over how enterprise sales gets built here, and a direct line to the people making product and GTM calls. Close a deal and the whole building knows by lunch.

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales. We invented AI sales roleplay, and we've built past it: Hyperbound Practice, Hyperbound Perform, and Kota, our AI agent, work together to close the loop between behavior, coaching, and execution. As we put it internally, we don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.

Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23), we've raised $18M total, including a $15M Series A led by Peak XV Partners. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

THE ROLE

You'll own full-cycle enterprise deals at Hyperbound, from first contact to signed contract, closing $100K–$500K+ ACV agreements across a roughly even mix of inbound and outbound. You'll build and run your own outbound motion, not just work leads that land in your inbox, and navigate the multi-stakeholder buying committees that come with selling into enterprise sales orgs.

You'll also help build the sales motion itself. We're pre-Series B, so a good amount of what a "normal" playbook looks like here still gets written by the people running the deals, including you. Expect travel for conferences and customer on-sites when it accelerates or closes a deal, and expect to work directly with founders and GTM leadership on strategy, not just deal reviews.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Close enterprise deals ranging from $100K to multiple six figures ACV, split roughly evenly between inbound and outbound

 - Source your own pipeline and build outbound motions that scale beyond you

 - Shape sales playbooks and GTM strategy as we build toward Series B

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years of total closing experience, including 2+ years in enterprise sales

 - A track record of sourcing your own pipeline and running full-cycle enterprise deals

 - Comfort building in ambiguity: you've helped design sales playbooks, not just followed them

 - Strong executive presence and the ability to navigate complex buying committees

 - A bias toward ownership: you want high impact and you're not waiting to be handed a playbook

BONUS POINTS

 - Prior startup, founder, or high-growth (Series A to B) experience

 - Experience selling into sales or revenue orgs

 - Familiarity with AI or sales tech categories

THE TEAM

We're building a cracked GTM team of hunters. Many of the people here are former co founders. Early customers have joined us. We've even hire people from our competition. 

You'll work closely with Isaac (VP Sales), and the founders directly, not through three layers of management.

Speed at the kernel layer is only worth what we do with it though and our enterprise offering promises we'll turn a customer's dataset into a specialist model in days. To do that we run SFT, RL, DPO, design evals and distillation down to smaller and edge-deployable models. We're hiring a Member of Technical Staff to own the modeling side of that end to end.

The infrastructure you'll be working on top of is unusually strong, which is the only reason we're able to train models so fast. Every experiment goes through Model Foundry, which let's you run experiments on the best hardware, look at overviews or dive deep into any detail all in a versioned and reproducible manner, making it trivial to reuse and modify recipes.  - You'll own the post-training pipeline end-to-end: data curation, SFT, preference optimization, RL, evals, distillation and finally deployment

 - You'll build an eval harness trustworthy enough to make a ship/no-ship call within a short window, especially where the target is subjective taste rather than a scored benchmark

 - You'll structure and generate datasets, including synthetic data pipelines, from whatever the customer actually has

 - You'll distill specialist models down into smaller models

 - You'll drive the time-to-model, which means finding what's actually on the critical path and removing it, run after run

 - Someone who's comfortable owning data: curation, filtering, labeling workflows and synthetic generation

 - Someone proficient in PyTorch or JAX

 - Someone willing to sit with customers' domain experts to turn their intuition into a reward function

NICE TO HAVE

 - Someone who's worked on RL infrastructure at scale: rollout engines, distributed training or throughput debugging

 - Someone with experience in distillation, quantization and speculative decoding

 - Someone who's post-trained for agents and tool use

 - Someone who's been forward-deployed or has customer-facing engineering experience

It needs to run three things: (1) our compiler measures every candidate program inside it, so a noisy or unfair sandbox directly corrupts the reward signal the search learns from, (2) our own post-training runs inside it (e.g., when we RL a model on AMD kernel engineering, every rollout is in a sandbox) and (3) customer workloads that require isolation, such as their RL rollouts, run on it too.

We already do this on NVIDIA and AMD, including having rolled AMD GPU support in gVisor from scratch https://x.com/BenKoska/status/2086211029713965099. The work now is depth and breadth, adding support for more vendors, higher fidelity instrumentation, faster cold starts and more features. A lot of our sandboxes need to run on spot pools without losing works, they can span multiple GPUs and sometimes multiple nodes, they need to survive failure and preemption as well as live-migration (which our stack does while keeping sockets intact so that instances can relocate mid-flight while still streaming data in or out without a hiccup).

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - You'll extend our sandboxing stack to new vendors and accelerators

 - You'll build and maintain GPU virtualization below the runtime, including gVisor work at the driver and ioctl level

 - You'll make sandboxes first-class citizens on spot capacity, which means preemption-aware scheduling, checkpointing and rescheduling

 - You'll support multi-GPU and multi-node sandboxes, including the interconnect (NVLink, NVSwitch) and RDMA paths (InfiniBand, RoCE) paths those require

 - You'll own live migration end-to-end, including our socket-preserving migration

 - You'll guarantee measurement and profiling fidelity as well as their isolation

 - You'll work directly with the compiler, post-training and kernel teams to ensure their throughput is not capped by sandboxes

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Someone with strong low-level systems engineering background: Linux kernel internals, containers, namespaces, cgroups, syscall interception or hypervisors

 - Someone with experience in GPU systems engineering: drivers, runtimes or scheduling on accelerator fleets

 - Someone comfortable with distributed systems failure modes: preemption, partial failure, checkpoint/restore and dealing with states you can't afford to loose

 - Someone proficient in Go, C/C++ or Rust

 - Someone with a strong bias toward building the thing yourself when no vendor supports what you need

NICE TO HAVE

 - Someone who's worked directly with gVisor, Firecracker, Kata, QEMU/KVM or similar

 - Someone who's worked directly on CRIU, -live migration or connection-preserving failover work

 - Someone familiar with NCCL/RCCL, RDMA, InfiniBand or vendor interconnects

 - Someone who's run large fleets on spot or other preemptible capacity

 - Someone familiar with bare-metal provisioning, hypervisors or fleet management at scale

 - Someone with a security background in isolation boundaries and untrusted code execution

WHY JOIN US

Most "serverless GPU" products stop at running a container on a GPU. Our's runs arbitrary code across four vendors, on spot capacity, across multiple nodes with migration that keeps live sockets open and timings clean enough to use as an RL reward. It's a hard systems problem and it's directly load-bearing, because the faster and more reliable the sandboxes, the more programs our compiler can search and the faster our models train the same week.

We're a small team operating at frontier scale. We pre-trained foundation models on 4,000 AMD GPUs as a team of three, designed and brought up GB300 NVL72 clusters and designed a TOP500 supercomputer.

We believe that hard problems get solved in person and most of our work happens at our office in San Francisco. We offer relocation assistance and, where possible, we'd like you her

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARINI

Arini is building the single platform to run all healthcare operations.

Healthcare has spent the last decade consolidating under large enterprises, but operations are still fragmented, manual, and expensive. A large group runs dozens of disconnected systems for scheduling, billing, insurance, accounts payable, and reporting, with people moving data between them by phone, fax, and spreadsheet.

Outpatient healthcare is a $650 billion market, and almost every dollar of it still runs on manual work. Consolidators bought thousands of clinics on the promise that scale would expand margins and lift their EBITDA multiple. Scale alone has not delivered it. Automation is now the only way to hit the numbers they promised investors, and Arini is how they get there.

We partner with some of the largest healthcare enterprises in the country, covering thousands of clinics and billions of dollars in annual revenue. We ship the systems that run their operations end to end, and the best of that work becomes the platform that scales across enterprises.

When operations run themselves, patients feel it: calls answered on the first ring, appointments booked in seconds, insurance sorted before they walk in, and clinicians who spend their day on care instead of paperwork. That is what we are building, for every clinic in the country.

We are backed by Y Combinator (W24) and on track to grow more than tenfold in 2026.

THE TEAM

Everyone at Arini ships code, including operators, growth, and customer leads. Our founders, Rami and Abdul, have worked together for over a decade. Rami studied computer science at MIT, Abdul at Harvard.

Everyone carries more than one job, and nobody has time for work that does not matter. If AI can do it, a person should not be doing it. We move extremely fast, take extreme ownership.

THE ROLE

You will build the platform that runs operations for the largest healthcare enterprises in the country. Our forward deployed engineers find the problems inside each customer. You build the systems that solve them once and run them everywhere: the integrations into practice management, billing, and payment systems, the agents that do the work, the data layer that makes an operation legible, and the infrastructure that keeps all of it running across thousands of clinics.

You own modules end to end: design, build, deploy, operate. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build the modules that run operations: scheduling, patient communication, insurance, accounts payable, reporting, and more.

 - Build integrations into enterprise healthcare systems: practice management, billing, payments, and vendors with no APIs.

 - Build and operate AI agents in production, with the evaluation, guardrails, and observability that let them take on work that matters.

 - Design the data models and pipelines that let an operation spanning thousands of locations be queried, monitored, and acted on.

 - Own reliability. You are on call for what you build, you find the root cause when it breaks.

FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Day 30: work alongside the engineer who owns a product line, and ship into it.

 - Day 60: write the plan for how you will own and build out a vertical of your own (e.g., insurance verification, outbound campaigns, etc.).

 - Day 90: own a product line end to end.

WHO YOU ARE

 - A strong generalist. You move between backend services, data, and the interfaces operators use. We work mostly in Python and TypeScript, on AWS and Cloudflare.

 - You have shipped and operated systems in production, and you have opinions about what went wrong and why.

 - You build with AI every day and expect the same from the people around you. If a model can do it, you do not do it by hand.

BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary with meaningful equity

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Lunch and dinner in the office

 - Unlimited PTO

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
We’re probably not the right fit for you.

THE REALITY

We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. We move fast and expect a lot. We’re most effective when everyone is in the same room, thinking out loud, catching each other's mistakes early.

You'll own your models end to end, training through production. We trust you to handle that. You'll spend most of your time working fine-tuning and running open source models in production, pushing models on-device, and building the evaluation frameworks that tell us whether a change actually worked instead of trusting our gut.

This will probably be one of the hardest jobs you've had. We think it'll also be one of the more exciting ones, and we'll be here right alongside you.

Sound exciting? Good. We’re excited too.

WHAT WE'RE BUILDING

Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform, the agentic operating system for sales. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next, turning real selling behavior into targeted roleplays, coaching, and workflow changes that make reps better without adding a single layer of management overhead.

Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23), we're 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

THE ROLE

You'll build and ship the models underneath Hyperbound's roleplay, scoring, and coaching products: real systems sitting on real sales calls. That means owning the full lifecycle, from training and fine-tuning through getting a model into production and keeping it working once it's there.

You will fine-tune and deploy open source models where they give us more control over cost, latency, or what the model can actually do. Some of it means getting models running on-device, wherever a customer's latency or privacy requirements demand it, with all the tradeoffs around quantization and distillation that come with it. And a good amount of it means building the evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and regression suites that tell us whether a change actually made things better, before a customer finds out for us.

You'll work closely with the founders and the rest of engineering, and you'll have real input into what we build next, not just how we build it.

THE TEAM

We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and hunters. We've hired people from our competition, former co-founders, and early customers who loved the product.

The engineers you'd work alongside are builders first. Some have started their own companies. Nobody here is precious about their code, and nobody hides behind "that's not my problem," people just see something broken and fix it.

We work hard and we celebrate for real. We’re demoing features we shipped that morning, and the whiteboards get erased and rewritten constantly. You can feel it when a team actually believes in what it's building, and that's very real here. Here's the team in Bali after we raised our Series A:

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/dc682caf-65e4-456d-8c74-c4a052bd4d85/6bbff623-0db9-4789-85c1-62038d005f9f/bali.jpg]

At the same time, this isn't a mattress-under-your-desk startup: plenty of people here have kids, people leave to make dinner, and they come back the next morning and ship. High standards don't require burnout.

We've doubled in size since this photo was taken a few months ago:

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/dc682caf-65e4-456d-8c74-c4a052bd4d85/23f0f291-c351-4ce4-ae7d-d662040fd951/image_large.png]

OWNERSHIP AND EQUITY

You own your models end to end: the training, the eval, the deployment, and everything that happens after. That cuts both ways, and when it works, that's yours too. Equity here is real, with real secondary opportunities, and we genuinely want the people who build this early to end up meaningfully rewarded for it.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Comp: $260k-$300k+ based on experience, meaningful equity 

Benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401k

Commuter and parking benefits

Unlimited PTO

Free lunch and dinner in the office

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

We move fast: an intro call, a technical conversation with the team you'd actually work with, and a final conversation with the founders. We move fast, 1-2 weeks from first conversation to offer.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Hyperbound is an equal opportunity employer. At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.

 - Owning the cash position and treasury strategy — cash flow forecasting, working capital, FX management, and structuring how we hold company funds to earn a sensible return without taking risk we shouldn’t

 - Managing our outsourced bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners — holding them to deadlines and quality, and pulling work in-house where doing so makes us faster

 - Owning the finance tech stack and having a strong opinion on it, actively replacing manual work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across reconciliations, invoice processing, variance analysis, and reporting drafts

 - AI-native in your approach — you already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and can talk specifically about what you’ve automated and what it saved you

 - Exceptional attention to detail, alongside the judgement to know when precision matters and when speed does

 - A clear communicator — you can explain a number to a non-finance audience without patronising them or losing them

 - Ideally, SaaS or subscription business experience, particularly ARR reporting and deferred revenue, and familiarity with modern billing infrastructure like Xero or Stripe

jobs.title: GTM Engineer – Revenue Systems
jobs.description:
ABOUT WARP

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.

About the Role

We're looking for our first GTM Engineer to build the operational layer our entire revenue motion runs on. You'll own how our GTM stack is designed, connected, and scaled, from Salesforce architecture to the automation and AI layers on top of it. This is a high-impact IC role where you'll pioneer the GTM Engineering function at Warp, working directly with tenured GTM leaders who give you the context to build well and the independence to decide how.

GTM Engineering is an emerging discipline that blends software operations principles, Salesforce development, and systems design. We're looking for someone excited to build this function from the ground up and treat our GTM stack as a product that needs to be engineered, maintained, and improved over time.

What You'll Own

 - Revenue systems: Build the operational layer the whole revenue motion runs on, from Salesforce architecture to the automation and AI layers on top of it

 - Salesforce build: Design and build objects, flows, validation rules, reports, and dashboards that support GTM teams across the company

 - Cross-functional building: Serve as the primary Salesforce builder for Sales, Tech Partnerships, CX, Finance, and more, translating process needs into technical solutions

 - Workflow redesign: Partner with GTM leaders and frontline teams to understand how the revenue motion works today and where it breaks, then redesign and automate those workflows with better systems design and AI (ergo, cedar, sumble, gumloop, clay, claude)

 - Agentic systems: Build agents that run parts of the revenue motion, not just automate steps in it

 - Commissions and incentives: Build the systems that run commissions and incentive calculation, so payouts are accurate and questions resolve without manual digging

 - Data quality: Build the validation, governance, and structure that the rest of the GTM stack can rely on

 - Systems integration: Connect Salesforce to adjacent systems through APIs, webhooks, and automation layers, and own the GTM tooling that runs on top of it, adding and integrating new systems as the stack evolves

 - Reporting infrastructure: Build the reporting and forecasting infrastructure GTM leaders use to plan, so pipeline and revenue data is clean and trustworthy by design

 - Documentation and enablement: Document and enable what you build so the rest of the org can trust and extend it, not route through you

 - Build for scale: Design for where we're going, not one-off fixes, as we bring our org from 30 sellers to 100+

What We're Looking For

 - 2-5 years in Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, or Sales Ops at a B2B SaaS company

 - Hands-on Salesforce experience: building within it, not just configuring it (Flow, custom objects, validation rules, reports, dashboards)

 - Familiarity with GTM tech stack (Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Apollo, Chili Piper, Sales Navigator)

 - Track record of building processes and systems from scratch in a fast-growth environment

 - Strong attention to detail: data quality issues are painful for customers and for us

 - Comfortable working autonomously and making decisions with limited oversight

 - Proficiency in Google Sheets/Excel. Can juggle multiple workstreams, keep projects moving, and translate messy data into clear insights

Nice to Have

 - Hands-on ability with APIs, webhooks, and cross-system workflow design

 - Experience building in Clay, or with AI automation tooling (ergo, cedar, sumble, gumloop, claude)

 - Ability to build and problem solve with Python, JavaScript, SQL, SOQL, or TypeScript

 - Experience with business intelligence tools and SQL

 - Experience building and maintaining pipeline/forecast reporting for GTM leaders

 - Salesforce Administrator or Developer certification

BENEFITS AT WARP: 

 - 100% Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents.

 - 401(k) Matching: Start investing in your future from day one.

 - Flexible PTO: We offer uncapped flexible PTO, meaning you’re trusted to take the time you need to recharge while balancing your responsibilities and team commitments.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre-tax commuter benefits for your daily trip to our NYC office.

 - Catered Lunch Daily: Great food, every day, on us. No meal prep, no decision fatigue.

 - Quarterly Offsites: Beautiful locations to connect as a team. Past locations include Spain, Catskills, and San Francisco.

Warp is based in New York City, and most of our team works together in-office 5x per week. Please refer to the top of this page for this position's hiring location and working model.

jobs.title: Founding Engineer
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

Hedge is hiring a founding engineer to build the agents that run an insurance company and the infrastructure that lets them scale. You’ll build systems that read messy submissions, chase missing information, navigate carrier requirements, and move accounts from a broker’s first email toward coverage.

Our agents are already in production, doing real work for paying customers. You’ll push them further: coordinating across carrier systems, recovering when things break, and improving through evals and feedback loops grounded in real outcomes.

You’ll build alongside the founders, inside the operation, with more than 100 insurance market partnerships already in place. The opportunity is to turn the work of placing insurance into software and give a small team the capacity to serve thousands of brokers.

HOW HEDGE STARTED

Luke Rosa and Luke Button worked together launching new markets at Traba, where Rosa built AI agents to manage $20 million in revenue. Buying insurance for Traba’s high-risk operations showed them how slow and manual the industry was.

Button later built Fernstone, an AI-native retail brokerage, and discovered a deeper bottleneck at the wholesale layer: access to carriers and control over the insurance product. They founded Hedge to address it, pairing Rosa’s experience automating operations with Button’s brokerage experience. Starting with wholesale distribution, Hedge is building toward an insurance company that combines distribution and underwriting.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Turn operational work into software. Work alongside brokers and the founders, follow real submissions, and build systems around the details that determine whether an account gets quoted and placed.

 - Productionize and scale the platform. Own architecture, data models, background jobs, integrations, monitoring, and failure recovery. Take responsibility for what happens after a feature ships.

 - Put agents to work in production. Extend agents that handle emails, interpret submissions, gather missing information, prepare documents, and coordinate carrier workflows. Build evals and feedback loops that use real outcomes to improve performance, and own the reliability of the complete workflow.

 - Make messy carrier data usable. Turn PDFs, emails, and API responses into consistent records of coverage, pricing, and outstanding requirements. Catch mistakes before they reach a broker or customer.

 - Connect engineering to business results. Understand how your decisions affect turnaround, conversion, servicing effort, and carrier relationships.

WHO THRIVES HERE

You’re deeply technical, resourceful, and willing to learn the business in detail. You can move from a conversation with a broker to debugging a production failure to making an architecture decision.

We look for:

 - Ownership from zero to one. You’ve taken an unclear problem to working software that people actually use. You can explain what you personally built, the decisions you made, and what happened after launch.

 - Technical depth. You can reason through data integrity, asynchronous workflows, reliability, and scaling. You know how to investigate a system when its behavior surprises you.

 - Exceptional work ethic and grit. When progress stalls, you investigate, find a way forward, and follow through. You’re willing to do the hands-on operational work required to understand and solve the problem.

 - Business judgment. You care whether the software helps people get work done and improves the economics of the business.

 - Speed and initiative. You identify useful work, build a first version, test it with real users, and improve it quickly.

There is no fixed years-of-experience requirement. The bar is high: show us technical depth, substantial ownership, and outsized initiative. Insurance experience is useful, but you can learn it here.

HOW WE WORK

We work seven days a week, with six days together in our San Francisco office. This is a high-intensity environment with fast decisions and substantial individual responsibility.

We use AI heavily for both engineering and production. You’ll have access to the latest frontier models and are expected to use them aggressively. We build prototypes quickly, try different approaches, and use what we learn to decide where to invest. You remain responsible for understanding, testing, and operating what you ship.

COMPENSATION AND OWNERSHIP

$150K–$250K base salary and 1%–3% equity, based on experience and scope. We offer health benefits and substantial responsibility for the company you’re helping build.

jobs.title: Senior Account Executive Defense - Israel
jobs.description:
We’re looking for an Account Executive based in Israel to join our sales team and play a key role in growing Jiga’s defense and aerospace business.

THE OPPORTUNITY IN ISRAEL

Manufacturing capacity is at the centre of the conversation in defense. Demand is surging across defense systems, drones, aerospace, and space, while critical programs still lose valuable time waiting for custom parts.

The capacity exists across Israel and the global supply base. What’s missing is the coordination layer that finds and qualifies the right capacity, removes friction, and moves work across it with the speed, traceability, and accountability these programs require.

Jiga is building that layer. We route demand to the right manufacturers, operate as supplier of record with full traceability, and become a production arm for custom mechanical parts.

ABOUT JIGA

Jiga is the professional manufacturing platform that helps the world's best companies make their products. Companies source the mission-critical parts that help them launch satellites, build robotics, and strengthen national security.

We're a fast-growing Series A, Y Combinator backed company transforming how hardware companies build their supply chains. We have strong and proven product market fit, growing exponentially YoY. Teams at companies like NASA, Collins, Archer and Leidos use our platform to get high-quality custom parts faster.

THE ROLE

You’ll own a portfolio of Israeli defense and aerospace accounts—from defense primes and Tier 2/3 contractors to defense-tech companies. You’ll sell Jiga as a strategic manufacturing solution, including production contracts, capacity agreements, and supplier-of-record relationships, working with the people who own supply chain, procurement, operations, and program delivery.

You’ll build your named-account list, generate your own pipeline, run deals end to end, and work directly with Jiga’s leadership on deal structure and where we invest. Some opportunities will be urgent and high-stakes; others will require a longer enterprise motion. You’ll know how to navigate both while building trust and durable customer relationships.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a book of strategic Israeli defense and aerospace accounts end to end, from the first conversation to a signed contract and account expansion.

 - Sell Jiga as a solution to programs through production contracts, capacity agreements, and supplier-of-record relationships.

 - Navigate the Israeli defense ecosystem. Understand who holds budget and influence at primes, Tier 2/3 contractors, and defense-tech companies, how sourcing decisions are made, and how to get in the room.

 - Travel to defense industry events and customer sites to build relationships with supply chain, procurement, operations, and program leaders.

 - Understand each customer’s manufacturing and program-delivery challenges, demonstrate how Jiga solves them, and structure the right commercial solution.

 - Shape deal structure with leadership and help decide where Jiga should invest resources and capabilities.

 - Guide customers through their first orders and ensure a smooth onboarding experience.

 - Bring market insight back into the company and collaborate with marketing, supply chain, and product to improve our offering and customer experience.

YOU’RE A FIT IF YOU

 - Bring a strong, active network in Israel’s defense and aerospace ecosystem. You already know decision-makers across supply chain, procurement, operations, and program leadership—and can name the accounts you would open first.

 - Have 10+ years selling into or operating inside aerospace and defense manufacturing, including experience with primes, Tier 2/3 contractors, or defense-tech companies.

 - Have a demonstrated track record of closing complex, high-value production contracts or enterprise deals, and can explain exactly how you moved them from first conversation to signature.

 - Speak shop floor and quality requirements fluently: CNC machining, injection moulding, DFM, tolerances, materials, AS9100, first articles, traceability, source approval, and export-control requirements.

 - Generate your own pipeline. You’re comfortable building an account book without relying on inbound leads or heavy marketing support.

 - Are a go-getter with a “hunter” mentality - you’re comfortable doing outbound.

 - Are deeply service-oriented - you care about the customer's success as much as the sale.

 - Are a great communicator who knows how to build trust and follow through.

 - Can manage yourself, your time, and your pipeline with minimal supervision.

 - Are excited about being part of a fast-moving startup.

 - Communicate professionally in both Hebrew and English.

 - Are based in Israel and able to travel regularly to customer sites and industry events.

 - Relevant security clearance or experience in program-sensitive environments is a plus.

 - Are tech-savvy and comfortable working in remote environments (Slack, Notion, Loom, etc.)

THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF

 - Most of your experience is in short, transactional sales cycles and you haven’t owned complex enterprise deals.

 - Your background is limited to government capture or program-office relationships without closing commercial supply-chain or production agreements.

 - You need a mature company brand or inbound pipeline to create opportunities.

 - You’re looking primarily for a management title or a team to lead. This is a hands-on selling role.
 
 

OUR CULTURE

We’re a remote-first company. We don’t count hours; we measure performance. We trust our team to deliver, encourage hard questions, and avoid micromanagement and unproductive meetings.

We play online games together and bring the entire company together once a year for a week-long offsite in a beautiful location.

 - Ownership - Build pipeline and close deals with full autonomy

jobs.title: Research Scientist
jobs.description:
About idler

idler is a frontier data research lab. We build the evals and environments that the world's leading frontier labs use to measure and train their models.

After raising a $9m seed round led by Paradigm, we spent the last year developing coding evals for top coding models you know and love. At the same time, we've expanded into other domains besides coding: RSI & Auto-Research, Law, Enterprise Business, Cybersecurity, and others. Now, we are facing more lab demand for our data than we can serve, and are rapidly scaling the team to grow the business.

Our approach to creating training data scales using technology, and all of our data products are built on a unified self-reinforcing platform that learns through experience.

You would be joining a close-knit team that has reached product market fit, and your work would directly help to multiply our revenue.

You can see some of our work here: https://idler.ai/collections

About the role

As a Research Scientist at idler, you'll own measuring and improving how models learn from our tasks. The job is to maximize learning signal we produce per unit time. You'll draw on your own experience and collaborate with researchers at the frontier to validate our data quality, identify where improvements are needed, and create new datasets. To succeed, you'll need to have extensive experience doing this work in production at a frontier lab.

Examples of what you’ll do

 - Work with our customers — researchers at frontier labs — to design novel post-training recipes and data quality measurement techniques

 - Design and run our in-house post-training stack to measure model lift on our tasks

 - Develop new data products based on datasets and experts available to us

 - Identify opportunities to take advantage of self-reinforcing exponential feedback loops

 - Create agents to analyze thousands of environments and millions of trajectories

 - Help curate and specify task distributions for new corpora

 - Work with procurement to ensure external data we acquire is suitable for refinement

 - Create scaleable systems for ingesting & evaluating data we are considering buying

 - Develop new techniques for mining data for signal

What we’re looking for

 - 1+ years of experience doing RL in production at a frontier lab

 - Track record of post-training an LLM end to end

 - Desire to drive the research roadmap and implementation on a fast-moving team

 - Deep curiosity about how machines learn from data and how to extract the maximum learning signal from our tasks

Tech stack

Typescript, React, NodeJS, Postgres, Redis, Vercel, Cursor/Claude Code/Codex, Tinker, Modal, AWS, Daytona, GRPO

Details

 - In-person in San Francisco

 - Competitive salary + meaningful equity

 - Free meals in office

 - Healthcare, 401(k), 15 days of PTO per year

 - Relocation assistance

 - Small, ambitious team

This is an in-person role in San Francisco. We're a tight-knit founding team and we play to win. Join us if you like to win too.

jobs.title: Forward-Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ALEX & THE ROLE

Alex is an AI recruiter. Alex screens and interviews candidates over voice — on the web and over the phone — and it works inside the systems companies already recruit with: their applicant tracking system, their requisitions, their hiring process. Enterprises and staffing firms use it to run interviews at a volume they otherwise couldn't.

Forward-Deployed Engineers are the technical owners of every Alex deployment. When a customer signs, FDEs are the people who make Alex work inside their systems and their process — and keep it working. It is the most end-to-end engineering role at the company: you design the solution, build it, integrate it, ship it to production, and own it afterwards.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build how a customer uses Alex. Turn a hiring process described in a meeting into workflows that actually run — triggers, filters, interview guides, and the actions we take back in their ATS. When a customer needs something their setup doesn't do yet, you drive it: design, build, test, roll out, verify.

 - Own the integration surface. We integrate with roughly two dozen applicant tracking systems, some directly and some through a unified API partner. You'll build new integrations, maintain existing ones, and go deep on the ones you own — along with the other systems a customer's workflow reaches into, like assessment providers and identity verification.

 - Run the technical side of onboarding. Connection, permissions and scopes, job import, field mapping, workflow build, test interviews, go-live — sequenced so nothing is discovered in front of a candidate.

 - Own the deployments in production. The team owns the support queue — for customers and candidates both — and diagnoses to root cause rather than working around it. You'll also build the monitoring that catches problems before a customer has to call.

 - Be the technical voice of the customer. You are the person who sees, across many accounts, where the product runs out. Turning that into an evidenced case our product engineering team can act on is part of the job.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Real engineering ability. This role reads code, writes code, and ships changes. It is not a technical-adjacent role.

 - Comfort working inside someone else's system with incomplete documentation. Much of this job is finding out what a third-party API actually does, as opposed to what its docs claim.

 - Debugging instinct — the reflex to go get the evidence rather than reason from the symptom.

 - Direct customer contact without a buffer. You'll run your own working sessions and say hard things clearly.

 - Strong writing. A large fraction of the output of this role is a clear written explanation.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Forward-deployed, implementation, solutions, or integrations engineering experience — especially anywhere with a long tail of third-party systems.

 - You've built against a messy enterprise API and lived with the result.

 - Fluency with observability tooling — logs, traces, dashboards, alerting you had to live with.

Why join

 - High ownership and growth opportunities

 - Collaborate with a tight-knit team of talented builders

 - Launch products that directly impact people’s careers

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - FSA, DCFSA, HSA options

 - Flexible paid time off (PTO)

 - 401(k) plan

 - Fully paid parental leave program

If you've gotten this far and this role resonates with you, we want you to apply. Your first conversation will be with Alex, our AI recruiter.

Alex is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

We raised a $5m seed funding round at the end of 2024.

About the Role: Clinical Partner Architect

This is a pivotal role bridging the gap between our AI technology and clinical reality. As a Clinical Partner Architect, you will spearhead Pharos' partner motion, solving complex problems, ensuring high satisfaction and platform adoption from day one onward. By aligning our software to specific clinical specialties and hospital workflows, while measuring Pharos's tangible impact on health systems, clinicians, quality specialists, and the patients they serve, you will deliver real benefit to real people every day.

What You'll Do

 - Implementation Leadership: Lead end-to-end deployment with new health system partners, tackling complex operational and technical hurdles during rollout.

 - Workflow Alignment: Map and tailor our platform to fit specific clinical specialties, acting as the primary partner voice to our product and engineering teams.

 - Impact Measurement: Define and track metrics that prove the platform's value in both highly specific individual goals and health system-wide initiatives across operational efficiency, quality improvement, and patient safety outcomes.

 - Partner Success: Foster deep relationships with hospital staff to ensure sustained engagement, immediate issue resolution, and continuous feedback.

What We're Looking For

 - Comfort at the clinical–technical seam. You've worked with EHRs, clinical data, or software implementations, and you can hold a real conversation with both an engineer and a physician without needing a translator.

 - Problem-Solving Prowess: A demonstrated ability to solve hard problems and untangle complex, nuanced health system workflows.

 - Data Fluency: Familiarity with clinical data structures, interoperability standards (FHIR, HL7), or standard EHR data models.

 - Mission-Driven: A deep, recognizable passion for improving the lives of others through technology.

PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES

High agency - You’re excited by the opportunity to take ambiguous product challenges and drive them from idea to execution without waiting for direction.

Motivated by impact - You’re energized to work hard as part of a high-performing team - holding a meaningful equity stake in a company with the real potential to save thousands of lives.

Ownership mindset - You take pride in acting like an owner, taking full responsibility for the quality and outcomes of your work.

Comfortable with ambiguity - You thrive in an early-stage startup environment where there’s no rigid hierarchy, everyone wears many hats, and you have real power to influence the path of the company.

What We Offer

Enjoy a rare chance to build a category-defining healthcare AI company with early impact and outcome potential through an equity stake. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Research (EU)
jobs.description:
ABOUT ABUNDANT

Abundant is an applied research lab focused on scaling reinforcement learning for safe and reliable agentic capabilities. We are an extremely talent-dense team of researchers, roboticists, founders, and operators whose work includes the Waymo Driver.

 

THE ROLE

You will own a research agenda where research meets production, co-designing strategies with researchers from frontier AI labs. You are the “PM of the model”: you pick the problem, design the data and reward signal that moves it, and see it through to a live training run. The job rewards a founder mentality and extreme ownership, including going into unfamiliar domains, from chemical engineering to complex legal logic, and getting to ground truth fast on problems others have written off.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Foundational capability research and execution. Architect and execute a research agenda to find simple, generalizable ideas that advance model reasoning at scale, and own it from hypothesis through to running in live systems.

 - Design tasks and verifiers that stay hard. Build long-horizon agentic tasks that are still difficult a model generation from now, with graders where partial credit means something and the obvious exploit does not score.

 - Diagnose failure modes. Read trajectories until you can say why a model fails a class of work, then turn that into the data or reward signal that fixes it. This is the core loop of the job.

 - Model alignment and data strategy. Partner with the world’s most advanced AI research teams on datasets and benchmarks that shape how frontier models behave, focused on alignment, safety, and reward signal design.

 - Autonomous problem selection. Identify, scope, and run long projects, choosing the problems that matter most for scaling data toward AGI.

 - System infrastructure. Work with engineering on data pipelines, internal tooling, and deep learning implementations. If a workflow produces bad data, you fix the workflow.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You write a lot of code. Strong software engineering and deep Python, comfortable owning a system end to end and debugging through layers you did not write.

 - You have built evaluations, RL environments, agent harnesses, verifiers, or execution sandboxes, and you have opinions about which of them can be trusted.

 - You have shipped research into production, particularly post-training, distillation, and high-stakes evaluation.

 - You have worked on large-scale agent systems: orchestration frameworks, tool APIs, distributed execution, observability, and logging.

 - You get to ground truth in an unfamiliar domain by building something and reading outputs, not by reading about it.

 - You notice the misspecified task, the ambiguous prompt, and the grader that can be gamed.

 - You have a thoughtful perspective on the societal and safety impacts of deploying general-purpose AI systems.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - A PhD (CS, ML, NLP) and publications at NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR. Neither is required.

 - Work on public benchmarks or task suites, for example Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench-style harnesses, or HCAST.

 - RLHF or RLAIF experience and a view on how training choices show up in model behavior.

 - Experience running work through large expert or annotation operations.

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$250,000 - $450,000

Cash Bonus

Sizable performance bonus tied to project and company milestones

Equity

Generous early-stage grant

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

 - Strategize and Execute Partner Events: Identify and execute partner events and activations. This includes securing speaking slots in partner theaters, organizing high-touch networking events, and managing joint sponsorships.

 - Campaign Integration: Collaborate with the Global Campaigns and Product Marketing teams to ensure partner messaging is woven into our core narrative, specifically targeting the "Developer to Decision-Maker" journey.

 - Lifecycle Partner Marketing: Collaborate on the end-to-end partner journey, from onboarding new technology partners to optimizing long-term co-marketing ROI.

 - Measurement & Optimization: Track, analyze, and report on the impact of partner programs. You will own the metrics for partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, iterating on tactics based on data-driven insights.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience: 8+ years of experience in partner marketing within the B2B SaaS space.

 - Ecosystem Knowledge: Proven track record of working with channel partners/resellers and major cloud providers like (AWS, GCP, Azure) or security/infrastructure technology partners.

 - Background: In cybersecurity and knowledge of industry.

 - The "Tradeshow" Mindset: You understand that events are about density and trust. You have experience managing logistics and high-stakes networking environments.

 - Project Management: Exceptional ability to manage multiple stakeholders (internal and external) and meet deadlines.

 - Tech Stack: Hands-on proficiency with Salesforce and marketing automation (HubSpot/Marketo). Experience with PRM (Partner Relationship Management) tools is a plus.

 - Communication: You can translate deep technical concepts into value-driven stories for both business and technical audiences.

 - Travel: Willingness to travel (up to 30%) to key partner hubs and major industry events.

 

HOW WE HIRE

Our process is designed to be straightforward and respectful of your time. We skip performative rounds and focus on what matters: understanding how you think and what you can do.

You'll start with a 30-minute recruiter screen, followed by another 30-minute interview with the hiring manager. Then we'll have you meet with other members of the marketing and sales organizations for 30-minutes each, and a final 30-minute round with our CMO.

 

Why Teleport

You're joining a company where the problem is real, the team is small, and your work shows up directly in the product. We're not a big company, you won't get lost in a crowd. You'll have the freedom and autonomy to do what you're great at, alongside teammates who care about doing it right and want to see you succeed. The work is collaborative, there's real room to grow, and the mission is one worth showing up for.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we're genuinely passionate about what we're building.

The Benefits

At Teleport, we believe your career is more important than a list of perks. That's why we focus on making your day-to-day the best it can be — giving you the autonomy, access, and support to do the best work of your career.

- Extensive health coverage

- Annual expense budget

- Rest and recovery policies that maximize your ability to recharge

- Investment in your future with retirement savings plans

- Professional development opportunities

Teleport is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any classifications protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Brand Designer
jobs.description:
ABOUT WARP

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.

As a Brand Designer at Warp, you'll be directly responsible for shaping how the world sees us. You'll own our logo and visual identity system, design the graphics that show up in every campaign, deck, and launch, and turn complex financial concepts into visuals people actually want to look at. Working closely with marketing, product, and the founding team, you'll set the visual bar for a company still still early in its story and design the marks and systems that carry Warp as we scale,

WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO'S OBSESSED WITH:

 - Craft. Sharp typography, clean systems, a logo and identity that hold up at any size or surface.

 - Story. Turning complex financial concepts into visuals people actually want to look at.

 - Speed. Shipping polished work fast, without waiting for a perfect brief.

 - Systems. Building the templates, guidelines, and libraries that let the rest of the company move fast without breaking the brand.
 
 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own Warp's logo and visual identity including the marks, systems, and standards that show up across product, marketing, and every customer touchpoint.

 - Design the assets that drive growth. Social posts, landing pages, event posters, and team merch that turn attention into pipeline while keeping the brand consistent.

 - Build the operating system for Brand: guidelines, templates, and asset libraries that let anyone at Warp ship on-brand work fast.

 - Prototype fast. Use design software and AI to test new directions before committing to a final concept.

 - Own the production pipeline from asset handoff to print- and web-ready exports, so design never becomes the bottleneck.

 - Partner directly with marketing, product, and sales to turn briefs into polished visual work that fits the moment.

 - Lead by making. Ship 2–3 brand-defining pieces of work each year—a rebrand element, a campaign identity, a flagship asset—that raise the bar for how Warp looks.

 - Spot the opportunities to sharpen and evolve Warp's visual identity as the company scales, and make the case for the changes that matter.

 - Coordinate with freelancers, print vendors, or production partners when a project needs extra hands.

 WHAT YOU NEED

 - 4+ years of experience in brand, graphic, or visual design.

 - Hybrid thinking, someone who thrives at the intersection of craft and speed, brand and business.

 - A strong portfolio demonstrating logo design and brand identity work.

 - Strong expertise in design software (pref. Figma, Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop)

 - Startup or digital agency experience.

 - Solid understanding of typography, color theory, layout, and visual hierarchy.

 - Strong operational instincts. You have a passion for building templates, guidelines, and processes that let the whole company move fast without breaking the brand.

 - Proactive, can-do attitude and are equally excited to push boundaries as you are to ship

 - Ability to juggle multiple projects with grace, manage your own timelines, and thrive in fast-paced environments.

 - Excellent communication skills

 - High agency and the ability to figure things out

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with motion graphics or basic animation

 - Familiarity with brand strategy or naming projects

 - Illustration skills

 - An understanding of fintech or B2B product branding

BENEFITS AT WARP: 

 - 100% Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents.

 - 401(k) Matching: Start investing in your future from day one.

 - Flexible PTO: We offer uncapped flexible PTO, meaning you’re trusted to take the time you need to recharge while balancing your responsibilities and team commitments.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre-tax commuter benefits for your daily trip to our NYC office.

 - Catered Lunch Daily: Great food, every day, on us. No meal prep, no decision fatigue.

 - Quarterly Offsites: Beautiful locations to connect as a team. Past locations include Spain, Catskills, and San Francisco.

Warp is based in New York City, and most of our team works together in-office 5x per week. Please refer to the top of this page for this position's hiring location and working model.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Pharos is a startup dedicated to improving patient safety in hospitals through advanced AI-powered reporting and analytics. Our mission is to make healthcare safer by automating hospital quality reporting and helping staff identify and prevent the root causes of avoidable harm. Our vision is an AI system reviewing every chart at scale, identifying patterns and giving clinicians the insights they need to prevent the 100k avoidable deaths that occur in U.S. hospitals every year. We raised a $5m seed funding round at the end of 2024.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a pivotal role as a founding member of the engineering team at Pharos. As a Software Engineer, you will bridge the critical gap between product vision and technical execution. You will be responsible for building, shipping, and maintaining our core user-facing applications, working in close partnership with the founders and design team. These products include an interface for users to review and correct AI-generated results to medical questions, as well as an analytics and root cause analysis platform where users can visualize clinical quality trends and drill down into the causes of specific patient safety events.

The scope of this role is intentionally broad. As one of our first engineers, you’ll be part of the founding team and work across product development, integrations, internal tooling, infrastructure, and full-stack engineering. We’re building a new category of product, so many of the problems you’ll work on won’t have an established playbook.

You’ll build customer-facing features, integrations with healthcare systems, internal tools that speed up clinical registry development and customer onboarding, and the LLM systems that power our product.

You’ll work closely with a high-agency, close-knit engineering team that moves quickly, shares context, and collaborates deeply on technical and product decisions. Your work will directly shape the systems healthcare workers use every day to make healthcare safer

WHAT YOU'LL DO
