jobs.title: Clinical QA Nurse (RN)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Registered Nurse with deep home health and hospice experience to own the clinical quality of the documentation flowing through our AI platform.

Our automations review referrals, OASIS documentation, certifications, physician orders, hospice election forms, face-to-face documentation, and supporting clinical records before they reach billing and authorization workflows. Your job is to ensure those automations make clinically sound decisions, identify where they fail, and continuously improve their accuracy.

You'll work at the intersection of clinical expertise, quality assurance, and AI. Rather than reviewing a handful of patient charts each day, you'll help build systems that review thousands correctly.

This is not a bedside or utilization review position. It's an operations and quality role for a nurse who enjoys finding edge cases, improving processes, and translating clinical judgment into scalable automation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

AUDIT CLINICAL QA PERFORMANCE

Review charts processed by our clinical automation platform for accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Validate whether documentation supports services, identify incorrect classifications, and investigate why automation errors occurred.

IMPROVE CLINICAL AUTOMATION LOGIC

Partner with engineering and product teams to refine how our AI evaluates clinical documentation. You'll identify where automations miss important clinical nuances, recommend decision rules, and validate improvements before they're deployed.

BUILD CLINICAL REVIEW STANDARDS

Develop SOPs that define how clinical documentation should be reviewed across home health and hospice. Standardize quality expectations while accounting for agency-specific workflows and payer requirements.

SUPPORT CUSTOMER IMPLEMENTATIONS

Work directly with agencies to understand their documentation standards, clinical workflows, and compliance expectations. Help configure automations that align with each client's operational processes.

DRIVE QUALITY METRICS

Measure and improve documentation quality, automation accuracy, exception rates, clinical escalations, and rework. Continuously identify opportunities to improve automation performance.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

REQUIRED

 - Active RN license (NY or compact license preferred)

 - 3+ years of home health and/or hospice clinical experience

 - Strong understanding of OASIS documentation and home health eligibility requirements

 - Experience reviewing physician orders, certifications, plans of care, face-to-face documentation, and hospice election paperwork

 - Hands-on experience with HomeCare HomeBase (HCHB), Axxess, and WellSky; KanTime a plus

 - Strong understanding of Medicare home health and hospice documentation requirements

 - Experience writing SOPs, QA guidelines, or training documentation

 - Excellent attention to detail and pattern recognition

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment

NICE TO HAVE

 - QA, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), or Compliance experience

 - Experience with AI, workflow automation, or healthcare technology companies

 - Familiarity with referral platforms including Careport and Forcura

 - Experience implementing or optimizing EMR workflows
 
 

WHY THIS ROLE

Scale your clinical expertise. Help AI review thousands of charts instead of reviewing them one at a time.

Own quality. Your feedback directly improves the clinical accuracy of our platform across every customer.

Influence the product. Work side-by-side with engineering to shape how AI understands home health and hospice documentation.

jobs.title: Prior Authorization Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring an experienced Prior Authorization Specialist to help build the future of authorization automation for home health and hospice.

Prior authorization is one of the largest operational bottlenecks for agencies. Our platform automatically verifies benefits, gathers documentation, submits authorizations, follows up with payers, and monitors approval status. Your role is to ensure those automations run accurately, efficiently, and according to payer requirements.

You'll combine deep operational knowledge with process improvement, helping us encode payer-specific workflows into software that scales across thousands of authorization requests.

This isn't a traditional authorization desk role. It's an operations role for someone who understands the complexity of authorizations and wants to help automate them.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

AUDIT AUTHORIZATION WORKFLOWS

Review authorization requests completed by our automations for completeness, accuracy, and turnaround time. Identify recurring failure points and determine whether issues stem from payer requirements, documentation, or automation logic.

IMPROVE AUTHORIZATION AUTOMATION

Partner with product and engineering teams to translate complex payer rules into scalable workflows. Help define escalation logic, documentation requirements, follow-up cadences, and exception handling.

BUILD PAYER PLAYBOOKS

Create and maintain SOPs covering authorization workflows across Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, managed Medicaid, commercial payers, and state-specific requirements.

PARTNER WITH CLIENTS

Meet with intake, authorization, and billing teams to understand agency workflows, resolve escalations, and configure automation to match operational needs.

TRACK OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE

Monitor authorization turnaround times, approval rates, denial trends, escalation volume, payer response times, and automation success metrics. Drive continuous improvement initiatives.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

REQUIRED

 - 3+ years of prior authorization experience within home health, hospice, or post-acute care

 - Deep familiarity with Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, managed Medicaid, commercial insurance, and authorization workflows

 - Experience obtaining authorizations across multiple payer portals

 - Strong understanding of eligibility verification, authorization documentation requirements, and referral workflows

 - Experience with HomeCare HomeBase (HCHB), Axxess, WellSky, and KanTime preferred

 - Strong organizational skills with excellent attention to detail

 - Experience documenting workflows or SOPs

 - Comfortable working independently in a fast-moving startup

NICE TO HAVE

 - RN, LPN, or clinical background

 - Experience with Careport, Forcura, Ensocare, or referral management platforms

 - Experience working with automation or RCM software vendors

 - Knowledge of hospice-specific authorization requirements and Medicaid room & board processes
 
 

WHY THIS ROLE

Multiply your impact. Your expertise becomes automation that processes thousands of authorizations every month.

Solve hard operational problems. Help eliminate one of the biggest administrative burdens in post-acute care.

Build the future. Join an early-stage healthcare AI company where your knowledge directly shapes the product roadmap.

jobs.title: People Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODES HEALTH

Codes Health is rebuilding how medical records move through the legal system. Today, plaintiff law firms rely on slow, fragmented vendors to retrieve medical records, often waiting weeks with little visibility or reliability. We're replacing that with modern infrastructure that retrieves records nationwide, navigates the complexity of every healthcare provider, and delivers organized, structured records that help firms move cases faster. Our mission is to fully automate record retrieval by building an agentic platform that continuously learns and improves across thousands of unique healthcare workflows.

We're a two-year-old, NYC-based startup backed by a $17.5M Series A, growing rapidly and tackling one of healthcare's most operationally complex problems. We're looking for our first People hire to help us scale the team and build the foundation for our next stage of growth. If you're excited by ambitious challenges, exceptional teammates, and the opportunity to make an outsized impact from day one, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

People and culture are critical to what we’re building at Codes Health, making this one of the most important hires we’ll make. As our first People hire, you’ll build the function from 0 → 1 and help us scale a small, high-performing team without losing the urgency, high standards, and culture that got us here. You’ll stay ahead of the challenges that come with rapid growth, ensuring we remain compliant while creating an environment where employees feel seen, heard, and supported.

This role is about speed and care, not process for its own sake. We want someone who prioritizes direct engagement and builds infrastructure that helps people and the business move faster. There is no existing People function to inherit—the scope is wide, the ownership is real, and you’ll report directly to the CEO.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the employee experience. Lead onboarding, offboarding, and everything in between to create a strong and consistent employee experience.

 - Be a trusted resource. Handle employee relations and sensitive matters with discretion, care, and sound judgment.

 - Own People operations and compliance. Manage policies, the Codes Health Employee Handbook, visa support, and People documentation.

 - Work closely with the CEO to shape organizational design for our scale, and hire your own team over time.

 - Be in the office five days a week. NYC based or willing to relocate.

WHO YOU ARE

 - 5–8 years of HR, People Ops, or talent experience, with strong HR fundamentals and a track record of building or scaling People functions in high-growth environments.

 - Energized by building from scratch, with a strong instinct for creating infrastructure and processes that help teams move faster.

 - High standards, strong judgment, and the ability to build trust quickly, navigate hard conversations, and solve problems directly.

 - Strong program management skills and experience with modern HR systems such as Rippling, Ashby, Lattice, or similar tools.

WHY JOIN CODES HEALTH

You'll own a function that directly shapes what this company becomes. This is a high-visibility role with real ownership, meaningful equity, and the opportunity to grow alongside, and help lead a company scaling quickly. You'll report directly to the CEO and have the opportunity to build out your own team over time.

As our first HR hire, the people programs, hiring process, and culture practices you build in your first year will still be the backbone of Codes Health as we scale 100x. If you want a role where your judgment and your care for people directly determine how well this company holds together while it grows fast, this is it.

COMPENSATION

 - Base salary: $100,000 - $200,000

 - Meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Healthcare, vision, and dental insurance.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Additional benefits such as paid dinner in office and Ubers from the office. 

Actual base pay is based on experience, skills, and qualifications and may vary from the range listed above, consistent with New York pay transparency requirements.

jobs.title: Financial Operations Lead
jobs.description:
At Solve Intelligence, we're building something people actually want - and we have the revenue and traction to prove it.

🏗️ THE ROLE: FINANCIAL OPERATIONS LEAD

Less than 24 months since launch, we are adding 7 figures of ARR per month, we have raised ~$60M USD, and we are quadrupling headcount this year. We've built a world-class team of AI PhDs, engineers, and patent attorneys. Now, we need a high-energy, ambitious Financial Operations Lead to help us scale to $1B+ ARR.

You'll be our first dedicated finance hire, based in London and working directly with the founders.

Until now, finance has not been run by any single person. Your job is to own it end-to-end: get the fundamentals running flawlessly, then build the processes, tooling, and budgets that scale us to 100+ people across our three offices (London, New York, and Munich) and our continued revenue growth.

This isn't a CFO-strategist role, and it isn't bookkeeping.

It's for a hands-on generalist who understands accounting deeply, executes relentlessly, and is happy to go invoice-by-invoice in the morning, build the company budget in the afternoon, and model financials in the evening. You'll do things that don't scale at first to learn the business inside out, automate them away with tooling and AI, and grow into a true business partner to Sales and Marketing — the person with a 360° view of Solve.

What you'll own:

 - Payments (AP): Own supplier payments end-to-end — approval workflows, invoices paid on time, duplicates and double-payments caught before they happen — and lead vendor negotiations on everything from software to office space.

 - Billing & Collections (AR): Own customer invoicing across our 1,000+ law firm and enterprise clients. Partner with RevOps to collect our backlog of overdue invoices fast and keep cash flowing in.

 - The Monthly Close & Metrics: Run our external accountants to an accurate, on-time close every month. Own our financial metrics — definitions, reporting, the single source of truth — and work hand-in-hand with the CEO on communicating them to the board and investors.

 - Processes & Tooling: Design and implement our finance stack from scratch. Approvals, procurement, spend management, billing, and more. Choose tools that scale and automate aggressively with AI.

 - Budgets & Financial Culture: Work directly with the founders to build our first budgeting and approval processes (hiring, marketing, conferences, offices, etc) and partner closely with every team. Help the founders instil a culture where money is not free.

 - Modelling & Big Decisions: Build the financial models behind our biggest calls — office leases, hiring plans, marketing budgets — and get stuck into special projects like M&A (we've already made two acquisitions this year).

 - International Finance: Own the finance side of operating and expanding across three countries (and counting): budgets for new office setup, transfer pricing, and international tax, working with our external advisors.

 - Cash & Treasury: Steward the ~$60M we've raised: payroll and vendors always paid, cash put to work safely.

💡 ABOUT SOLVE INTELLIGENCE

We are the fastest-growing startup transforming Intellectual Property. Our AI platform handles everything from invention harvesting and patent generation through to litigation and licensing.

 - Growth: 20–30% MoM revenue growth; 8 figures of ARR just ~2 years since launch.

 - Market: 600+ IP teams across 6 continents, including Tier-1 firms like DLA Piper, tech giants, and boutiques.

 - Impact: Users report 50–90% efficiency and quality improvements.

 - Backing: ~$60M from Y Combinator, 20VC, Microsoft, Thomson Reuters, and the founders of top companies like Stripe, Perplexity, Tinder, Deel, Hugging Face, and Canva. See our Series B announcement https://www.solveintelligence.com/blog/post/solve-intelligence-raises-40m-series-b-to-build-ai-for-patents-and-launches-charts.

👋 WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

You'll be joining a founding team with deep pedigree:

 - Sanj https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanj-ahilan-844b33137/ (CRO): PhD in AI (Gatsby Unit, UCL), ex-Huawei R&D, former lead at Magic Carpet AI (acquired).

 - Chris https://www.linkedin.com/in/chris-parsonson/ (CEO): PhD in AI (UCL), published researcher, ex-Dyson and Alan Turing Institute.

 - Angus https://www.linkedin.com/in/angus-parsonson/ (CTO): MEng Computer Science, ex-Qualcomm and Coremont (Brevan Howard).

🚀 WHO YOU ARE

We are a high-performance culture. To thrive here:

 - You get your hands dirty: You'll happily go line-by-line through invoices, the CRM, and the bank to make things clean — then automate the process so it stays clean.

 - You're detail-obsessed: Duplicate invoices, overdue payments, wrong pricing — nothing gets past you.

 - You have high agency: There's no playbook and no finance team behind you (yet). Give you an ambiguous problem and you'll work it out: find the mess, own it, fix it.

 - You're a business partner, not a back-office cop: You work close to Sales, Marketing, and the wider team, helping everyone spend smarter and move faster. You know the highest-leverage thing finance can do here is accelerate growth — nudging our treasury yield from 2.7% to 2.9% is not the job.

 - You're all-in: Solve is fast and intense, and this isn't a 9–5. You get passionate — even obsessive — about the problems you own.

 - You're ambitious: You'll do the dirty work now because you want to build the finance function as we scale.

🛠️ WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Haves:

 - 5+ years in finance or finance-heavy operations at high-growth tech companies — e.g., FP&A lead/head, finance ops, or a generalist operator with a finance spike — now hungry for broader scope.

 - Deep fluency in accounting — you can run external accountants to an on-time close — without needing to be an accountant yourself.

 - A track record of implementing finance processes, tooling, and automation that scale with a fast-growing company.

 - Strong modelling skills acros

jobs.title: Compliance Lead
jobs.description:
tl;dr: We’re automating compliance for banks and fintechs with AI agents that work on existing systems like human analysts. We’re looking for someone who understands both compliance and product management, someone who can turn regulatory workflows into scalable systems that help define how our AI agents reason, decide, and learn.

BACKGROUND

If you’ve worked in compliance, you’ve seen it firsthand: the endless reviews, duplicate alerts, and outdated systems that make even simple controls take hours. The rules make sense; the systems don’t.

Sphinx is fixing that. We build AI analysts that work inside browsers and internal systems just like humans — automating AML, KYC, KYB, and transaction monitoring end-to-end.

Instead of replacing judgment, our agents replicate it – learning from analyst feedback, explaining their reasoning, and improving over time. The result: faster onboarding, fewer false positives, and compliance teams that focus on decisions, not data entry.

Banks and fintechs across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and LatAm use Sphinx agents to handle 90% of their manual work and cut costs by 4x.

WHY JOIN SPHINX

 1. Redefine compliance: Banks spend $50B a year hiring thousands of analysts to manage compliance operations. You’ll design how financial crime prevention works in the age of AI – replacing checklists and manual reviews with robust reasoning systems that explain their logic.

 2. Work directly with clients: You’ll collaborate with banks, fintechs, and MSBs to deploy automation that meets real-world standards.

 3. Build at the frontier: You’ll work with engineers to design interpretable, auditable, and explainable AI systems that regulators can trust.

 4. We have never lost a deal to a competitor: Yes you heard that right, we’ve won every RFP we’ve been in.

 5. Small team, big surface area: Our co-founders previously sold an AI company & have built ML systems that scaled to millions of users and closed deals with major banks. The rest of our team in SF includes PhDs, industry experts, and competitive coders.

WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

Define how our agents think. That means turning complex regulations into structured, machine-readable logic – and ensuring it works across jurisdictions, languages, and edge cases.

Partner with customers to understand how their compliance processes are actually done, then design products that remove the bottlenecks: mapping workflows, refining alerts, improving output quality & accuracy, and building transparency into every decision.

You’ll collaborate with engineering to make sure every product decision is explainable and compliant by design – ensuring regulatory adherence, technical precision, and customer success.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You bring real compliance experience: You’ve spent 3–5 years in AML, risk, or compliance roles at a bank, fintech, or regtech – and you know how investigations, onboarding, and escalations actually work.

 - You bridge compliance and product: You can translate regulatory logic into product requirements engineers can act on – turning policies, SOPs, and edge cases into automated workflows.

 - You think in systems: You know how to deconstruct manual review processes, identify leverage points, and design scalable automation.

 - You care about false-positives: you know how to use metrics to understand issues, and love diving deeper to find a pattern.

 - You’re impact-obsessed: You want to see your work move the company forward – every day.

ABOUT THE INTERVIEW

 - Intro call 

 - Case Study

 - Fit call

 - Offer 🎉

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - 🍽 Lunch, dinner and snacks at the office

 - 🏥 Comprehensive healthcare

 - 🏝️ Unlimited PTO

 - 🗺️ Annual offsite (last one in Mexico!)

 - ✈️ Paid relocation & one-month temporary housing

 - 💻 Latest tech and as many monitors as you can fit on a desk

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer (Forward Deployed)
jobs.description:
About Teleport

Don't wait for the future of infrastructure. Be part of it.

Teleport is the AI Infrastructure Identity Company. We're solving one of the hardest problems in security: giving every human, machine, workload, and AI agent a cryptographically secured identity, improving engineering velocity while maintaining security. We make trusted computing simple. This gives you the freedom, power, and autonomy to build and innovate with confidence.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we work with companies like Nasdaq, DoorDash, and Elastic to secure infrastructure for an AI world.

About the Role

 

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer that will work directly with customers to ensure successful Teleport deployments.

You will meet regularly with customers, understand pain points blocking deployments and remove roadblocks. This includes writing and fixing IaC deployments (like Helm charts), developing workarounds, and writing Go code to fix bugs and implement small features.

For more complex issues, you will work with customers to articulate the problem they are trying to solve, gather requirements, and make the business case to the product and engineering teams to invest in resolving the issue.

What You'll Do

 - This job sits at the intersection of product, engineering, and revenue.

 - You won't just work closely with the engineering team, you will be on the engineering team.

 - The range of problem solving includes networking, performance, security and integrations with existing systems.

 - Most of the code you will write will be open source.

 - Our products are loved by their users, you'll get to meet them regularly.

What We're Looking For

 - Excellent communication skills.

 - Willing to travel to customer sites.

 - Infrastructure as Code (IaC) experience (like Terraform, Ansible, Helm).

 - Linux systems engineering experience.

 - Go or Rust experience.

 - As we are a startup, you should be comfortable changing the area of focus and working directly with customers.

How We Hire

jobs.description:
ABOUT RETELL AI

Retell AI is using first-principles thinking to reimagine the call center with cutting-edge voice AI. Thousands of companies now use Retell's AI voice agents to handle sales, support, and logistics calls that once required large teams of human agents. Backed by Y Combinator, Alt Capital, and other leading investors, we've scaled to $80M in ARR with a team of 50, up from $5M at the start of 2025, and are now valued at over $1.5B.

Our vision for 2026 is to build a modern CX platform where entire contact centers are powered by AI. Instead of basic automation that needs constant human tuning, we're creating intelligent AI “workers” that act as frontline agents, QA analysts, and managers, continuously executing, monitoring, and improving every customer interaction.

We're growing fast and looking for ambitious builders who want to tackle hard technical problems, move quickly, and have a real impact on one of the fastest-growing voice AI companies in the world.

Let's build the future together.

Recent recognition:

 - No. 1 Best Places to Work in the Bay Area, San Francisco Business Times 2026 https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/voice-ai-startup-retell-ai-145200025.html

 - Top 50 AI Apps, a16z (2025) https://a16z.com/the-ai-application-spending-report-where-startup-dollars-really-go/

 - Top-Ranked Startup, Lean AI Leaderboard https://leanaileaderboard.com/

 - Backed by Y Combinator https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/retell-ai

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Retell AI transforms customer experience with voice AI for enterprises, including customers like CVS/Aetna, American Airlines, Lenovo, and Grab. We have more customer stories than we can tell!

We are hiring an Enterprise Account Executive to build and grow our new business revenue. This is a high-ownership craft role. You report to the CEO and work closely with the founding team.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own Complex Enterprise Deals: Own the full sales cycle from first conversation through signed production agreement. Lead discovery, solution positioning, business-case development, technical validation, security and procurement, commercial negotiation, and executive alignment.

 - Turn Customer Problems Into Retell Deployments: Understand the customer’s call center operations, existing technology stack, priority use cases, and success criteria. Translate these into a clear deployment roadmap and compelling vision for how Retell can transform their customer operations. 

 - Design Pilots That Convert: Structure tightly scoped pilots with clear stakeholders, timelines, success metrics, production requirements, and commercial next steps. Maintain urgency throughout the pilot and drive a decisive transition into production. 

 - Run Rigorous Deal Qualification: Use MEDDPICC to identify the economic buyer, decision process, technical and business criteria, internal champion, competition, procurement path, and quantified customer pain. Maintain accurate forecasts and proactively address deal risk. 

 - Build and Quantify the Business Case: Connect Retell’s technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes, including automation rate, resolution rate, cost reduction, customer experience, revenue impact, and speed to deployment. 

 - Navigate Complex Buying Committees: Build trusted relationships across executives, contact center leaders, IT, security, procurement, legal, product teams, and technical champions. Multithread every strategic account and create alignment across business and technical stakeholders. 

 - Lead Technical and Product Collaboration: Partner closely with solutions engineering, FDE, product, and engineering teams to demonstrate Retell’s platform, validate integrations, resolve technical blockers, and design solutions that can succeed in production at enterprise scale. 

 - Drive Production and Expansion: Stay accountable beyond the initial signature. Partner with deployment and customer success teams to ensure successful implementation, demonstrate value, and expand Retell across additional use cases, teams, business units, and geographies. 

 - Bring the Market Back Into Retell: Represent the customer internally by clearly communicating objections, competitive intelligence, product gaps, and emerging enterprise requirements to Retell’s product and leadership teams.

 

REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of enterprise sales experience at a high-growth SaaS or AI company, with a track record of closing $300k+ ACV complex enterprise deals.

 - Experience selling technical products to enterprises, ideally across contact centers, CCaaS, CRM, communications infrastructure, or AI.

 - Proven ability to manage long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles involving business leaders, IT, security, legal, procurement, and executive buyers.

 - Strong track record of designing successful pilots, building quantified business cases, and converting technical evaluations into large-scale production deployments.

 - Skilled in MEDDPICC, multithreading, commercial negotiation, pipeline management, and accurate forecasting.

 - Strong executive presence with the technical fluency to earn credibility with both business and engineering stakeholders.

 - Highly organized, proactive, and accountable, with the ability to create urgency and drive complex deals forward with limited structure.
 

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IF

 - You have 5–10 years of enterprise SaaS or AI sales experience, consistently closing complex six- and seven-figure enterprise deals.

jobs.title: Enterprise Sales Development Representative (Ent-SDR)
jobs.description:
ABOUT CODES HEALTH

Codes Health is building the modern platform for medical record retrieval. Record requests today move through fax machines, phone trees, and manual follow-up, a process that can take weeks and routinely stalls the legal and clinical decisions that depend on it. We use AI in conjunction with human review to pull decision-ready records in a fraction of the time, with a level of accuracy legacy vendors can't match.

We just turned two, doubling order volume month over month, and on a clear path to category leadership. We're well-funded (post Series A) and building toward 100x our current scale.

Our mission is to fully automate record retrieval. Getting there takes sharp engineering and relentless execution, in equal measure.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is one of the best entry points into tech sales you'll find. Codes Health is growing fast. We've doubled our sales team since January. As an SDR, you'll be on the front line of that growth: the first Codes Health voice most prospects hear, and the person responsible for turning cold outreach into real conversations for our Account Executives.

You won't be making calls into a void. You're selling into a category we're already winning. This is a product that saves law firms and healthcare providers weeks of waiting, with real urgency behind every conversation. Know that you are selling an outcome. You'll learn how to research accounts, craft messaging that lands, run outbound sequences, and qualify opportunities with a disciplined approach and uncompromising rigor. You'll see the direct impact of your work within your first few months, not your first few years.

This role is built as a launchpad. Our strongest SDRs move into Account Executive and sales leadership roles as we scale. If you're hungry, coachable, and want a front-row seat to what building a category-defining company actually looks like, this is it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Prospect and research enterprise target accounts across personal injury law, identifying the right people to talk to.

 - Run outbound outreach to generate qualified meetings for our Account Executive team: calls, email, LinkedIn, and creative channels.

 - Qualify inbound interest, quickly separating real opportunities from noise so AEs spend their time in the right conversations.

 - Learn and help refine our messaging and playbook as we scale from a handful of reps to a full sales organization.

 - Work closely with Account Executives and the VP of Sales to understand what makes a great opportunity, and build toward owning full-cycle deals yourself. Your goal is to book high-intent, qualified demos for AEs.

 - Represent Codes Health with energy and professionalism in every interaction. You're often the first impression a prospect has of the company.

 - Work from our Dumbo headquarters five days a week, with regular travel for client meetings and conferences (50% in the field).

 - Understand that we are selling an outcome, not a service.

WHO YOU ARE

 - Hungry to build a career in sales and excited about joining a high-growth startup at an early stage.

 - A strong communicator, outgoing, confident on the phone, sharp in writing, and comfortable initiating conversations with strangers.

 - Coachable and resilient. You take feedback well, iterate fast, and don't get rattled by a string of "nos" on the way to a "yes."

 - Organized and self-motivated. You can manage a high volume of outreach without letting things fall through the cracks.

 - In-person oriented. You want to learn in a room full of people who are further along than you.

 - 2+ years of SDR experience selling to operational and financial decision-makers (Ops, Finance, COO/CFO).

 - NYC preferred. Open to exceptional remote candidates.

WHY JOIN CODES HEALTH

This is a rare shot at getting in early. We're two years old, growing fast, and building the category we operate in. And, we're doing it with a team small enough that your work is visible from day one. You won't be an anonymous name on a dashboard; you'll be one of the people who helped shape Codes Health's sales engine during its formative stages.

The runway here is real. We're investing in our SDRs as future AEs and future sales leaders. You'll get direct mentorship from experienced sellers and our VP of Sales, hands-on training in modern sales tools and technique, and a clear, fast path to more ownership as you prove yourself.

The work matters. Every meeting you book moves a law firm closer to resolving a case or a healthcare provider closer to delivering care faster. If you want to learn sales at a company that's actually growing, surrounded by people who will push you to get better fast, this is the role.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary: $80,000–$90,000, commensurate with experience.

 - On-target earnings: $135,000–$145,000 total compensation, including commission tied to meetings booked and pipeline generated.

 - Meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Health benefits and a setup built around doing your best work.

 - A defined path to promotion into Account Executive and beyond.

Actual base pay is based on experience, skills, and qualifications and may vary from the range listed above, consistent with New York pay transparency requirements.

jobs.title: GTM Engineer
jobs.description:
GTM ENGINEER

Location: San Francisco, CA Type: Full-time, on-site

COMPANY OVERVIEW

AgentMail is building the communication and identity layer for AI agents.

Agents are starting to do real work, but they still lack basic infrastructure humans already have: persistent identity, reliable communication, permissions, memory, and a system of record. AgentMail gives every AI agent its own programmable inbox.

Developers use our API to create inboxes, send and receive email, manage threads, parse messages into structured data, route webhooks, attach domains, and build agents that can communicate across the internet.

We're backed by Y Combinator and have raised $6M led by General Catalyst, with support from the founders of Ramp, Supabase, and HubSpot, as well as Paul Graham.

We're early, moving fast, and building in a category without a playbook. If you want to help define core infrastructure for the agent era, we'd love to meet you.

TLDR

We're hiring a GTM Engineer to build the machine behind AgentMail's growth: the data pipeline, the outbound engine, and the source of truth the whole company runs on. This is a build-and-own role, not a support role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the growth data layer end to end: instrument the funnel, enrich every signup, and build the dashboards the company treats as the source of truth

 - Turn our best customers into ten more: lookalike modeling, automated outbound, LinkedIn plays, and surfacing champions and buyers inside companies already using us

 - Run experiments across the PLG engine (content, integrations, backlinks, paid) and double down on what moves signups

 - Connect the stack through APIs, webhooks, and automation so data moves cleanly between PostHog, our CRM, enrichment providers, and outbound tooling

 - Decide what tools we use and what gets kicked to the curb. You own the stack

 - Build AI-powered internal tools

 - Ship systems from prototype through rollout and adoption, then hold your ground. You built it, the team follows it

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A technical foundation: CS, data science, or equivalent. You write real scripts in Python/TypeScript/SQL, wire APIs together, and are dangerous with Claude Code or Codex

 - You've seen a great growth motion up close, or you've been obsessively reverse-engineering how the best PLG companies grow

 - High agency in ambiguity: you call out what's broken, come with an opinion, and fix things without being asked

 - Low ego, high buy-in

 - Organized enough that the systems you build don't rot. Clean data is a discipline, not a feature

 - You want to help invent a market, not just run someone else's process

BONUS POINTS

 - Hands-on experience with tools like Clay, n8n, enrichment waterfalls, or sending infrastructure

 - PostHog fluency (we live in it)

 - You've shipped agentic workflows or internal AI tooling before

 - You've worked at or studied a technical PLG company up close

jobs.title: Head of GenAI Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom https://www.photoroom.com is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

HEAD OF GENAI PLATFORM

ROLE SUMMARY

We're looking for a Head of GenAI Platform to lead the strategy and technical direction behind Photoroom's generative AI platform, spanning model orchestration, evaluation, agentic workflows, and foundation model training, enabling our teams to ship breakthrough AI products faster than anyone else. You'll partner closely with our Infrastructure team on inference infrastructure and model serving, rather than owning that layer outright.

This is a highly strategic leadership role combining strong technical grounding, organisational leadership, and product thinking. Deep technical expertise already exists across our ML and Research teams, so we're not looking for the single deepest expert in the room, we're looking for someone who has been hands-on in ML or research themselves, understands the space well enough to lead a credible technical conversation and make sound calls, and can create the conditions for that expertise to thrive. You'll work closely with our CTO and senior leaders across Product and Engineering to shape how AI is built, deployed, and scaled across the company.

Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity

Location: Paris, France (Hybrid)

Relocation: Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000 available

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be responsible for building both the technical foundations and the organisation that enable Photoroom's next generation of AI products.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Defining the long-term vision and technical strategy for our GenAI Platform around model orchestration, evaluation, agentic workflows and foundation model training

 - Partnering with our Infrastructure team on inference infrastructure, model serving and reliability, so the platform stays scalable and cost-efficient across billions of inference requests

 - Partnering with Research to rapidly bring new models into production

 - Leading and growing a multidisciplinary team of ML Engineers, Software Engineers and Researchers, setting direction for the team as a whole, while day-to-day management of individual contributors continues through the team's existing engineering leads

 - Creating an environment where ambitious technical ideas can move from research to production in days rather than months

 - Building evaluation frameworks that measure model quality, cost and latency consistently across the platform

 - Working closely with Product, Engineering and Executive leadership to ensure platform investments directly accelerate product innovation
 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

We're looking for someone with strong technical grounding and proven leadership experience. You don't need to be the foremost technical authority in every area, as that depth already exists in the team, but you should have been a hands-on ML/research practitioner at some point in your career, ideally with some research experience, so you can lead the function credibly.

You'll likely have:

 - Significant experience leading Machine Learning or AI organisations within product-focused companies, having started your career as a hands-on ML engineer or researcher before moving into leadership

 - Experience building and operating AI platforms: model orchestration, evaluation pipelines or agent frameworks, with enough grounding in inference infrastructure and model serving to partner effectively with an Infrastructure team, without needing to own that layer directly

 - Strong technical expertise across Generative AI, Computer Vision or Foundation Models

 - A track record of taking emerging technologies from research into production systems used by millions of users. We don't expect deep, specific agentic-workflow experience, the field is relatively new and nobody has a long track record there, but we do want evidence you can effectively leverage new technologies to productise what's next

 - Experience growing high-performing engineering and research teams through hiring, coaching and organisational design

 - Enough technical depth to follow and meaningfully contribute to an architecture conversation outside your core area, you don't need all the answers, but you must understand the building blocks well enough to ask the right questions and make a call when needed

 - Strong product instincts and the ability to balance long-term technical investments against immediate customer impact

 - Excellent communication skills and experience partnering with Product, Engineering, Marketing and Executive stakeholders
 
 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within your first 12-18 months, you'll have:

 - Established a clear long-term strategy for Photoroom's AI platform

 - Built infrastructure that significantly reduces the time required to ship new AI capabilities

 - Enabled research teams to move new models into production rapidly and reliably

 - Improved platform performance, reliability and infrastructure efficiency at scale, in close partnership with the Infrastructure team

 - Built and retained a world-class team of ML Engineers, Researchers and Platform Engineers

 - Created evaluation frameworks that allow model quality, cost and latency to be measured consistently across the platform

 - Helped define the technical direction that underpins the next generation of AI-powered products

jobs.title: Events Lead
jobs.description:
At Solve Intelligence, events aren't a marketing side-quest. They're our #1 growth channel.

We're doing 70+ conferences this year, we just hosted 100 of Silicon Valley's biggest tech companies in one room, and we're ready to invest serious capital to go much bigger. Now we need someone to own the whole machine.

🏗️ THE ROLE: EVENTS LEAD

Just ~3 years since launch, we are adding 7 figures of ARR per month, we have raised ~$60M USD, and we are quadrupling headcount this year. In-person events drive more of that growth than any other channel. Until now, they've been run part-time by the founders and our GTM team.

You'll be our first dedicated events hire, based in London and working directly with the founders. Your job is to own events end-to-end; the commercial events that drive pipeline, the flagship we want the IP industry talking about for years, and the hackathons and meetups that pull the best AI engineers into Solve's orbit. Much of it you'll coordinate remotely from London; for the ones that matter, you'll be there.

What you'll own:

 - Strategy & ROI: Own Solve's global events strategy end-to-end — across GTM, talent, and brand — and the return on every dollar spent. Treat each event as an experiment: measure it with our growth marketer, triple down on what works, kill what doesn't.

 - Conferences (our #1 channel): Lead our presence at the 70+ industry conferences we sponsor each year across the US, Europe, and Asia (AIPLA, INTA, IPO, EPO) — booths, speaking slots, and the dinners and drinks receptions around them.

 - The Flagship: Build Solve's annual flagship event from zero — concept, audience, partnerships, content, on-the-day execution. We recently hosted 100 of the largest Silicon Valley tech companies (Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft) for a closed-door panel and networking evening; think ElevenLabs-Summit scale next, with real capital behind it.

 - Curated gatherings: Founder dinners, customer roundtables, rooftop socials, and product-launch moments across London, New York, and Munich.

 - Talent & employer brand: Hackathons, technical meetups, university partnerships, and our presence at AI conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) — bringing the best AI engineers and researchers into Solve's orbit, in partnership with our Talent team.

 - Operational excellence: Vendors, budgets, logistics, run-of-show, and post-event follow-up — all handled without drop.

 - AI-powered event ops: Scale a traditionally high-touch function with AI — attendee research, follow-up sequences, content repurposing — and partner with our RevOps engineers to wire every event into HubSpot and Ashby with full attribution.

💡 ABOUT SOLVE INTELLIGENCE

We are the fastest-growing startup transforming Intellectual Property. Our AI platform handles everything from invention harvesting and patent generation through to litigation and licensing.

 - Growth: 20–30% MoM revenue growth; 8 figures of ARR just ~3 years since launch.

 - Market: 600+ IP teams across 6 continents, including Tier-1 firms like DLA Piper, tech giants, and boutiques.

 - Impact: Users report 50–90% efficiency and quality improvements.

 - Backing: ~$60M from Y Combinator, 20VC, Microsoft, Thomson Reuters, and the founders of top companies like Stripe, Perplexity, Tinder, Deel, Hugging Face, and Canva. See our Series B announcement https://www.solveintelligence.com/blog/post/solve-intelligence-raises-40m-series-b-to-build-ai-for-patents-and-launches-charts.

👋 WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

You'll work directly with the founders, alongside our GTM, RevOps, and Talent teams:

 - Sanj https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanj-ahilan-844b33137/ (CRO): PhD in AI (Gatsby Unit, UCL), ex-Huawei R&D, former lead at Magic Carpet AI (acquired).

 - Chris https://www.linkedin.com/in/chris-parsonson/ (CEO): PhD in AI (UCL), published researcher, ex-Dyson and Alan Turing Institute.

 - Angus https://www.linkedin.com/in/angus-parsonson/ (CTO): MEng Computer Science, ex-Qualcomm and Coremont (Brevan Howard).

🚀 WHO YOU ARE

We are a high-performance culture. To thrive here:

 - You're a scrappy, entrepreneurial owner: From sourcing the venue to printing the name badges, nothing is beneath you — you'd rather run the experiment this month than perfect the plan for next quarter.

 - You're a born host: You love bringing people together, and it shows — people leave your events talking about them.

 - You think in ROI: Every event is a bet with a number attached. You're comfortable being measured on pipeline, hires, and brand — and killing your own ideas when the numbers say so.

 - You have high agency: There's no playbook and no events team behind you (yet). You spot the opportunity, own it, and deliver it.

 - You leverage AI everywhere: Research, ops, follow-ups — you use AI to do the work of a small team, and it's why one of you is enough.

 - You're all-in: Solve is fast and intense, and this isn't a 9–5 (events rarely are). You get obsessive about the details that make something memorable.

🛠️ WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Haves:

 - A track record of running events people remember — conferences, summits, hackathons, or community events — owned end-to-end, with results you can point to.

 - Commercial instinct: You can show how events you've run contributed to pipeline, revenue, or hires — with numbers.

 - Serious operational rigour: Vendors, budgets, logistics, run-of-show, and follow-up all handled without drop.

 - Comfort with a global remit: You'll coordinate events across three continents from London, and travel internationally for the ones that matter.

 - Exceptionally clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred & Nice-to-Haves:

 - High-growth experience: You've run events at a fast-growing B2B SaaS or AI company and know what good looks like.

 - Flagship from zero: You've designed and launched an annual flagship event from scratch — concept, audience, format, brand.

 - Technical events: Hackathons, meetups, or developer-facing events at an AI or dev-tools co

jobs.title: Account Executive, New Business
jobs.description:
ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE, NEW BUSINESS

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

THE ROLE

You are the proof. AI now does most of the work of getting a business quoted and covered at Harper — but a human still closes, and that human is you. You sit at the exact line where the machine hands off to judgment: you take warmed, qualified small-business owners and turn them into customers, on the phone, at volume, all day.

This is high-velocity SMB sales, not enterprise. Short cycles, fast decisions, no procurement committees. The number you move is revenue, and you move it by talking to a lot of people and closing a lot of them. As we get better at converting judgment into software, your job is to close what the system surfaces today — and to show us where a human still beats the machine, so we can teach it that part next.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Close SMB deals at volume. 100+ calls a day with small business owners. Learn the playbook in week one, beat it by week two. You're measured on policies closed and revenue generated — nothing softer.

 - Sell with the tools, not around them. Use Harper's AI to prep, qualify, and follow up so your conversion holds when the call count climbs. When a tool slows you down, you say so; when you find an edge the tool should learn, you write it down.

 - Hold your close rate at scale. Call 100 gets the same sharpness as call 1. Quality doesn't decay as volume goes up.

 - Expand into new lines. As Harper adds insurance products, you close across them. The book grows; so does what you can sell.

 - Make yourself reproducible. The way you handle an objection, sequence a pitch, or save a deal becomes input the company keeps — playbook, prompt, or process. Your best instincts shouldn't live only in your head.
 
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - You've built a career closing SMB and you understand how small business owners think, decide, and buy — and you earn their trust fast.

 - You're a closer first, with a real track record of closing at high velocity and high volume. 100+ calls a day is a rhythm you've lived, not a number that scares you.

 - Your close rate doesn't fall apart when the volume doubles.

 - You're comfortable being measured hard, in public, on revenue.

 - You treat AI as leverage — using it to prep and qualify faster — and you have opinions about where it helps and where it gets in the way.

 - You don't need insurance experience on day one. We'll teach you. You'll get licensed fast (we pay for it).

 - Ex-founders and operators who've built something from nothing tend to do well here.

THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY

This job is the phone. ~5am–7pm, Monday–Friday, on-site in San Francisco, in the building with the team. 100+ calls a day, every day. You'll need a commercial insurance producer license within roughly your first 30 days — we pay for the training and the exam, but you have to pass it, fast, while you're also ramping on the phones.

The hours are long and the pace is relentless because the company is growing ~100x and the sales engine can't lag the rest of the rebuild. Almost no one takes this job because they love insurance. The people who thrive here love closing, love being measured, and want a front-row seat to an AI-native company being built at full speed. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.

COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS

 - Salary: $150,000–$200,000 OTE. Top performers earn more.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based here or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, very early morning start, in-office 5 days a week.

 - Licensing: Commercial insurance producer license required within ~30 days of start; Harper pays for training and licensing.

BENEFITS

 - Uber commuter benefits

 - Meals provided — breakfast, lunch, and dinner

 - Snacks, drinks, and coffee stocked daily

 - Free gym membership

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

PROCESS

 1. Lead screen — fit and alignment

 2. Founder screen — skills and judgment

 3. Super day — how you actually operate, in real time

TO APPLY

Send your resume and tell us about the hardest deal you closed at volume — what almost killed it, and what you did on the call to save it.

jobs.title: Research Product Manager (RPM)
jobs.description:
ABOUT ABUNDANT

Abundant is an applied research lab focused on scaling reinforcement learning for safe and reliable agentic capabilities. We are an extremely talent-dense team of researchers, roboticists, founders, and operators whose work includes the Waymo Driver.

THE ROLE

Research PM (RPM) is a role unique to Abundant. RPMs are PMs of the model, unlike traditional PMs who own an application or a feature. RPMs design and implement model capabilities, either as part of an AI lab, data lab, or other research organization. This is a founding-level role with outsized ownership.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Co-design capabilities of the model: define areas of improvement for the model, along with the Researcher.

 - Perform literature review: headroom analysis, identifying recent work in academic and industry circles.

 - Run experiments and benchmarks: using our internal simulation stack and our open source tooling such as Oddish to define and hillclimb on the vertical.

 - Become the voice of the model user: Talk to individual users and/or enterprises, in order to deeply understand where models and agents are underperforming, turning these insights into evaluation and training data.

 - Work on data pipelines: internal tooling to support research operations.

WHO YOU ARE

 - Technically fluent: Deep understanding of evaluations, RL, and how LLMs and Agents work.

 - Research-oriented — Able to read papers and keep up with SOTA literature.

 - Extreme owner — You have extreme agency and a founder mentality; you are resourceful and scrappy.

 - Creative problem solver — You leverage creativity and research skills to design projects from the ground up.

 - Must be highly proficient with coding agents such as Codex or Claude Code.

 

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$150,000 - $210,000

Cash Bonus

Sizable performance bonus tied to project and company milestones

Equity

Meaningful early-stage grant

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Research
jobs.description:
ABOUT ABUNDANT

Abundant is an applied research lab focused on scaling reinforcement learning for safe and reliable agentic capabilities. We are an extremely talent-dense team of researchers, roboticists, founders, and operators whose work includes the Waymo Driver.

 

THE ROLE

You will own a research agenda where research meets production, co-designing strategies with researchers from frontier AI labs. You are the “PM of the model”: you pick the problem, design the data and reward signal that moves it, and see it through to a live training run. The job rewards a founder mentality and extreme ownership, including going into unfamiliar domains, from chemical engineering to complex legal logic, and getting to ground truth fast on problems others have written off.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Foundational capability research and execution. Architect and execute a research agenda to find simple, generalizable ideas that advance model reasoning at scale, and own it from hypothesis through to running in live systems.

 - Design tasks and verifiers that stay hard. Build long-horizon agentic tasks that are still difficult a model generation from now, with graders where partial credit means something and the obvious exploit does not score.

 - Diagnose failure modes. Read trajectories until you can say why a model fails a class of work, then turn that into the data or reward signal that fixes it. This is the core loop of the job.

 - Model alignment and data strategy. Partner with the world’s most advanced AI research teams on datasets and benchmarks that shape how frontier models behave, focused on alignment, safety, and reward signal design.

 - Autonomous problem selection. Identify, scope, and run long projects, choosing the problems that matter most for scaling data toward AGI.

 - System infrastructure. Work with engineering on data pipelines, internal tooling, and deep learning implementations. If a workflow produces bad data, you fix the workflow.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You write a lot of code. Strong software engineering and deep Python, comfortable owning a system end to end and debugging through layers you did not write.

 - You have built evaluations, RL environments, agent harnesses, verifiers, or execution sandboxes, and you have opinions about which of them can be trusted.

 - You have shipped research into production, particularly post-training, distillation, and high-stakes evaluation.

 - You have worked on large-scale agent systems: orchestration frameworks, tool APIs, distributed execution, observability, and logging.

 - You get to ground truth in an unfamiliar domain by building something and reading outputs, not by reading about it.

 - You notice the misspecified task, the ambiguous prompt, and the grader that can be gamed.

 - You have a thoughtful perspective on the societal and safety impacts of deploying general-purpose AI systems.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - A PhD (CS, ML, NLP) and publications at NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR. Neither is required.

 - Work on public benchmarks or task suites, for example Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench-style harnesses, or HCAST.

 - RLHF or RLAIF experience and a view on how training choices show up in model behavior.

 - Experience running work through large expert or annotation operations.

COMPENSATION

Base Salary

$250,000 - $450,000

Cash Bonus

Sizable performance bonus tied to project and company milestones

Equity

Generous early-stage grant

Benefits

Health, dental, vision + flexible PTO

jobs.description:
ABOUT CARIBOU

International Tax is a rigged system. Tax rules get ever more complicated, compliance gets more expensive, and the Big Four controls the expertise. They charge fees that only giant companies can afford, while smaller businesses are left flying blind.

Caribou is a tax platform designed to make international tax accessible to every global business. We're fixing Transfer Pricing first, where one million businesses are in need, but only ten thousand experts exist. R&D relief is our next product.

Our backers include Y Combinator, Accel, Lakestar and angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies in London and San Francisco.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Caribou is building a new R&D tax offering at the intersection of transfer pricing and innovation funding — and we're looking for a Senior Manager to own it end-to-end.

This isn't a pure advisory role. You'll be working alongside our engineering team to productize the service: systematising claim processes, building tooling, and turning what used to be manual consulting work into something scalable. The mix of hands-on R&D tax advisory with product instinct is what makes this different from a standard tax consultancy position. We're looking for someone who's been in the trenches with HMRC and/or the IRS on R&D claims, with a passion for building things that don't exist yet.

You'll report directly to our Head of Tax, James Boreham, and have real ownership of the vertical from day one.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Liaise directly with customers to assess R&D eligibility and understand their business.

 - Own the end-to-end claim process, from notification of intent to claim through advance assurance, drafting, submission, and defending claims under enquiry.

 - Translate your real-world claims experience into rules, checklists, and logic that can be built into an automated product.

 - Identify what proof and documentation a claim actually needs to withstand scrutiny, and work with the team to design data capture that gets it right the first time.

 - Explain R&D concepts to non-specialists, ranging from founders to operations leads, to accountants.

 - Coordinate with a customer's other advisors, including bookkeepers, lawyers and other tax experts.

 - Shape the R&D product itself - pricing, scope, and what should be automated versus handled by a specialist.

 - Determine a customer's reporting obligations and build the workflows that generate the necessary documents.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

 - Meaningful hands-on experience with HMRC and/or IRS R&D claims, including defending claims under enquiry

 - Deep practical understanding of what proof and evidence a tax authority actually requires, beyond the written guidance

 - You take ownership and enjoy driving multiple projects involving a wider range of stakeholders

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment with ambiguous and rapidly evolving priorities

BONUS POINTS

 - Experience across both UK and US R&D regimes

 - Startup experience

PERKS & BENEFITS (FOR UK-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES)

 - Competitive salary

 - Generous EMI options

 - 100% book subsidy

 - Pension

 - Health Insurance

 - Custom WFH equipment setup
 

London-based, hybrid.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Payments
jobs.description:
We are making travel effortless. Join us.

Whether it's to visit the people closest to us, starting an exciting adventure, or a career-defining business trip, travel is an essential part of our lives. Yet we've all experienced the aches and pains of getting to our destination. Today, more than 4 billion airline passengers rely on technology that hasn't kept up with the expectations of the modern connected traveller.

That's why we've started to rebuild the infrastructure that underpins the travel industry. We're on a mission to unravel travel, simplifying systems and building the tools that will make the future of travel effortless.

We were part of Y Combinator S18's cohort and we are backed by Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures and Kima Ventures, a fantastic set of investors that has helped build some of the world's largest companies.

Payments at Duffel

Our Payments team looks after the infrastructure that powers our travel operations: payment acceptance, supplier settlement, reconciliation, commission tracking and payouts, billing, and more. These are some of the hardest and most interesting challenges Duffel is facing as we operate as a global travel platform.

About the role

As the Product Manager for Payments, you'll own the roadmap for the operational backbone of our Payments product. The role is largely internal. You'll work closely with Finance, Engineering, and Operations to optimise settlement, billing, commissions and reconciliation, and to build the platform services that other Duffel teams, and eventually external partners, rely on. There's a customer-facing dimension too, but the bulk of the work is making the inside of the product as well-engineered as the outside.

You'll spend most of your time with engineering, define the weekly goals and milestones for the product squad, work closely with internal stakeholders (Finance especially), and bring real depth to a team that values getting the detail right. You'll own the overall Payments roadmap, to shape where your areas go next, including parts of the product we've barely touched yet.

What we're looking for

 - You're fluent in payments without being wedded to the rails. You understand how money moves (settlement, reconciliation, commissions, FX, chargebacks) but you're more energised by building great internal product on top of that than by optimising payment rails for their own sake.

 - You're a builder. Most of what this team needs, we build rather than buy. You like designing the systems, automated commission flows, supplier reconciliation, billing, that Finance, Operations and eventually external partners rely on.

 - You translate between worlds. A big part of this job is sitting between Finance and Engineering: turning finance narratives into technical requirements, technical realities into language Finance and Ops can act on, and getting both sides to genuinely understand each other.

 - You prioritise ruthlessly. This is a small, in-demand team (three engineers) constantly trading internal needs against customer-facing work. You're good at deciding what matters now and saying no to the rest.

 - You sweat the detail. Reconciliation logic, commission edge cases, audit trails: this is the kind of work that energises you rather than drains you.

 - You shape product direction. You can take a roadmap area, work out where it should go and why, and drive it.

 - You've got commercial instinct. You can spot when something we've built for ourselves (like reconciliation) could become a product customers would pay for.

 - You're API-literate. You don't need to write code, but you can have a meaningful conversation with engineering about how systems actually work.

 - You handle ambiguity, breaking complex, undefined problems into a clear way forward, and use both quantitative and qualitative analysis to back your calls.

 - You think being challenged on your assumptions makes you better, and that challenging others helps them grow.

 - Nice to have: exposure to travel-specific payments (BSP, IATA, virtual cards, agency settlement). Useful, not essential.

Some reasons why you’ll love working here:

🏡 Work From Anywhere - work abroad for part of the year

🛩️ Duffel Travel Allowance - because building in travel should come with travel perks

🍼 Enhanced parental leave

🧘 Sabbatical options - proper time to recharge

🪩 A Shoreditch office near Liverpool Street + regular team socials

💰 Competitive salary + potential equity

 

You’ll join a smart, kind, ambitious team building something meaningful in travel with real ownership, autonomy, and the chance to shape how we hire as we scale and we think that’s pretty exciting.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Your goal is to shorten the path to value for Ploy customers. To achieve this goal, you'll own account strategy, implementation, onboarding, training and support for Ploy customers.

 - Lead customer onboarding end-to-end: kickoff, requirements, setup, launch, and handoff

 - Configure and validate the customer’s setup in Ploy:
 
 - Design system / brand system setup
 
 - Knowledge base setup (structure + initial content hygiene)
 
 - Core integrations setup and verification
 
 - Initial “ploybooks” configuration and scheduled ploys that match the customer’s goals

 - Provide Ploy customers with advice and best practices to get the most out of Ploy

 - Turn customer goals into an implementation plan with clear milestones and owners

 - Identify blockers early (data, access, content, approvals) and drive resolution

 - Build repeatable onboarding playbooks and continuously improve the process based on what breaks

 - Be the voice of the customer to Product/Engineering: patterns, gaps, and high-impact fixes

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Customers launch on time with a working, correct setup (brand system, KB, integrations, initial ploys)

 - Customers reach “first value” quickly (they can point to a tangible outcome in the first week or two)

 - Fewer onboarding escalations and less founder/engineering involvement over time

 - Onboarding becomes more standardized, measurable, and repeatable

WHO YOU ARE

 - A strong operator. You run a tight process, keep multiple stakeholders moving, and don't let things fall through the cracks.

 - Web-native. You have real web design experience — you understand design systems, brand guidelines, and how good web execution actually works. This isn't something you'll learn on the job; it's the foundation of your credibility with customers.

 - Technically comfortable. You're not an engineer, but you can troubleshoot integrations, navigate data issues, and figure out product workflows independently.

 - A great communicator. Crisp docs, clear status updates, confident customer calls. Customers feel like they're in good hands because they are.

 - High ownership. You don't wait for perfect instructions. You figure it out and ship.

 - Customer-obsessed: You care about outcomes and you proactively prevent surprises.

BACKGROUND WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required:

 - 2–4 years of experience in a web design, digital marketing, or agency environment — you've built or overseen web properties and understand what makes them work

 - Strong marketing fundamentals: web design, SEO, CRO, performance marketing/ads, and related growth channels

 - Demonstrated ability to manage client relationships and complex, multi-stakeholder projects

Nice to have:

 - Experience in customer success, onboarding, implementations, or solutions engineering in B2B SaaS

 - Familiarity with design systems, branding workflows, and/or knowledge base tooling

 - Experience at an early-stage startup with fast iteration loops

WORKING STYLE

This is a cross-functional role. You'll work closely with Sales (warm handoff), Product and Engineering (customer feedback loop), and customers directly — both on calls and heads-down inside the product configuring real setups.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
