jobs.title: Technical Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARTOS:

At Artos, we build tools that help biopharma companies create and manage their R&D documentation in a fraction of the time. If you’re looking to join a team whose mission is to fundamentally change the way that drug development gets done, we’d love to talk to you.

THE ROLE:

We’re looking for a Technical Solutions Engineer who brings a strong mix of DevOps, software engineering, and customer-facing skills to help customers deploy, operate, and scale Artos.

You’ll troubleshoot across the full stack, from Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, networking, and deployment configuration to the Artos platform itself. When something breaks, you’ll determine whether the problem lives in the customer’s environment, our application, or somewhere in between, then dig into the logs, configuration, infrastructure, and code to find the root cause.

You’ll work directly with customer engineering teams while partnering closely with Artos Engineering to reproduce issues, resolve bugs, and improve the reliability and supportability of the platform.

This is a great fit for someone who enjoys moving between infrastructure and application-level debugging and is equally comfortable working directly with customers to solve complex technical problems.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Lead technical deployments of Artos into customer-managed AWS, Azure, and GCP environments.

 - Configure and troubleshoot Kubernetes, containers, networking, IAM, authentication, secrets, and other deployment dependencies.

 - Diagnose issues across customer infrastructure, Artos application services, APIs, integrations, and application behavior.

 - Use logs, metrics, traces, and code-level debugging to isolate root causes and drive issues through resolution.

 - Reproduce application issues, investigate bugs, contribute to bug reports, validate fixes, and partner with Artos Engineering on resolution.

 - Build and maintain deployment automation and infrastructure-as-code using Terraform and related tooling.

 - Partner directly with customer DevOps, infrastructure, engineering, and security teams throughout deployment and ongoing operation.

 - Improve CI/CD workflows, monitoring, observability, and operational tooling that make Artos easier to deploy and support.

 - Own customer-facing technical documentation, including installation and deployment guides, architecture documentation, runbooks, and security review materials.
 
 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 5+ years of experience in solutions engineering, DevOps, SRE, platform engineering, software engineering, cloud infrastructure, or a similar technical role.

 - Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, and cloud infrastructure.

 - Experience deploying and supporting production applications on AWS, Azure, or GCP.

 - Software engineering skills and the ability to debug application-level issues rather than treating the application as a black box.

 - Ability to work with and troubleshoot APIs, application services, integrations, logs, and distributed systems.

 - Ability to write and debug code or automation using TypeScript, Python, Bash, or similar languages.

 - Strong understanding of networking, IAM, authentication, secrets management, and cloud security fundamentals.

 - Familiarity with CI/CD, monitoring, logging, and observability tooling.

 - Strong communication skills and experience working directly with customer engineering teams.

 - Ability to independently take ambiguous technical problems from initial customer report through root cause and resolution.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with BYOC, self-hosted, or private-cloud deployments.

 - Experience supporting technical enterprise SaaS products.

 - Experience with Helm, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, or similar tooling.

 - Experience investigating or fixing bugs in a production software codebase.

 - Experience with enterprise security or compliance reviews.

 - Familiarity with AI/LLM infrastructure or ML platforms.

 - Experience in life sciences, healthcare, or another regulated industry.

Other Information:

Very comfortable working in a fast-paced and intense startup environment

Willing to work in-person in our office in Mission Bay 4-5 days/week

Likes matcha KitKats, believes every LLM prompt is just Schrödinger’s cat waiting to be observed, and knows too many random facts about the Mongol postal system

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
JOIN US IN BUILDING THE FUTURE OF DIGITAL WORK

At Sola, we’re transforming the way work is done. We’re developing AI agents that make powerful automation effortless, enabling any user to record a workflow and instantly scale it up to millions of executions.

Sola today powers enterprise workflows in Fortune 100 companies, with a horizontal platform that works across healthcare, finance, legal, logistics, and more. We’ve raised $21M in funding from a16z, Conviction (Sarah Guo), and Y Combinator, and are looking for passionate builders to help us continue to scale.

If you’re interested in being on the forefront of agentic automation, we’d love to hear from you!

WHAT TO EXPECT 

Our goal is to bring Figma-level UI/UX excellence to enterprise AI workflow automation. Sola's automations run in real enterprise environments under complex constraints: they need to be intelligent and self-directed, but also predictable and consistent.

The questions you'll own are at the forefront of AI today:

 - From the execution perspective, what should an agent be trusted to do, where does a human stay in the loop, and how do we make non-deterministic models operate reliably at scale?

 - From the building perspective, how can we make automation at scale easy for users in the world’s largest enterprises? How do we make enterprise automation feel as intuitive and elegant as the best consumer and creative tools? How do we design experiences that help non-technical users understand complex workflows, collaborate across teams, and trust AI doing real work on their behalf?

As our first dedicated product hire, you'll partner closely with our CEO and Head of Engineering to turn a fast-moving space into a clear, opinionated roadmap, own features end-to-end from customer problem to shipped product, and help define not just what we build but how we do product as the team grows. This is a job for a builder, not a backlog manager.

We work in person at our NYC HQ, and you'll work directly with the founders to help shape the company's future.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 - Partner with our CEO, design, and engineering to set product strategy and own the roadmap, balancing near-term needs with long-term vision.

 - Drive features end-to-end: requirements, crisp specs, stakeholder alignment, and keeping design, engineering, and go-to-market in lockstep.

 - Talk to users constantly, turning their pain points into a clear sense of what's most valuable to build next.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 - You have 5+ years of experience 

 - Sharp product judgment paired with genuine design taste: a high bar for elegant, simple user experiences, and the instinct to sweat the details.

 - Enough technical fluency to go deep on a genuinely technical product domain and partner with engineering as a peer.

 - A clear, concise communicator who brings structure to ambiguity and can represent both users and engineering tradeoffs to any audience.

 - AI fluency: you explore and prototype with the latest AI tools, and you can reason about model capabilities well enough to make product calls.

 - You're open to working 5 days a week out of our office in NYC (we'll cover relocation!)

WHY SOLA 

 - $21M raised from top-tier VCs (a16z, Conviction, YCombinator) and growing incredibly fast

 - Proven traction with Fortune 100 customers, with horizontal applicability across a variety of domains (including finance, healthcare, legal, logistics, and more)

 - Leading-edge agentic AI tech, solving deep problems in partnership with the AI labs (ex. Anthropic https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7426684058077855744/?originTrackingId=gMllhO4VY3OEPmt2do6k3g%3D%3D, AWS AGI Lab https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7402073015020310528/)

 - Small team, early stage, with an opportunity for outsized impact on the company’s future

 - Work closely with founders Jessica Wu (ex-Citadel, Thrive Capital) and Neil Deshmukh (MIT Quest for Intelligence Lab), alongside David Fullerton (ex-CTO Heap, Stack Overflow)

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Sola offers competitive salary plus meaningful equity at Series A stage. Exact compensation is based on experience and level.

We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) matching, daily meals together in the office, flexible PTO (4 weeks per year), and relocation support for candidates not already based in NYC.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Dedalus Labs builds persistent computers for AI agents. Our flagship product, Dedalus Machines, gives agents an isolated environment where they can run software, keep files and state, and work over time.

We're looking for someone who keeps asking what happens underneath an API, a process, or a virtual machine, then reads and experiments until they can explain it. You'll make scoped improvements to our control plane or Rust virtual machine monitor (VMM), the software that runs virtual machines. You'll work with engineers who care about correctness and performance.

ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP

This is a paid, full-time internship or co-op in San Francisco lasting 3-9 months, depending on the program and agreed scope. Applications are open throughout the year, including off-cycle terms. Share your available start date and duration. You'll work alongside Dedalus engineers with direct feedback on your implementation and decisions.

We want evidence that you can learn something difficult, finish a working version, and improve it when the first approach fails. You do not need prior production ownership. You should already have a project you understand well enough to explain its hardest bug, its limits, and your personal contribution.

Your main work will be fixing bugs and papercuts, simplifying code, improving tests and tooling, and making focused speed improvements. You will work within existing systems with support from an engineer. This is how you learn the codebase and our standards. Responsibility grows as you demonstrate sound judgment, reliable execution, and clear communication.

WORK YOU MIGHT TAKE ON

 - A reproducible investigation into a slow startup, restore, or I/O path. Establish a baseline, isolate the bottleneck, and measure a focused change.

 - A runtime or storage improvement with tests for cancellation, resource cleanup, or recovery after a process stops.

 - A failure-injection test that exposes an incorrect ordering or lifecycle assumption and verifies the repair.

 - A small refactor that removes repeated work, reduces allocations, or makes a slow code path easier to measure.

The project will have an agreed scope and completion criteria. Finishing includes code, tests, an explanation of the decisions, and a handoff another engineer can use.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

You can build and debug software in Rust, Go, C, C++, or a similar language. Rust is preferred but not required. You have a working understanding of memory, concurrency, data structures, and the operating-system behavior your project depends on.

Relevant work might be a small storage engine, networking tool, runtime, compiler, operating-system component, or performance investigation. Coursework, research, employment, open source, and independent projects all count. Explain what you personally implemented and what you learned beyond the initial instructions.

When you get stuck, you narrow the problem, read the relevant source or documentation, and try an experiment that can teach you something. You ask for help with the evidence you've collected and explain what you need to understand next. You act on feedback and keep ownership of the result.

You use AI coding tools where they help. You must be able to explain the resulting code, test its behavior, and correct it when it is wrong. We care about your judgment and understanding throughout the work.

THIS INTERNSHIP MAY BE A POOR FIT IF

 - You want a tutorial with every implementation step supplied.

 - You cannot explain or debug the code in the project you submit.

 - You lose interest after the first successful run, before checking failure cases or documenting what remains incomplete.

LOGISTICS

Paid, full-time, and in person in San Francisco for an agreed term of 3-9 months. In-person attendance is required. Applications are accepted year-round. Relocation assistance may be available, with details agreed individually. Tell us your expected graduation date and when you could start full-time. Interns who demonstrate strong work, judgment, ownership, and mutual fit may be considered for full-time roles. Conversion is not guaranteed.

SHOW US YOUR WORK

Use your application to show us one thing you built and one difficult problem you investigated. They can come from the same project. Choose work you already have. We are not asking you to build a new project for this application.

 - Work: Show the code, demo, design, or result. Explain what you personally owned, what you reused, and one decision that made the result better or simpler.

 - Investigation: Describe the symptom, your first explanation, the evidence that changed your thinking, and how you established the result. Include the workload or users involved and any important limitations.

 - Writing: Share one piece of writing you care about as a separate, required sample. Any medium or length is welcome. Tell us why you wrote it, who it was for, and what you wanted to communicate. Looking back, what works well and what would you change? We care about the quality of your thinking and writing, and your reflection on the work. Link it or paste a redacted excerpt. Explain your contribution and any coauthors or AI assistance.

Work from employment, open source, research, coursework, or independent projects is welcome. Public source code is optional. A redacted excerpt or a concrete account of private work is fine. Keep confidential information out of your application.

Tell us which problem in this role you want to own and why. If your strongest evidence is easy to miss on a resume, point us to it. An existing demo or short screen recording is welcome, and video is optional.

COMPENSATION

Off-cycle internships pay $30-$40 per hour. Summer internships pay $45-$50 per hour. Actual pay is based on hours worked. At 40 hours per week, this is approximately $5,200-$6,933 per month off-cycle or $7,800-$8,667 per month in summer. We agree the applicable rate and dates before the internship begins.

ABOUT CTGT & THE MISSION

Despite massive investment in commercial AI, organizations often find that demonstrated value is elusive, primarily due to the non-deterministic risk inherent to generative models. CTGT is the deterministic governance layer that enables the most important global institutions to deploy AI workflows with confidence.

Born out of Stanford University research, we provide the control plane that makes it possible. A lightweight, model-agnostic system that enforces policy, prevents drift, and produces auditable decisions in real time. When benchmarked on HaluEval, the CTGT Policy Engine (paired with GPT-120B OSS) outperformed frontier models (Gemini 3 Pro Preview, Claude 4.5 Opus and 4.5 Sonnet) at drastically lower compute cost.

While we sit on the edge of AI research, CTGT brings frontier intelligence into real-world environments. We apply cutting-edge theory directly in production to make large language models more reliable, controllable, and performant in practice.

Our mission is to bring models to the level of performance and accountability required by the Fortune 500. By bridging the gap between LLM capabilities and domain-specific requirements, we unlock the true potential of generative AI to solve the most pressing problems in our world today.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
At Parallel, we build AI agents that help healthcare organizations automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.

Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost to manual, repetitive administrative tasks. Legacy software hasn't helped: it has made work slower, more complex and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change this. Our technology combines large language models with system-level automation to do real work inside existing hospital tools. No integration, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding and frees up time for medical teams to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024 and already have 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people. We are backed by top-tier investors (Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI), and this is just the beginning.

The future of healthcare isn't just digital, it's automated. Come help us build it!

CONTEXT

Up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work — and the AI systems that can fix it only matter if they actually run in production, inside real hospitals, on sensitive health data. Building that is the heart of this role.

This is an AI Engineer role: you won't just write models, you'll shape Parallel's core AI architecture, define our machine learning strategy, and embed intelligent systems directly into hospital workflows. You'll work hand in hand with the CTO and the founding team, with very high ownership over everything from agentic LLM workflows to the way AI outputs land in the tools doctors actually use.

YOUR MISSION

Design and deploy production-ready AI systems — LLM-powered and agent-based — that automate medical coding and reduce administrative workload in hospitals, owning each feature from prototype to monitoring.

OUTCOMES

 - Production LLM systems: design and deploy LLM-powered systems that automate medical coding in real clinical environments.

 - Agentic workflows: build and iterate on agent-based workflows tailored to complex clinical operations.

 - Secure data pipelines: work with hospital IT to build secure, scalable data ingestion pipelines that adhere to health-data security standards.

 - Product integration: integrate AI outputs into the apps used by doctors and hospital staff.

 - AI roadmap & full ownership: partner with the CTO to define the AI roadmap, and own the full lifecycle of each AI feature — research, prototyping, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.

WHO YOU ARE :

This job is for you if:

 - You have 3+ years working on applied ML/AI problems in production environments — real systems that run, not just POCs.

 - You have strong experience with LLMs and NLP, including prompt engineering and/or fine-tuning.

 - You're proficient in Python or Node.js and have worked with ML libraries (Hugging Face, LangChain, PyTorch, etc.).

 - You have a deep sense of ownership and can move from prototype to product quickly.

 - You're action-oriented and autonomous, and you thrive in a fast-paced startup where you shape the core, not execute tickets.

 - You care about solving user problems over shipping features, and you're comfortable getting close to the product and its users.

 - Bonus: familiarity with backend services (Node.js/TypeScript) and data infrastructure.

 - Bonus: experience working with sensitive or regulated data (healthcare, finance, etc.).

HIRING PROCESS

 1. Quick chat with Wallerand, our recruiter (30 min)

 2. Chat with our CTO, Chris (30 min)

 3. AI / technical case study, in person at our Paris office (60 min)

 4. Meeting with our CEO, Paul (30 min)

WHY SHOULD YOU JOIN US?

 - A rare opportunity: you shape Parallel's core AI architecture and ML strategy from day one, with very high ownership alongside the founders.

 - Real-world impact: your systems directly reduce hospital burnout and free up medical staff to focus on patients, not paperwork.

 - Cutting-edge work that ships: state-of-the-art LLM and agentic systems deployed into real clinical environments — with the engineering rigor (type safety end to end, automated best practices, rapid iteration with tools like Cursor) to make them reliable.

 - Package & perks: competitive salary and meaningful equity, plus our standard benefits (Alan health insurance, Swile meal vouchers, Apple equipment, 50% public-transport coverage).

 - Flexibility: on average one day of remote work per week, and one remote week per year.

 
 
 

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.
If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.

Harper's GTM Engineer builds the data infrastructure. You're the one who tells us what it's saying. Every morning you'll wake up asking the same question: what does the data want us to do today? You sit closest to our Growth Marketing Lead, synthesizing signal from across every channel and turning it into clear, confident recommendations they can act on. You're not a report generator — you're an analytical partner who helps drive decisions, translating the noise into the two or three things that actually matter and helping the team move on them.

You're a growth-oriented data analyst who's as comfortable drawing a conclusion as you are running the query that supports it. You've worked closely with marketing or growth teams before — not as a data service desk, but as a real partner in the work. You know what good channel performance looks like, you understand the metrics that matter in paid acquisition, and you can translate a cohort analysis into a budget recommendation without anyone having to ask. jobs.description:
ABOUT

 - We're building the future of storytelling and video editing.

 - We're a small team that moves fast and builds things we're proud of.

 - We care obsessively about taste: in design, in product, in every detail.

 - We're solving these https://www.cardboard.ai/hard-problems hard problems.

 - We're backed by a Tier-1 global fund, YC, and founders of billion dollar companies.

DESIGN

Video is the most powerful way humans tell stories. It always has been. But creating it today is still painfully hard. Fragmented tools, steep learning curves, and workflows that get in the way of the actual creative work. We're building Cardboard to change that.

As our founding designer, you'll shape not just how the product looks, but how it works. You think product first and push back when something doesn't serve the user, and think through every user flow before a component gets shipped.

In our team, everyone has incredible speed, taste, and care that they put into their work. You'll often see people coming up with micro-interactions nobody asked for and losing sleep over things that feel slightly off by a sheer two pixels. Your job is to accelerate and harness that energy to make sure everything we build feels cohesive and intentional.

YOU WILL

 - Own product design end to end: flows, UI, prototypes, and everything in between.

 - Advocate for the user in every room like a PM does.

 - Work closely with founders, engineering, and growth.

 - Build a design system.

 - Make something people love.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have taste.

 - You own things end-to-end.

 - You think like a PM. You notice the extra click, the label doing two jobs, the feature that shipped but isn't really done.

jobs.title: Quality Engineer, Hardware
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO 

Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure.

ROLE AT A GLANCE

We are hiring a Quality Engineer to build, formalize, and support the quality systems that underpin our product development and robot operations. This role spans the full quality lifecycle — from establishing robust processes and inspection disciplines to driving supplier accountability, internal audit rigor, and systematic corrective action.

You will work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to ensure that our inspection services are implemented effectively and efficiently — and that when problems arise, they are resolved at their root cause and don't recur.

This is a hands-on role suited for a quality professional who is comfortable in both the details of technical standards and the dynamics of cross-functional collaboration. You'll have direct visibility into how your work shapes product reliability, supplier performance, and operational efficiency.

This role includes up to 25% travel to other Gecko Robotics locations (Houston, United Arab Emirates, etc), supplier sites, and field environments.

Must be able to obtain a US Government security clearance.

This role supports U.S. Navy manufacturing programs. Its essential functions require regular access to export-controlled technical data, U.S. Government information systems, and customer facilities subject to U.S.-person access requirements. To satisfy the U.S. Government contractual and customer-access requirements applicable to this role, the selected candidate must qualify as a “U.S. person," that is, a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, or other protected individual, including a refugee or asylee, as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3). This requirement applies only to roles with these access needs and is not a general condition of employment at Gecko Robotics or its affiliates.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

PROCESS DEVELOPMENT & IMPLEMENTATION

 - Develop, document, and maintain quality processes across Gecko Robotics’s locations, including calibration and nonconforming product programs, engineering drawing release workflows, supplier performance, and configuration management procedures

 - Ensure quality systems are compliant with applicable standards and effectively implemented across programs and locations

 - Partner with engineering teams to integrate quality requirements early in the product development lifecycle

 - Continuously improve quality procedures based on data, audit findings, and lessons learned

 - Support the establishment and refinement of systems and tools to improve process efficiencies and cross-department collaboration, including PDM/PLM, ERP and CRM solutions

INSPECTION PLANNING & PERFORMANCE MONITORING

 - Develop inspection plans and acceptance criteria for incoming, in-process, and final inspections for robotic components, parts and assemblies

 - Own the performance of inspection activities — tracking metrics, identifying gaps, and implementing improvements

 - Collaborate with manufacturing and engineering to ensure inspection methods are practical, repeatable, and risk-appropriate

 - Maintain calibration records and monitor system integrity for inspection equipment

 - Support the performance of internal audits across multiple locations

SUPPLIER QUALIFICATION & PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT

 - Lead supplier qualification activities including documentation review, First Article Inspections (FAI) and reporting requirements

 - Monitor and manage supplier quality performance using scorecards, metrics, and structured feedback mechanisms

 - Drive supplier corrective actions for non-conformances, ensuring timely resolution and sustained improvement

 - Build and maintain productive working relationships with key suppliers to proactively address quality risks

FAILURE ANALYSIS & ROOT CAUSE LEADERSHIP

 - Lead structured failure analysis and root cause investigations

 - Collaborate with inter-departmental teams to identify and implement effective corrective actions

 - Communicate findings clearly to stakeholders at all levels, including technical and executive audiences

CORRECTIVE ACTION SYSTEM

 - Own and administer the corrective action system, ensuring timely initiation, assignment and closure

 - Track and report on corrective action metrics, escalating overdue or at-risk items as appropriate

 - Verify effectiveness of corrective actions through follow-up audits and data analysis

 - Drive a culture of accountability and continuous improvement around non-conformance resolution

TECHNOLOGIES WE USE

 - Onshape, Solidworks, Altium, Arena PDM/PLM solutions

 - NetSuite and Salesforce ERP/CRM supporting supply chain and operations

 - Atlassian Jira supporting critical process and feedback initiatives

ABOUT YOU

REQUIRED SKILLS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, or related field (or equivalent practical experience)

 - 5+ years of experience in in quality engineering within a hardware, manufacturing, or electromechanical product environment

 - Hands-on experience across quality management systems and processes, including calibration systems, engineering drawing control, and configuration management

 - Demonstrated proficiency in inspection planning, GD&T interpretation, and measurement system analysis

 - Experience managing supplier quality, including audits, FAI, and supplier corrective action processes

 - Familiar

jobs.title: Field Marketing
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Our vision is to become the marketplace for everything expensive, specialized, and difficult to move. We’re building the infrastructure that powers the procurement and disposition of assets across America’s essential industries, automating everything from discovery and payments to freight, warranty, and financing. Today, Garage operates in cities and towns across all 50 states and has surpassed $100M+ in annualized transaction volume on the platform.

Our mission is to save local governments and essential services businesses time and money. We started with fire departments two years ago and have since expanded into EMS and heavy-duty, launching new verticals while growing revenue >10x last year.

If you move fast, hold a high bar, and want meaningful ownership in building a category-defining company, Garage is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Garage is hiring a Field Marketing Lead, Conferences & Events person to build the events engine that turns high-intent industry moments into a qualified pipeline. As Garage scales its go-to-market motion, events are becoming a critical way for us to get in front of the right audience, deepen customer relationships, and create more high-quality sales conversations.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can own the full event motion: choosing the right conferences and field opportunities, building the plan with Sales, managing the logistics, driving attendance, and making sure every event has a measurable follow-up strategy.

You will partner closely with Sales, Marketing, and company leadership to identify the rooms Garage should be in, create thoughtful experiences for buyers and customers, and translate event activity into conversations, opportunities, and revenue.

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Own Garage’s pipeline-focused event calendar across conferences, trade shows, field events, dinners, and other in-person customer or prospect experiences.

 - Manage event execution end to end, including timelines, budgets, vendors, venues, booth or sponsorship deliverables, shipping, staffing, collateral, and day-of logistics.

 - Build repeatable playbooks for event planning, sales coordination, lead capture, follow-up, and post-event reporting.

 - Create strong attendee experiences that make Garage clear, credible, and memorable to buyers in essential industries.

 - Partner with Sales to define event goals, target accounts, attendee strategy, pre-event outreach, on-site coverage, and post-event follow-up.

 - Evaluate which events Garage should sponsor, attend, host, or skip based on audience fit, pipeline potential, cost, and strategic value.

 - Work with Marketing and Sales to turn event moments into campaigns, customer touchpoints, executive meetings, and pipeline-generating follow-up.

 - Track event performance, report on outcomes, and use learnings to improve Garage’s event strategy over time.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - You are a practical, high-ownership event marketer who can create structure from zero and connect event work directly to business outcomes.

 - You are comfortable working closely with Sales, managing multiple moving pieces at once, and making clear recommendations about where Garage should spend time and money.

 - You bring strong judgment, crisp execution, and a bias toward turning every event into real customer conversations.

REQUIRED

 - 2+ years of experience planning and executing events such as conferences, trade shows, field events, customer dinners, or executive experiences.

 - Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage timelines, vendors, budgets, stakeholders, and logistics without dropping details.

 - Clear written and verbal communication, especially when coordinating across internal teams and external partners.

 - Ability to build lightweight processes, make tradeoffs quickly, and execute in an environment where the event program is still being built.

 - Ability to travel for events as needed, approximately 2-5 days a month

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building an event marketing program or repeatable event playbooks from an early stage.

 - Experience marketing to public sector, government, emergency services, industrial, fleet, logistics, marketplace, or other operational buyers.

 - Experience with event measurement, attribution, CRM hygiene, or marketing automation workflows.

 - Experience managing sponsorships, booths, speaking opportunities, or executive dinners.

OUR VALUES

 - Customers Come First. Our customers operate in an industry burdened by slow, expensive, and outdated processes. We attack the problems that cost them the most and measure our success by the time and money we give back to them.

 - Play For the Front of the Jersey. We put the mission ahead of ourselves. We challenge each other directly, support each other relentlessly, and step up whenever the team needs us. We win together, and we have fun doing it.

 - All Gas, No Ego. Building something that matters takes relentless effort. We move fast, take ownership, and see hard problems through. When we fall short, we own it, learn quickly, and come back stronger.

 

WHY JOIN GARAGE?

 - Make an outsized impact. You’ll join a talent-dense, high-performance team where every person moves the company forward.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer / Technical Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT TAMARIND BIO

We enable any scientist to access AI-powered drug discovery. Thousands of scientists from large pharma companies, top biotechs, and academic institutions use Tamarind to design protein drugs, improve industrial enzymes, and create cutting edge molecules that weren’t feasible until now.

New AI models are quickly eclipsing physics-based tools in computational drug discovery. Scientists often struggle to fine-tune, deploy, and scale these models, leaving breakthroughs on the table. Tamarind provides a simple interface to the vast array of tools being released daily.

Staff Software Engineer / Technical Lead

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to provide technical leadership across our engineering team as we continue to scale the platform behind Tamarind.

Today, our engineering team consists primarily of early and mid-career engineers. As the complexity of our systems and customer requirements continues to grow, we're looking for someone who can help guide technical decision-making, mentor engineers, and drive architectural discussions across the organization.

This is not an engineering management role.

We're looking for a hands-on technical leader who enjoys writing code, reviewing designs, solving difficult engineering problems, and helping other engineers grow. You'll work closely with the CTO to shape technical direction while remaining deeply involved in execution.

The role spans architecture, infrastructure, product development, code reviews, technical mentorship, and engineering best practices.

What You'll Do

 - Partner with the CTO on architecture, technical planning, and major engineering initiatives

 - Provide technical guidance across a team of 7-8 engineers

 - Lead design reviews and architectural discussions

 - Help engineers navigate complex technical challenges

 - Contribute directly to the codebase across infrastructure, backend services, APIs, and product development

 - Review code and provide feedback on implementation approaches

 - Identify opportunities to improve reliability, scalability, performance, and developer productivity

 - Support technical decision-making across new products and platform capabilities

 - Work closely with customers and internal stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into practical solutions

 - Help establish engineering standards as the team continues to grow

Week in the Life

 - Collaborate with the CTO on technical priorities and architectural decisions

 - Review designs and provide guidance on implementation approaches

 - Build and operate services across infrastructure, ML systems, APIs, and customer-facing applications

 - Participate in code reviews and technical discussions

 - Help unblock engineers working through difficult technical problems

 - Work directly with customers to understand requirements and gather feedback

 - Balance hands-on engineering work with technical leadership responsibilities

Ideal Qualifications

 - 7+ years of software engineering experience

 - Experience serving as a senior technical contributor, staff engineer, principal engineer, or technical lead

 - Strong software architecture and distributed systems experience

 - Experience building and operating production infrastructure and cloud services

 - AWS experience (EC2, S3, DynamoDB, Docker, etc.)

 - Ability to mentor engineers and provide technical guidance across multiple projects

 - Strong communication skills and sound engineering judgment

 - Comfort operating in an early-stage startup environment

 - Willingness to work onsite in San Francisco

Technology

Our technology sits at the intersection of DevOps, MLOps, and Computational Biology. We support workloads ranging from large-scale ML inference and model deployment to workflow orchestration across research, infrastructure, and scientific computing environments.

The role requires someone who enjoys moving between architecture, implementation, operations, and mentorship while helping a growing engineering team tackle increasingly complex technical challenges.

jobs.title: Mid Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT PROSPER AI

Prosper is building the most advanced conversational AI agents for healthcare — human-like phone agents that handle the administrative work draining the system: claims status checks, benefit verification, prior authorizations, patient scheduling, and balance reminders. Our mission is to eliminate $200B in administrative waste so healthcare professionals can focus more on healing and less on paperwork.

Headquartered in New York with an office in Barcelona, we work with dozens of large and enterprise healthcare organizations, and we've raised $35M from top investors including a16z, Base10, YC, and Emergence. We're a highly motivated team of 40 — ex-MIT, HBS, Bain, and Math/CS/Physics olympiad medalists — and as we prepare for our next stage of growth, we're looking for ambitious, exceptionally talented people to help scale our product and grow with us.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

At Prosper, we're pushing the limits of what's possible with real-time AI. We're not just making voice agents that "talk" — we're engineering systems that sound human, reason under strong latency constraints, and integrate seamlessly with our customers' complex internal tools. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work side by side with our AI PMs to find technical opportunities that increase the performance of our agents for each of our clients.

Day to day, you'll:

 - Build features that ship fast — develop new capabilities, MVPs, and internal tooling across our FastAPI (Python) + PostgreSQL backend and React (TypeScript) frontend, with a bias toward getting things in front of clients quickly.

 - Integrate with messy real-world systems — build and maintain integrations with EHRs and payor systems (and the APIs, edge cases, and quirks that come with them) so agents fit seamlessly into each client's stack.

 - Debug live, high-volume systems — diagnose and resolve issues for agents making thousands of daily phone calls, where reliability and call quality directly affect patient and provider experience.

 - Turn client feedback into product — close the loop with AI PMs and engineering, surfacing patterns across clients and feeding them back into the core platform.

 - Tune and optimize voice agents — iterate on LLM prompting, voice and transcription configuration, and conversation logic to make agents sound more human and perform reliably under real-time latency constraints.

 - Manage multiple clients at once — prioritize across competing deadlines while keeping quality high.
 
 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years experience with software development

 - A good understanding of the technologies that power our stack or their equivalents in other languages: FastAPI (Python) + PostgreSQL backend with a React (TypeScript) frontend.

 - Experience working closely with clients and finding creative solutions to their needs.

 - Familiarity with LLMs, AI agents or other ML models is a plus.

 - Founder mindset: ownership + hard work. You see Prosper as a learning step for your future startup.

 - Be ready to handle the challenges of supporting AI voice agents making thousands of daily phone calls.

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Maths, Physics or related field (or equivalent experience).

WHAT WE OFFER

 - The opportunity to work alongside an experienced team that has built and scaled a fast-growing, Series A company backed by top Silicon Valley investors

 - Work on innovative products that are transforming US healthcare operations and sit at the heart of conversational agents.

 - Significant growth opportunities as the company scales and the team takes on increasing ownership

 - Competitive compensation

 - Join an international team based in the heart of Barcelona

 - Have real ownership and impact from day one

 - Be part of a culture that rewards bold thinking, analytical rigor, and tangible results

 - Flexible environment

INTERVIEWING PROCESS

 1. Initial conversation to understand who you are, what you want to do, and where you want to go (30 minutes)

 2. Work on a take-home challenge to discuss in the following interview

 3. Review your solution with a couple of engineers from the team (60 minutes)

 4. Talk with the co-founder (30 minutes)

 5. Offer stage
 
 

This is a full-time role in Barcelona office (3-4 days in office).

jobs.title: HPC/ML Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:

We’re looking for an experienced HPC infrastructure engineer to lead bringup, administration, and operations on is probably the largest anime AI training cluster in the world. You’ll serve as the bridge between our researchers and the bare GPU machines, helping to make sure that SLURM jobs are running, parallel filesystems are serving, network is transmitting, and that the anime models are training.

YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:

YOU LOVE ANIME AND THE ANIME AESTHETIC.

This probably one of the only jobs in the world where you will get to combine your love of anime and large-scale GPU systems.

YOU’RE FAMILIAR WITH THE MODERN HPC SOFTWARE LANDSCAPE

Once upon a time, our team could install SLURM on a few bare metal nodes and get away with it. Now the landscape has become unbelievable complex, with SLURM deploys through Slinky on K8s, provisioning through warewulf/MAAS/ansible, filesystems through WEKA/VAST/Ceph, VPN and access through tailscale, and monitoring via the Grafana/Prometheus stack. We’re looking for someone with relevant experience up and down the stack (and maybe a papercut or two to show for it!)

AS WELL AS THE TRADITIONAL SYSADMIN LANDSCAPE

Bringing up and managing cluster still requires good old linux sysadmin skills, including wrangling ldap, triaging dmesg, and setting sticky bits on directories for misbehaving users and tools.

YOU'RE NOT AFRAID OF PHYSICAL COMPUTERS

We’re building out edge datacenters and our CEO is still personally racking, stacking, and provisioning HGX-based nodes in our living room. Also his VLAN design sucks and he’s bad at fiber routing. Please send help.

AND YOU'RE COMFORTABLE WORKING ON SMALL, FAST-PACED TEAMS.

We currently have a very tiny research team, and you’ll be directly helping some of the AI researchers in the world train the best anime image model in the world.

We also believe in the unmatched speed of in-person teams, and prefer on-site collaboration in either our primary research office in Tokyo (downtown Akihabara), or San Francisco (dogpatch!). Bay area is strongly preferred as we have physical hardware in the Bay Area. Visa sponsorships are available.

jobs.description:
The Token Company (YC W26, HF0 S26) is a seed stage startup in San Francisco, CA, and has raised ~$12M from First Round Capital, NEA, YC and SV Angel along with investors such as founders of Dropbox, Slack, Supercell and Huggingface and key people from OpenAI, xAI and DoorDash.

The Token Company trains machine learning models to compress raw LLM inputs before they are passed to the expensive LLMs. Our models are able to recognize parts of inputs that are unimportant, reducing inference costs for scale-ups and enterprises that integrate LLMs into their products. The team is 5 people with a research and product focus.

As a Member of Technical Staff on our infrastructure team, you'll own the cloud systems that serve our compression API end-to-end. You'd get to build global low-latency, high-throughput GPU ML inference infra that sits in the critical path of customer traffic, from deployment and scaling to reliability and cost-efficiency. This is a very high ownership role where you'd need to learn a lot of new solutions and technologies, constantly improving and researching what's best. The ideal candidate fits our culture and is:

A quick learner: grasping the product and the systems around it and moving fast is important

ABOUT CODES HEALTH

We’re fixing one of the most broken and crucial parts of plaintiff litigation: getting complete, accurate medical records. Today, that takes 30 to 50 days of faxing, calling, and portal-chasing across thousands of providers, each running its own back office.

We deliver records 2-3x faster. To do this, we're building an agentic layer that operates in this messy, real-world environment. Every retrieval teaches our system how to access another corner of American healthcare, building a provider data layer you can't scrape or buy. All while putting us at the most upstream point of a $20B+ market where everything downstream depends on us.

This problem extends far beyond the plaintiff legal space. It's also pervasive in healthcare, where our CEO Alvaro first encountered it while running a home health agency, as well as in disability services, life sciences/clinical trials, and the insurance industry. All of these verticals face this same challenge.

“Codes isn’t just participating in the workflow; it’s capturing the moment where the most important data is created, positioning itself to expand from ingestion into orchestration and ultimately own the entire stack.” - Amplify Partners, Boring is Sexy https://www.amplifypartners.com/blog-posts/boring-is-sexy-the-anatomy-of-a-good-vertical-ai-startup

We've gone from $0 to a $3M+ run rate in a year and grown 2.5x quarter over quarter for four straight quarters. We've raised $17.5M from Amplify, General Catalyst, Haystack, and Y Combinator. We serve 130+ law firms across plaintiff litigation and mass tort, including the largest plaintiff firm in the country.

THE WORK

The core challenges are data complexity and reliability under extreme variability.

You can think about it as reverse-engineering the back office of every healthcare facility in the U.S., then rebuilding it as a system that continuously learns from outcomes and improves across thousands of edge cases.

That includes:

 - Building agentic systems that run end to end across fax, email, web portals, and physical mail, where each document type triggers a different workflow.

 - Processing records that average 300 pages, sometimes hit 30,000, and run roughly 70% duplicate, and still surfacing what matters to a case.

 - Matching patients and facilities across messy provider networks, where a single system like NYU Langone is 340+ care locations with no clean way to match them.

We're a lean team where everyone works on everything. The work splits loosely across automating the retrieval pipeline, the customer-facing product law firms use to request and view records, and the applied AI threaded through both.

You'll move between them as our goals shift, ship customer-facing product one month and go deep on the pipeline the next, and stay close to both the customer and the data.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

This role is open at all levels. You might be a fit if you:

 - Have shipped features start to finish in production and want to own outcomes.

 - Go deep on the domain: the data systems and the workflows our agents run.

 - You’ve explored LLMs and are excited about turning them into reliable systems.

 - Want to talk to users directly and ship off their feedback.

 - Are excited to apply real engineering rigor to a messy, economically valuable problem.

You'd work directly with the founders and a small, high-bar engineering team.

NON-NEGOTIABLE

Fully in person in Dumbo, Brooklyn.

STACK

TypeScript and React on the frontend. Python and FastAPI on the backend.

COMPENSATION

Competitive base salary ($160k -$300K depending on years of experience), early-stage equity, unlimited PTO, and additional benefits such as paid dinner in office and Ubers from the office.

jobs.title: Product Engineer
jobs.description:
At Lapel, we believe the most hospitable companies win. We're building the data, infrastructure, and tools that help customer-facing teams understand every customer and act on that insight at scale throughout the entire customer lifecycle.

Most internet businesses want to treat customers well, but their tools work against them. We’re building the layer that makes every interaction feel personal again: unifying context, coordinating action, and closing the gap between intent and experience.

It’s a technically ambitious challenge spanning data infrastructure, AI, and systems design – with a deeply human outcome: helping software companies serve people better. We call it hospitality at scale.

We’re well-funded, backed by top-tier investors, and already working with exceptional companies, from fast-growing startups to large enterprises. We’ll share more details when we talk.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

At Lapel, our product engineering team owns all product surface areas from ideation to delivery to customers. On this team, you'll own features end-to-end across our entire stack and be expected to bring both product judgment and technical depth to ship things that actually work the way customers need them to.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build, ship, and iterate on product features across the full stack

 - Work closely with founders, designers, and customers to define and deliver product experiences

 - Own features end-to-end, from ideation and implementation to deployment and iteration

 - Design and implement APIs, services, and integrations

 - Translate product requirements into scalable, maintainable technical solutions

 - Develop both frontend interfaces and backend services as needed

 - Continuously improve product quality, performance, and usability

 - Contribute to product decisions, prioritization, and trade-offs

 - Write clean, maintainable code and improve engineering standards

OUR STACK

Lapel is built end-to-end in TypeScript in a single monorepo.

 - React, Vite, and Tailwind on the frontend;

 - Node.js and Postgres on the backend;

 - Temporal and Pulsar to power orchestration.

We ship quickly, and care about creating a developer experience where anyone can prototype, experiment, and get ideas into production fast.

YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have 5+ years of experience building and shipping products

 - Have owned large-scale, enterprise products end-to-end

 - Are comfortable working with APIs, databases, and system design

 - Have strong product instincts and care about user experience

 - Enjoy owning problems end-to-end, not just implementing tasks

 - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and working in early-stage environments

 - Collaborate well with designers and product teams

 - Move fast while maintaining a high bar for quality

THE PROCESS

We aim to hire with intention, respect your time, and offer feedback along the way.

 1. Initial conversation (20 minutes) We’ll explore your motivations, share what we’re building, and answer your questions.

 2. In-depth interview (60 minutes) We’ll go deeper into your craft and experience. No live coding. No prep work necessary.

 3. Take-home project (2–4 hours) You’ll complete a short, well-scoped exercise that mirrors the kind of work you’d do here.

 4. On-site visit (1–2 days) Join us in the office to review your take-home, grab lunch, and work on something real.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We believe great people build great companies – and we invest accordingly.

 - Competitive salary + meaningful early-stage equity

 - Full benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and commuter benefits

 - Generous time off: many company holidays and coordinated team-wide breaks throughout the year to focus and recharge

 - Office perks: lunch and dinner provided daily, in-office snacks, and health & wellness benefits

 - Team culture: regular off-sites, tight feedback loops, and a bias toward action

WHY LAPEL, WHY NOW

 1. A trillion-dollar problem hiding in plain sight. Companies spend over $1T a year on customer-facing teams and $150B on the tools meant to support them, yet every team still pieces context together across a dozen disconnected systems. We're rebuilding this from the foundation, and AI makes now the only moment it's possible.

 2. The most interesting place to apply AI is where the work actually happens. Customer operations is one of the largest, most under-built surfaces in software. Every company runs on it, every team feels the pain, and the tools haven't been seriously reimagined in fifteen years. We think the next generation of category-defining B2B companies will be built here.

 3. One platform, every customer-facing team. Sales, success, support, and ops all serve the same customer relationship, but each one buys a different tool to do it. Owning the foundation means the surface area grows with the company, from a single team to the entire revenue org to the whole business. That's the market, and the mission: better service at internet scale.

Lapel works in person in San Francisco, five days a week, at our office on Market Street. We hire people who'd be restless anywhere else.

OTHER NOTICES

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

jobs.title: Senior founding designer
jobs.description:
Making preventive health the default for every human in Europe

 

The mission

At Lucis https://lucis.life/?utm_source=career_job_desc&utm_medium=content, we believe healthcare should be preventive, not reactive. We’re building the OS for human longevity to help people add more healthy years to their lives. You can read more about who we are and how we work here https://lucis.life/careers?utm_source=career_job_desc&utm_medium=content.

Why this role exists

We hire for one thing: people who deliver high-value experiences, fast. Fast is not corner-cutting. It comes from two things we refuse to trade off.

 1. Choosing the right experience. The judgment to know which problem is worth solving, so speed compounds instead of producing polished waste.

 2. Getting it right the first time. Craft high enough that an experience is remembered and trusted, held coherent from the first screen to the last so nothing drops at the handoffs.

Most companies build a design seat around one of these. We're building this one around both. It's a consumer product role with the soul of a brand designer: you run your own strategy, Discovery, and Delivery, and you don't wait for a spec to start.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The experience, end to end. From "which problem is worth solving this week" to the last micro-interaction. You frame it, prioritize it for value, and carry it to shipped.

 - Craft that holds. Interaction, motion, and visual quality high enough to be remembered, coherent across every surface Lucis touches: mobile home, coach, results, web, launches, partner work.

 - Complexity made calm. Biomarkers, protocols, clinical results. You turn dense, high-stakes information into something that feels simple, and earns trust.

 - The brand's point of view, in product. You defend a definition of good and keep Lucis feeling like Lucis, not like everyone else's safe-and-polished.

 - The agentic pipelines that let design move fast. You operate the stack daily, improve it when it drags, and reach for leverage so your time goes to the hard 10%.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You run product and UX strategy. You frame the problem and prioritize for value; you own it end to end because no one is going to feed you a spec.

 - Your craft is remembered, not just shipped. You'd happily show us your worst shipped screen alongside your best, because the floor tells the real story.

 - You're an interaction designer at the core. You think in prototypes and motion, not static frames. You show how something feels, not only how it looks.

 - You have consumer instincts. Your reflex reaches for reassurance over density. The SaaS-dashboard register is the one thing we can't coach fast, and you already have the other one.

 - You have high agency. You've operated without a manager or a mature design org, and you preferred it that way.

YOU'LL STAND OUT IF

 - You have bold brand taste and a point of view you'll defend. When AI flattens everyone to safe-and-polished, taste is the moat.

 - You've shipped consumer product at real scale, carry a wide cultural reference set, and you're hungry to mine it for ideas nobody else would reach for.

 - You move well across squads and get to speed on unfamiliar problems fast.

 - An AI-native, ship-to-git workflow lights you up rather than makes you uneasy.

 - You use design systems as leverage for craft, not as the product itself.

 - You've made dense or high-stakes data feel calm and simple before.

BONUS (TIE-BREAKERS)

 - Mobile-native fluency. Mobile home and coach are our live priority surface.

 - Health or another high-consequence domain in your background. It builds restraint.

 - Motion or prototyping as a genuine strength.

 - Bilingual FR/EN.
 
 
 

What you'll inherit on day one

 - A working agentic asset stack: Claude skills, Figma plugins, and image and video pipelines that turn a Notion brief into a shipped carousel, newsletter, or ad in under an hour.

 - A versioned knowledge base that encodes Lucis voice, taste, calibration tiers, compliance, and output contracts.

 - Direct access to image and video generation, and every system you need to move.

How we work

We work together from our Paris hub. We're passionate about what we're building and believe the fastest way to make something exceptional is side by side. We're open to relocation support for the right people, and we welcome missionaries who travel to work with us in Paris on a regular basis.

 - Rigor without ego. Audits, science, and code all held to the same high bar.

 - Radical ownership. Feedback loops are short; everyone contributes to the best version of Lucis.

 - Velocity over perfection. We ship daily, and we prefer a good decision today to a perfect one next week.

PROCESS

 - Screening call (20 min)

 - Craft deep-dive (60 min)

 - Take-home case study using our actual stack (~3 to 4 hrs), plus a 45-min review

 - Half-day on-site with the team in Paris

 - Two reference calls

 - Decision within 10 days of the on-site

At Lucis, AI isn't just our product, it's our engine. Every team runs on the best AI agents we can give them. You'll have carte blanche to automate everything that can be, so your time goes to the work only you can do.

WHY AUCTOR

Auctor is building the AI layer for professional services and software implementation. Think of us as the brain behind the best solution engineers, forward-deployed engineers, and onboarding teams—automating the documentation, the discovery, and the decision-making that powers $400B+ in services work. As a Product Operations Manager, you'll work alongside our founding team of engineers and product leaders to build the infrastructure that turns raw customer signal into sharp product decisions. You'll own the systems that connect our customers, engineering, deployment, and go-to-market—synthesizing feedback into clear themes, defining the metrics that tell us whether the product is landing, and keeping the whole company oriented around the same priorities. WHAT YOU BRING

jobs.title: Solution Scientist
jobs.description:
ABOUT ARTOS:

At Artos, we build tools that help biopharma companies create and manage their R&D documentation in a fraction of the time. If you’re looking to join a team whose mission is to fundamentally change the way that drug development gets done, we’d love to talk to you.

We’re growing very fast, and we’re looking for a domain-expert technical product lead —someone with a strong pharma background who can sit between engineering teams and end users, help implement our system in real customer environments, and translate deeply technical capabilities into workflows that actually make sense to scientists, medical writers, and regulatory teams.

This is not a traditional product manager role, nor a traditional medical writing role. It’s a hybrid: part domain architect, part technical translator, part customer-facing problem solver.

 

The Role:

 

As a core member of Artos’s product team, you will act as the bridge between engineering and domain experts.

duct.

This role is about systems, not just documents.

 - Translate domain rules, conventions, and preferences into clear product and engineering requirements

 - Help implement Artos in customer environments and support early adoption

 - use cases

Who This Role Is For:

 

This role is ideal for someone who:

 

 - Comes from pharma or biotech and deeply understands regulatory documentation

 - Enjoys acting as a translator between technical and non-technical teams

Requirements:

 - Willingness to be customer-facing and support implementation

 - and feedback loops

 - Experience working with life sciences software tools is a plus

 - Ability to operate independently in a fast-moving startup environment

Other Information:

Very comfortable working in a fast-paced and intense startup environment

Willing to work in-person in our office in Mission Bay 4-5 days/week

Our Vision: Unlock Healthcare's Full Capacity

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10–20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $31M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.

OUR VALUES

We hire and grow everyone against the same four values. Each one comes from a real Vitalize story—interview with us to hear them!

 - 🚗 Push the Car. Step in regardless of role. We help wherever we're needed, own problems end to end, and don't stay in our lane. People can count on us.

 - 🏥 Premier 1K. We show up for our customers, always. Nearly everyone visits a customer site in their first month, and customer feedback informs everything we do.

Every recommendation Vitalize makes flows through this team. We build the intelligence that helps hospitals decide who should float, when to call someone in, when staffing is becoming unsafe, and eventually when the system can safely make those decisions on its own.

This is where Vitalize evolves from software that reports what’s happening into software that actively runs hospital operations.

 

THE ROLE

Clinical leaders make hundreds of staffing decisions every day under time pressure using disconnected systems. We’re replacing that with software that reasons through the problem, recommends, and eventually executes the best next actions.

You’ll own the decision engine behind those recommendations, turning messy operational reality into software customers trust with some of the most important decisions inside a hospital.

 - Systems thinking—You can reason through complicated edge cases

Bun • TypeScript • Effect • React • TanStack Router • Planetscale

At Parallel, we build AI agents that help healthcare organizations automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.

Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost to manual, repetitive administrative tasks. Legacy software hasn't helped: it has made work slower, more complex and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change this. Our technology combines large language models with system-level automation to do real work inside existing hospital tools. No integration, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding and frees up time for medical teams to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024 and already have 800+ customers and a team of 30+ people. We are backed by top-tier investors (Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI), and this is just the beginning.

The future of healthcare isn't just digital, it's automated. Come help us build it!

Context

We're at a pivotal moment. We've closed a $20M Series A with Index Ventures, we're deployed in 40+ hospitals, and we're scaling fast. The company was built by Paul Lafforgue (Polytechnique, ex-Meta, ex-McKinsey) and Chris Rydahl, whose previous company Hublo became Europe's largest healthcare staffing platform. We're 15 people, based in Paris.

We're now hiring a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to help us scale — not just to write code, but to shape our architecture, make key product decisions, and define our engineering culture.

Your mission

Own the full technical stack — from core backend services to user-facing interfaces — and help deploy reliable AI agents in hospitals.

Concretely, you will:

 - Build production-grade systems, not prototypes — robust, secure, and HDS-compliant, designed to run in demanding hospital environments

 - Ship and iterate on LLM-powered agents that automate complex end-to-end workflows

 - Work alongside the CTO to make the right architecture decisions, balancing speed and long-term scalability

 - Build interfaces that doctors and administrative operators actually want to use — understanding their pain points, not just closing tickets

 - Lay the engineering foundations: CI/CD, observability, internal tooling, code quality standards

Outcomes

In your first months, we expect you to:

 - Own the full lifecycle of major features — from spec to production monitoring

 - Design a modular backend architecture that supports multiple clients with complex, custom business rules

 - Deploy AI agents in production with a high reliability bar

 - Build and maintain solid data pipelines between hospital systems and our stack, HDS-compliant

 - Improve team velocity through better tooling, CI/CD, and observability

This job is for you if:

 - You have 5+ years of full-stack experience

 - You're strong in Node.js & TypeScript (NestJS, Express, Prisma, Postgres) and React (TanStack, Tailwind)

 - You've played with LLMs and AI agents — whether on side projects or professionally (LangChain, Hugging Face)

 - You're comfortable with infrastructure and deployment (AWS, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions)

 - You care about the product, not just the code — you push back when something doesn't make sense, and you propose solutions proactively

 - You're autonomous and pragmatic — done beats perfect, especially at this stage

 - You're French-speaking

 - You graduated from a top engineering school

Hiring process

 1. Quick call with Chris, our CTO

 2. Case study at our Paris office

 3. Meeting with Paul, our CEO

 4. Drinks with the team

Why join us?

 - Real traction. Seed and Series A closed in under a year, with Index Ventures on the cap table. This isn't a maybe — it's a company that's moving.

 - A problem worth solving. Cutting hospital admin directly gives time back to care teams. The impact is tangible.

 - A genuinely different technical approach. Agents that work on top of existing systems without heavy integration is a real competitive edge — and you'll be the one building it.

 - A team that has done it before. The founders have built and scaled before (Hublo, Meta, McKinsey). High standards, low ego.

 - Actual ownership. You won't be handed a backlog. You'll co-build the architecture and set the engineering culture from the ground up.

 - Competitive salary and equity package, premium health insurance (Alan), Swile meal vouchers, latest Apple equipment, Paris office (Strasbourg Saint-Denis).

 - Flexibility: on average one day of remote work per week, and one remote week per year.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.
If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

jobs.title: Head of Capacity
jobs.description:
About Blacksmith

 - We started by building infrastructure to run CI workloads really fast. Our first product helps companies run GitHub Actions substantially faster and cheaper by owning and operating our own global fleet of bare-metal machines rather than renting generic cloud VMs.

 - Today, we orchestrate tens of millions of Firecracker VMs each week, running CI for 10,000+ companies and tens of millions in ARR. We’ve grown 20x so far in 2026.

 - We operate thousands of bare-metal machines across multiple regions, regularly schedule 300k+ vCPUs concurrently, and run a petabyte-scale Ceph cluster that we manage ourselves.

 - We’ve raised $125M from Seed to Series C, led by Sequoia, Google Ventures (GV) & Peak XV Partners, and we’re intentionally building a small, but exceptional team.

 - Blacksmith was founded by a team with deep systems and scaling experience, including building search/ads infrastructure at Faire, and operating large distributed systems at Cockroach Labs. Our GTM is led by Jon Boyer, formerly Head of Sales at Zapier.

 - We're now extending the same CI infrastructure into a broader platform: running agent sandboxes at scale and building our own background coding agent on top of it.

About the Role

Blacksmith's infrastructure footprint is growing rapidly.

Every quarter, we make decisions around servers, storage, networking, datacenter capacity, power, and geographic expansion. As demand for software validation grows, ensuring that capacity is available when and where we need it becomes increasingly important.

We're looking for someone to own this problem.

You'll work directly with the founders and infrastructure team to forecast demand, plan capacity growth, manage supplier relationships, and ensure Blacksmith can scale ahead of customer demand.

Your job is simple to describe but difficult to execute: Make sure Blacksmith never runs out of capacity.

What You'll Do

 - Own capacity planning across compute, storage, networking, and datacenter infrastructure.

 - Build forecasting models for infrastructure demand and growth.

 - Partner with engineering to understand future workload requirements.

 - Develop deployment plans across regions and datacenter partners.

 - Manage relationships with hardware vendors, datacenter providers, and infrastructure suppliers.

 - Lead hardware procurement and infrastructure expansion efforts.

 - Evaluate new suppliers, hardware platforms, and deployment opportunities.

 - Track utilization and ensure infrastructure investments are deployed efficiently.

 - Build processes and systems that allow Blacksmith to scale from thousands of servers to many times that number.
 
 

You Are a Good Fit If You

 - Have experience operating large-scale infrastructure, cloud, hosting, networking, or datacenter environments.

 - Have experience with capacity planning, forecasting, or infrastructure operations.

 - Can balance long-term planning with day-to-day operational realities.

 - Are highly analytical and comfortable making decisions under uncertainty.

 - Have strong vendor management and negotiation skills.

 - Can work effectively with both technical and business stakeholders.

 - Enjoy solving operational problems at scale.

 - Want to work closely with founders on company-critical infrastructure decisions.

 - Enjoy working in person 5 days a week in SF/NYC.
 
 

Bonus

 - Experience at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, hosting company, CDN, or infrastructure startup.

 - Experience procuring servers, networking equipment, storage, or datacenter capacity.

 - Experience managing infrastructure supply chains.

 - Experience with power planning, datacenter operations, or colocation providers.

 - Experience scaling infrastructure through periods of hypergrowth.
 
 

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year:

 - Blacksmith has a clear, data-driven capacity planning process.

 - Infrastructure growth is forecasted quarters ahead of demand.

 - Hardware procurement and deployment timelines are predictable.

 - Vendor and datacenter relationships are strong and scalable.

 - Leadership has visibility into future capacity constraints before they become operational issues.

 - Blacksmith can confidently scale infrastructure without becoming constrained by supply, deployment timelines, or planning failures.

Compensation and benefits

 - Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance.

 - Competitive base + equity.

 - 401K match.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Annual offsite.

 - Early-exercise stock options

 - 12 weeks fully paid parental leave (US)

jobs.title: Collections Lifecycle Manager

The mission:
